# Kokiri

> *"They looked like children, all of them. But their eyes were older than the trees. The fairy on the scout's shoulder watched me the whole time, and somehow I felt it understood more of what I said than she did."*
> — Viator Fortuitus, A Bard's Record, Ch. 18 excerpt

Deep within the Lost Woods, where sunlight filters green through canopies so thick they blot out the sky, live the Kokiri, the forest children of Hyrule. Small, bright-eyed, and ageless, they have dwelt in the shadow of the Great Deku Tree since before the kingdom was founded, under the guidance of their fairy companions and the Tree's own patient will.

To most of Hyrule, the Kokiri are little more than a rumor, glimpsed between the trees and gone before anyone looks directly. The Lost Woods itself discourages visitors, and the Kokiri have little reason to seek outsiders out. They are not hostile. They belong to the forest so completely that the world beyond it feels like someone else's concern.

### Children Who Never Age

The most striking thing about the Kokiri, to those who encounter them, is that they never visibly grow older. Every Kokiri looks as though they are between ten and twelve years old: small and slight, with round faces and wide eyes that carry more depth than their apparent age should allow. They do not gray or wrinkle or stoop. An elder Kokiri who has lived three hundred years looks identical to one who has lived thirty.

This agelessness is not a choice or an affectation. A Kokiri's body is bound to the forest's own timelessness, held at the point of early growth the way a seedling is held before it becomes a tree. Their minds mature at a normal rate; Kokiri are no less capable of adult reasoning, complex emotion, or long experience than any other race. They simply carry all of that inside a body that never changes.

Most Kokiri are at peace with this. Some find it strange, particularly those who spend time among short-lived races and watch them age while they themselves stay the same.

\column

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### The Fairy Bond

Every Kokiri is born alongside a fairy companion, a small luminous fey spirit of the forest that attaches to a single Kokiri and stays bonded to them for life. A fairy is a partner, not a pet. It has its own personality and opinions, it thinks for itself, and it feels as much as its Kokiri does.

Fairy companions are small enough to fit in a cupped hand, usually a few inches long, and they trail soft light in a color that varies by individual (pale gold, forest green, warm rose, cool silver). They can speak in a voice only their Kokiri partner can clearly hear, though others may catch some meaning in the musical tones they produce. They watch constantly, advise constantly, and have an opinion about everything their partner does.

A Kokiri without a fairy is deeply unusual, rare enough that other Kokiri treat it as a serious misfortune, though fairies lost to violence or dark magic may in time be replaced through the Great Deku Tree's blessing. No Kokiri tradition records one rejecting their fairy on purpose. It would be treated as a spiritual wound.

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:55%,--offsetY:55%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/DTCTlG2.png){top:0px,left:300px}
}}

{{imageMaskEdge4,--offset:3%,--rotation:270
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/NMuksuF.png){top:50px,left:550px,height:500px}
}}

{{imageMaskCorner20,--offsetX:-50%,--offsetY:-50%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/wFufXFC.png){top:820px,left:160px,height:15%}
}}

{{artist,bottom:120px,left:70px
##### Kokiri Crest
}}

\page

### The Great Deku Tree's Children

The Kokiri do not worship the Great Deku Tree the way one might worship a deity. He is more immediate than that, closer to a parent and a chief and a living home at the same time. They speak with him. They bring their problems to him. When the Tree sends one of them out into the world it is a commission, not an exile: a specific task only that Kokiri can do, granted with the Tree's blessing so they can survive the journey.

Kokiri who adventure outside the Lost Woods have, almost without exception, received this blessing. Some carry a specific charge from the Great Deku Tree: find this person, return this object, warn that settlement. Others have been sent simply to learn, or to act as the Tree's eyes in a world he cannot walk through. A very few left of their own accord, testing the limits of what the forest will permit, and found that the world did not end them.

### Kokiri and Other Races

**Deku.** The Kokiri consider the Deku distant cousins, forest folk tied to the same deep green. But where Deku are territorial and suspicious, Kokiri tend toward curiosity and welcome. The Deku find the Kokiri reckless; the Kokiri find the Deku unnecessarily grim.

**Hylians.** Fascinating and bewildering at the same time. Kokiri love Hylian stories, Hylian food, and Hylian music. They find Hylian mortality quietly distressing and rarely mention it.

**Koroks.** The Kokiri know the Koroks as transformed cousins, the ones who shed their humanoid forms for plant-spirit shapes in another age. They treat this knowledge with reverence and leave it at that.

**Sheikah.** Respected. The Sheikah's secrecy feels familiar, and they understand forest spirits in a way most races do not.

**Gorons.** Amiable, if loud. Their relationship to stone feels to the Kokiri the way the Kokiri's relationship to the forest feels to Gorons. Both are personal, and neither was chosen.

### Kokiri Names

Kokiri names are short and musical, often inspired by natural sounds, seasons, or the qualities of their fairy companion.

**Given Names:** Saria, Mido, Fado, Navi, Fari, Kalo, Lumi, Brin, Wyn, Telo, Dayo, Sera, Noko, Pell

**Fairy Names (given by their Kokiri):** Spark, Glint, Whisper, Bloom, Ember, Chime, Mist, Flicker, Hush

\column

### Kokiri Traits

Your Kokiri character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

**Age.** Kokiri mature mentally at a normal rate but never visibly age past the appearance of early childhood. Their lifespan is tied to the health of their grove. Those who remain close to living forest can persist for centuries.

**Alignment.** Most Kokiri tend toward neutral good, guided by the forest's quiet ethics of growth and protection rather than formal law or morality.

**Size.** Kokiri stand between 3 and 4 and a half feet tall, slightly taller than Deku. Your size is Small.

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common and Kokiri.

**Fey Ancestry.** The magic of the forest runs through you. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and you cannot be magically put to sleep.

**Nature's Child.** You have proficiency in the Nature skill. Your fairy companion's constant guidance means you notice plants, terrain, creatures, and weather patterns that others walk right past.

**Timeless Body.** You do not age visibly and are immune to magical aging effects. Effects that would magically cause you to grow older have no effect on you.

**Fairy Companion.** You are bonded to a fairy companion, a small fey spirit of the forest who has been your partner since birth. Your fairy is always present and cannot be permanently lost, though it can be temporarily frightened away or incapacitated by powerful magic (it returns to you within 1 hour if separated).

Your fairy grants you the following benefits:

- ***Fairy Guidance.*** You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception), Wisdom (Survival), and Intelligence (Nature) checks. Your fairy constantly observes, remembers, and advises.
- ***Fairy Light.*** Your fairy emits dim light in a 5-foot radius. You can suppress or restore this light as a bonus action.
- ***Fairy Warning.*** You cannot be surprised while your fairy is conscious. It watches while you sleep and wakes you before danger reaches you.
- ***Fairy Revival (Once per Long Rest).*** When you are reduced to 0 hit points, your fairy may immediately use its action on your initiative to stabilize you automatically, without requiring a roll. You are stabilized at 0 hit points. The fairy cannot use this ability again until you finish a long rest.

{{footnote Races of Hyrule | Kokiri}}
{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Rito

*"The stone spire climbed into the freezing skies, its peak lost among the clouds. Homes clung to its sides, swaying gently in the wind. Above them, the Rito wheeled through the air, feathers cutting the currents, bows slung easily at their sides, as natural to them as breathing."*

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; — *Viator Fortuitus*  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; *A Bard's Record, Ch. 10 excerpt*

High above forests, seas, and snow-capped peaks dwell the Rito, a proud avian people whose lives are shaped by wind and sky. Whether soaring between mountain spires or carrying messages across open waters, the Rito see the world from above, and think little of those bound only to the ground.

---

### People of Wind and Feather

Rito are tall, bird-like humanoids with feathered wings in place of arms, sharp talons, and beaked faces. Their plumage varies widely in color and pattern, often reflecting family lines or regional traditions. Most Rito stand between five and six and a half feet tall, with lean, lightweight builds well suited to the air.

Though flight defines Rito culture, it is not granted freely. Young Rito first learn to **glide**, mastering control and balance long before they ever take to the skies in earnest. True flight is earned through discipline, strength, and tradition.

---

### Life Above the World

Rito settlements are built where few others could live: atop stone spires, cliff faces, and remote islands lashed by wind and cold. Their homes are suspended by ropes, carved into rock, or balanced delicately along narrow ledges.

Rito society values skill, awareness, and self-reliance. Children are taught from a young age to read the wind, judge distances, and trust their instincts. While they are not numerous, Rito communities are tightly knit, bound by shared responsibility and mutual respect.

---

### Archers of the Open Sky

Across Hyrule and beyond, Rito are known as peerless archers. From the air or from high vantage points, their arrows strike with deadly precision. Bows are treated as extensions of the self, and many Rito personalize their weapons with feathers, carvings, or charms.

Despite this martial reputation, most Rito are not conquerors. They serve as hunters, sentinels, messengers, and scouts, watching the lands below.

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### Tradition and Change

Rito culture varies greatly depending on homeland. Some cling to ancient rites and sky-borne ceremonies, while others embrace trade, travel, and diplomacy. What unites them all is reverence for the wind, respect for freedom, and a belief that perspective, both literal and figurative, is the key to wisdom.

---

### Rito and Other Races

**Hylians.** Curious ground-dwellers. Rito often serve as their messengers and scouts.

**Zora.** Graceful but bound to water. Mutual respect runs deep.

**Gorons.** Reliable allies, though far too heavy for flight.

**Gerudo.** Strong and proud, but dangerously grounded.

**Sheikah.** Watchful and secretive. Rito trust their results, if not their methods.

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:53%,--offsetY:45%,--rotation:0

}}

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:50%,--offsetY:20%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/P1826Hk.png){top:20px,left:450px,height:60%}
}}

{{footnote Races | Rito }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Rito Names

Rito names are melodic and often inspired by wind, song, or flight. Many adopt titles based on deeds or roles.

**Names:** Revali, Teba, Kass, Medli, Komali, Harth  
**Titles:** Windcaller, Scout, Courier, Skywarden

### Rito Traits

Your Rito character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

**Age.** Rito reach adulthood in their teens and rarely live beyond 100 years.

**Alignment.** Rito tend toward neutral alignments, valuing freedom, perspective, and personal responsibility.

**Size.** Rito vary widely in height and build, from barely 5 feet to well over 6 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common and Rito.

**Feathered Adaptation.** You are immune to the effects of extreme cold for the purposes of Weather Exhaustion.

**Glide.** When you are not wearing medium or heavy armor, you can use your wings to slow your descent.
- When you fall, you can use your reaction to reduce the falling damage you take by an amount equal to **five times your character level**.
- While falling at least 10 feet, you can move horizontally up to **5 feet for every 10 feet you descend**.
- You do not provoke opportunity attacks from creatures you move past while gliding downward.

**Ranged Experts.** You have proficiency with shortbows and longbows. In addition, you gain a **+1 bonus to ranged weapon attack rolls** when any of the following is true:

- You are flying, gliding, or falling.
- Your target is at long range for the weapon you are using.
- You and your target are both outdoors under open sky.

**Aerial Agility.** You have proficiency in the Acrobatics skill.

**Eagle-Eyed.** You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

**Flight.** Starting at 5th level, you gain a flying speed of **50 feet**. You can't use this flying speed if you're wearing medium or heavy armor.

::::::::::::

### Rito Subraces

Rito culture diverges sharply based on homeland. Choose one of the following subraces.

#### Highland Rito

Highland Rito dwell among frozen peaks and towering stone spires, where wind and altitude test even the hardiest travelers. These Rito are hunters and sentinels, shaped by relentless cold and roaring skies.

**Wind-Hardened.** You ignore disadvantage imposed by strong winds, high altitude, or severe cold on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws made to resist being pushed or knocked prone by wind or environmental effects.

**Mountain Hunter.** You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made in cold, snowy, or mountainous terrain. In addition, when you make a ranged weapon attack against a creature that is at least **10 feet below you**, you have advantage on the attack roll.

#### Isle Rito

Isle Rito inhabit windswept islands and coastal spires, living as messengers, traders, and navigators. Their culture emphasizes communication, travel, and maintaining bonds between distant peoples.

**Seasoned Navigators.** You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to navigate, avoid becoming lost, or determine direction while traveling.

**Island Envoy.** You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: **Persuasion, Deception, or Insight**.  
In addition, you learn **one additional language** of your choice.

# Sheikah

*"We made our way first to the royal castle. We were not alone. My Rito companion, Nyth, spotted silver blurs along the rafters, too fast to follow and too precise to be chance. Wisely, he said nothing. Those who speak ill of the Sheikah, or of the royal family, tend not to last long."*

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; — *Viator Fortuitus*  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; *A Bard's Record, Ch. 06 excerpt*

From the shadows of history and the silence between heartbeats, the Sheikah watch. They are guardians, spies, scholars, and executioners, bound by ancient oaths to the Goddess Hylia and her mortal bloodline. Though few in number, their influence has shaped the fate of Hyrule for millennia.

---

### Chosen of the Goddess

The Sheikah were chosen by the Goddess Hylia in the age before the Kingdom of Hyrule, tasked with protecting her people and guiding them through ages of calamity. Even after Hylia relinquished her divinity, the Sheikah remained steadfast, their loyalty passing to the royal family she left behind.

Sheikah bear distinct features: pale or ash-toned skin, **red or crimson eyes**, and long pointed ears similar to Hylians, though sharper and more angular. Their presence is often unsettling, less for any cruelty than for the fact that they are *always aware*.

---

### Lives in Shadow

Secrecy defines Sheikah culture. From childhood, they are trained to observe without being seen, to speak little, and to act decisively. Many Sheikah villages are hidden or disguised, existing in plain sight only to those who know where to look.

Despite this secrecy, Sheikah are not emotionless. They form deep bonds of loyalty and kinship, though such attachments are carefully guarded. Duty always comes first, sometimes at terrible personal cost.

---

### Blade, Scroll, and Sigil

Sheikah excel in disciplines that reward precision and preparation. They are master spies, assassins, monks, and tacticians. Many are also scholars who preserve forbidden histories and ancient technologies best left forgotten.

Shadow magic, particularly illusions and misdirection, is a closely guarded tradition passed down through generations. These techniques are subtle tools for confusing an enemy, distracting them, or vanishing without a trace.

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### Sheikah Names

Sheikah names are short, sharp, and often symbolic. Many abandon personal names entirely when assuming certain roles.

**Names:** Impa, Paya, Koko, Cado, Rauru  
**Titles:** Shadow, Sentinel, Watcher, Monk, Blade

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:55%,--offsetY:35%,--rotation:0

}}

}}

{{footnote Races | Sheikah }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

\column

### Sheikah and Other Races

**Hylians.** The reason for their existence. Sheikah protect them from threats they will never see.

**Gerudo.** Watched carefully. Power and ambition demand vigilance.

**Gorons.** Trusted allies, though too straightforward for subtle work.

**Zora.** Respected for memory and tradition.

**Rito.** Useful scouts, though too visible for true secrecy.

### Sheikah Traits

Your Sheikah character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Intelligence score increases by 1.

**Age.** Sheikah reach adulthood in their teens and rarely live beyond 100 years.

**Alignment.** Most Sheikah tend toward lawful or neutral alignments. Duty and loyalty outweigh personal morality.

**Size.** Sheikah vary widely in height and build, from barely 3 feet to well over 6 feet tall. Your size is **Small or Medium** (your choice).

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is **35 feet**.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common.

**Shadowy Folk.** You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill. If you already have proficiency in Stealth, you instead gain expertise in that skill.

**Shadow Blessing.** You learn one cantrip of your choice from the Illusion school of magic. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

When you reach 3rd level, you learn one 1st-level Illusion spell of your choice, which you can cast once without expending magic points. You regain the ability to cast this spell in this way when you finish a long rest.

# Twili

*"The Twili emerged from mirrors like smoke, their golden eyes piercing the gloom. In their realm, light twists, and shadows whisper."*  

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; — *Viator Fortuitus*  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; *A Bard's Record, Ch. 28 excerpt*

Beyond the veil of Hyrule lies the Twilight Realm, a place of eternal dusk, warped light, and silent skies. From this shadowed world hail the Twili, a people shaped by exile, magic, and survival beneath a broken sky.

### Exiles of the Gods

Long ago, the ancestors of the Twili were powerful sorcerers who sought dominion over sacred magic. Their ambition drew the wrath of the gods, and they were cast into the Twilight Realm, a fractured mirror of the world they once knew.

There, under alien stars and dim light, they changed.

Generations passed, and the Twili became something new: graceful, otherworldly beings attuned to shadow and distortion. What once was punishment became identity.

### Twilight Flesh and Form

Twili are tall and slender, with elongated limbs, pale or ashen skin, and eyes that glow gold, violet, or amber in low light. Their features often appear subtly distorted: necks that bend too far, markings that glow faintly, or shadows that lag behind their movements.

They dress in flowing garments stitched with arcane sigils and twilight metals, and favor form and symbolism over practicality.

### A Fractured Society

Twili society is deeply hierarchical, ruled by monarchs and high sorcerers who interpret ancient laws left behind by the gods. Power is respected, but recklessness is feared. History has taught them the cost of hubris.

Most Twili value:
- Control over emotion
- Subtlety over force
- Knowledge over conquest

Those who leave the Twilight Realm are rare and often viewed with suspicion by both worlds, outsiders twice over.

::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### Twili and Other Races

**Hylians.** Objects of resentment and fascination. They inherited the world the Twili lost.

**Sheikah.** Dangerous kin. Their secrets mirror Twili magic too closely for comfort.

**Gerudo.** A cautionary tale of ambition and prophecy.

**Zora.** Timeless and patient. The Twili envy their acceptance of fate.

**Rito.** Free in ways the Twili can never be.

---

### Twili Names

Twili names are soft, flowing, and often symbolic. They reflect concepts rather than lineage.

**Names:** Midna, Zant, Ravio, Keshra, Thalos, Nyxil  

**Titles:** Shadow Regent, Twilight Scholar, Veilwarden, Mirrorbound

}}

}}

### Twili Traits

Your Twili character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Intelligence score increases by 2, and your Dexterity score increases by 1. Alternatively, you may increase two different ability scores by +1 each.

**Age.** Twili mature at a similar rate to Hylians and can live up to 200 years.

**Alignment.** Twili tend toward neutral alignments. Their culture prizes restraint and order, but individuals vary widely.

**Size.** Twili typically stand between 5 and 7 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common and Twili.

**Twilight Affinity.** You have resistance to necrotic damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being blinded or charmed.

**Eyes of Twilight.** You have darkvision out to 120 feet. This vision functions in both magical and nonmagical darkness.

**Umbral Step.** When you are in dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness.  
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

**Twilight Veil.** You can cast *disguise self* without expending magic points. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you cast it in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 2 MP to cast it again.

# Zonai

*"They descended from the heavens in an age before memory. To the people of the surface, they were gods."*  

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; — *Fragment of an Ancient Tablet*

&nbsp;

### Children of the Heavens

Zonai are tall, imposing humanoids with vaguely caprine features, elongated ears, and luminous third eyes upon their foreheads.

Their skin tones range from pale ivory to muted sage green. Their hair is often white, silver, or faintly glowing gold.

A faint aura of ancient magic surrounds them, particularly when they channel power.

They favor flowing garments adorned with geometric patterns and sigils representing skyward spirals.

Zonai are tall and slender, with elongated torsos and eyes of blue, violet, or amber.

### A Dwindling People

The Zonai were once a great civilization. Now, only a handful remain.

Most Zonai value:
- Balance
- Sacred duty
- Stewardship of power

Zonai society was built upon divine responsibility rather than dominance.

::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### Zonai and Other Races

**Hylians.** Once worshipers, now heirs to a world the Zonai helped shape.

**Sheikah.** Kindred spirits in arcane mastery. Their technology mirrors Zonai constructs in lesser form.

**Gerudo.** Strong and ambitious. Zonai respect their willpower.

**Zora.** Ancient and dignified, a people who understand what it means to outlast an age.

**Rito.** Remind the Zonai of their skybound origins.

**Gorons.** Grounded and lasting, the opposite of Zonai transience.

}}

### Zonai Names

Zonai names are melodic and ancient, often symbolic of virtues or celestial phenomena.

**Names:** Rauru, Mineru, Kaelor, Seraphae, Lumeris, Vaerun

**Titles:** Lightbearer, Secret Keeper, Skywarden, Stonebound

\column

### Zonai Traits

Your Zonai character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.

**Age.** Zonai mature at a similar rate to Hylians and can live up to 300 years.

**Alignment.** Zonai tend toward lawful alignments, valuing responsibility and balance. However, divine power without guidance can lead to extremes.

**Size.** Zonai typically stand between 7 and 8 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common and Zonai.

**Divine Ancestry.** You have resistance to radiant damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed.

**Third Eye of Insight.** You have darkvision out to 60 feet. Once per long rest, you can open your third eye as a bonus action for 1 minute.

While your third eye is open:
- You gain advantage on Perception checks.
- You can see invisible creatures within 10 feet.

**Ancient Zonai Magic.** You can channel the magic of your ancestors.
- You know the *light* cantrip, and you can cast it twice per long rest without expending magic points.
- At 3rd level, you can cast *guiding bolt* once per long rest without expending magic points.
- At 5th level, you can cast *lesser restoration* once per long rest without expending magic points.

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

# Zora

*"The water embraced silver architecture, towers rising like frozen waves. Their weapons and armor gleamed with the same pale sheen, stark against smooth, bright skin. Where a Hylian bears hair, the Zora wear flowing fins, each shaped like the tail of some distant fish. Spears caught the sunlight as they watched us in silence."*

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; — *Viator Fortuitus*  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; *A Bard's Record, Ch. 18 excerpt*

Graceful and ancient, the Zora are the stewards of Hyrule's waters. From crystalline rivers to vast inland seas, their domains are places of beauty, danger, and deep memory. To understand the flow of time in Hyrule, one need only listen to the Zora.

---

### Children of River and Sea

The Zora are aquatic humanoids bearing traits of fish and amphibians: smooth, scale-less skin in hues of blue, green, silver, and coral; webbed hands and feet; and long head-fins resembling flowing crests or tails. These fins vary wildly between individuals and families and are a source of great pride.

Zora architecture mirrors water itself: smooth curves, flowing arches, and structures grown or shaped rather than built. Their cities gleam beneath the surface or rise from riverbanks like sculpted stone reefs.

---

### Long Lives, Long Memories

Zora lifespans dwarf those of most surface races. They mature slowly, often not reaching full physical adulthood until around a century of age, and many live for four centuries or more. This longevity grants them extraordinary patience, and also a tendency to cling to tradition.

Some elder Zora undergo dramatic physical changes with age, growing massive in size or becoming wizened and eel-like. These elders are revered as living relics of history, though such transformations are exceedingly rare among adventurers.

---

### Guardians of the Flow

Zora culture is deeply tied to guardianship. Rivers must remain pure, tides respected, and the balance between land and water maintained. Pollution, damming, and reckless magic are treated as sacrilege.

Most Zora are trained in spear combat and swimming from childhood. While not a warlike people, they are formidable defenders who strike from the water and are gone beneath the surface again before anyone answers.

::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

### Royal Lineage and Sacred Duty

Zora society is traditionally ruled by a royal family believed to be divinely favored. Kings and queens are expected to act as mediators between their people, the waters, and the land-dwellers upstream.

Music and ceremony are central to Zora life. Songs are used to mark seasons, remember the dead, and even calm dangerous waters. Many Zora adventurers carry these traditions with them, performing rites wherever they travel.

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:53%,--offsetY:40%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/DTCTlG2.png){top:0px,left:300px}
}}

{{imageMaskCorner29,--offsetX:53%,--offsetY:40%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/ZHRZsGh.png){top:0px,left:200px,width:700px}
}}

{{footnote Races | Zora }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Zora and Other Races

**Hylians.** Short-lived, but earnest. Zora often act as their historians and advisors.

**Sheikah.** Respected, but unsettling. They know too much.

**Gorons.** Loud, friendly, and dangerously fond of bathing in rivers.

**Rito.** Cousins of wind and sky. Zora admire their freedom but distrust their distance.

**Gerudo.** The desert's thirst makes cooperation... complicated.

### Zora Names

Zora names often flow like water, passed down through families and echoing ancient heroes.

**Names:** Mipha, Sidon, Dorephan, Ralis, Lulu, Rutela  
**Titles:** Prince, Princess, Warden of Tides, Riverguard, Tidecaller

### Zora Traits

Your Zora character has the following racial traits.

**Creature Type.** You are a Humanoid.

**Ability Score Increase.** Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

**Age.** Zora reach physical maturity around 100 years of age and can live up to 400 years or more.

**Alignment.** Most Zora tend toward neutral or lawful alignments, valuing balance, patience, and tradition.

**Size.** Zora vary widely in height and build, ranging from barely 3 feet to well over 6 feet tall. Your size is **Small or Medium** (your choice).

**Speed.** Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

**Languages.** You can speak, read, and write Common and Zora.

**Great Swimmer.** You have a swimming speed of **60 feet**. You can breathe both air and water, and you can swim up waterfalls and strong currents as if they were normal flowing water.

**Zora's Grace.** You gain proficiency in the Athletics skill.

**Slippery.** You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape grapples, restraints, or effects that would restrain or impede your movement.

:::::::::::::::::::

### Zora Subraces

Zora society is not monolithic. Over centuries, different waters have shaped distinct cultures, temperaments, and fighting styles among the Zora. Choose one of the following subraces.

---

#### River Zora

River Zora dwell in clear rivers, sacred springs, and great inland domains. They are known for their regal bearing, diplomacy, and strict adherence to tradition. Many serve as nobles, emissaries, or ceremonial guardians of vital waterways.

**Graceful Presence.** You gain proficiency in either **Persuasion** or **Performance** (your choice).

**Voice of the River.** When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Performance) check, you can treat a roll of 7 or lower on the d20 as an 8. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

**Ceremonial Bearing.** You have advantage on Charisma checks made to interact peacefully with aquatic creatures or to influence nobles, officials, or spiritual authorities.

---

#### Sea Zora

Sea Zora are swift, expressive, and fiercely independent. They live among open waters and powerful tides, and they value freedom above almost anything else. Their movements are fluid even by Zora standards, and many are performers, scouts, or roaming guardians of the coast.

**Oceanic Agility.** Your swimming speed increases by **10 feet**.

**Fluid Motion.** When you take the Dash or Disengage action while swimming, you gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) check you make before the end of your turn.

**Born Performer.** You gain proficiency in **Performance** or **Acrobatics** (your choice).

---

#### Swamp Zora

Swamp Zora inhabit murky wetlands, stagnant waters, and hostile marshes where survival demands aggression and cunning. Often misunderstood or feared, they are territorial and deadly in close quarters. Their culture prizes strength, ambush, and dominance over their environment.

**Marsh Stalker.** You gain proficiency in the **Stealth** skill.

**Ambush Predator.** Once per turn, when you hit a creature that hasn't taken a turn yet in the current combat, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

**Bog-Hardened.** You have advantage on saving throws against poison and disease.

# Temperature

The blazing heat of the Gerudo Desert or the freezing cold of the Hebra Mountains can break even seasoned adventurers. Extreme environments in Hyrule are obstacles in their own right, meant to test preparation, endurance, and resolve.

When traveling through extreme temperatures, creatures may be forced to make **Weather Exhaustion checks**, which represent mounting strain from heat or cold. These rules exist to **gate dangerous regions**. They reward proper gear, planning, and magical protection, and still let desperate heroes push forward at great risk.

:
Your environment and your level of preparedness determine the **DC** of a Weather Exhaustion check, as well as how frequently checks are required. For example, traveling through the Gerudo Desert at midday in common clothing might require a DC 10 check every hour, while traversing the caldera of an active volcano could require a DC 20 check every 10 minutes.

:
On a failed check, a creature gains **1 level of Weather Exhaustion**. On a success, no Weather Exhaustion is gained.

:
Some races, features, or equipment may grant **advantage** on Weather Exhaustion checks, reduce the DC, or increase the time between checks, at the DM's discretion.

:
Weather Exhaustion is a **separate condition** from standard D&D exhaustion. It represents environmental strain rather than physical collapse.

:
Weather Exhaustion can be reduced by **1 level per short or long rest**, provided the creature is sheltered from the environment (such as resting in a cave, oasis, tent, or magically protected space).

### Checking the Weather
A cautious player may ask the DM "How's the weather in this area?" or "How are traveling conditions today?" That question is the DM's cue to say whether Weather Exhaustion is a factor here. Alternatively, a DM may ask for a Wisdom (Survival) check to see whether the character recognizes if the conditions are safe to travel in given what they are carrying.

:::::::::::::::::

#### Heat
Extreme heat includes deserts, volcanic regions, badlands, and sun-scorched plains.

A creature with **resistance to fire damage** has advantage on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by heat. A creature with **immunity to fire damage** automatically succeeds on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by heat.
Certain items, spells, or clothing may grant resistance or immunity to heat, or otherwise reduce its effects.

#### Freezing
Extreme cold includes tundras, arctic regions, high mountains, and frigid desert nights.

A creature with **resistance to cold damage** has advantage on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by freezing conditions. A creature with **immunity to cold damage** automatically succeeds on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by freezing conditions.

Certain items, spells, or clothing may grant resistance or immunity to freezing conditions.

{{imageMaskCorner20,--offsetX:55%,--offsetY:72%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/BotW_Edge_Cover_Official_Illustration.png){Right:0px,top:-60px,height:40%}
}}

{{imageMaskCorner32,--offsetX:-70%,--offsetY:-70%,--rotation:0
  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/Link_has_a_pumpkin_to_climb_-_BOTW_art.jpg){Right:280px,height:30%}
}}

:

### Weather Exhaustion Levels
| Level | Effect |
|:----:|:--------|
| 1 | Disadvantage on **Perception checks** and **initiative rolls**. |
| 2 | Disadvantage on **all ability checks**. |
| 3 | Your speed is reduced by **10 feet**. At the start of each of your turns, choose **attack rolls or saving throws**. You have disadvantage on the chosen rolls until the start of your next turn. |
| 4 | Your speed is reduced by **20 feet**, and you **cannot gain advantage** on any d20 rolls. |

:
Weather Exhaustion cannot directly kill a creature.

:
**While a creature is at Weather Exhaustion Level 4, any additional failed Weather Exhaustion checks instead cause the creature to gain 1 level of standard D&D exhaustion.**

:
### Standard Exhaustion
Standard exhaustion follows the normal D&D 5e rules.

There are **6 levels of exhaustion**, and a creature dies if it reaches level 6.

:
Finishing a long rest reduces a creature's exhaustion level by 1, provided the creature has had adequate food and water.

{{footnote Mechanics | Temperature }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Stamina System

Stamina Points (SP) represent a creature's physical endurance, focus, and ability to push beyond normal limits. All classes gain stamina points, though at different rates depending on class and level.

Stamina is primarily used to fuel **called shots**, certain **class features**, movement through harsh terrain, and emergency magical recovery. Unlike Magic Points, stamina is a **universal resource**, so both martial and magical characters can push themselves when they need to.

:
Stamina points are normally fully replenished upon completing a **short rest**, provided the creature is able to rest safely (see Resting & Stamina below).

:

### Difficult Terrain
Adventurers often face dense forests, deep swamps, rubble-filled ruins, steep mountains, deep snow, and ice-covered ground, all of which count as difficult terrain.

:
Normally, moving through difficult terrain costs **2 feet of movement for every 1 foot traveled**. However, a creature may expend stamina to push through obstacles.

:
By expending **1 stamina point**, a creature may treat **5 feet of difficult terrain as normal terrain**.

:
This represents bursts of effort such as leaping across rubble, forcing a path through deep snow, or sprinting through choking sand.

---

#### Climbing, Swimming, and Crawling
Climbing, swimming, or crawling costs **1 extra foot of movement per foot traveled** (or **2 extra feet in difficult terrain**), unless a creature has an appropriate movement speed.

:
A creature may expend **1 stamina point** to move **5 feet** while climbing, swimming, or crawling as if it were normal terrain.

:
The DM may still require a Strength (Athletics) check in hazardous conditions, such as slick surfaces, sheer cliffs, or strong currents, even if stamina is spent.

:::::::::::::::::

### Resting & Stamina Recovery (Rest Economy)
Stamina recovery is intentionally limited by environment and safety.

:
A creature **cannot benefit from a short rest** while:
- In **difficult terrain**
- In **extreme temperatures**
- While Weather Exhaustion checks are required
- While under immediate threat or pursuit (DM discretion)

:
These restrictions prevent creatures from endlessly recovering stamina while pushing through dangerous environments.

:
A short rest taken in a **safe, sheltered location** fully restores stamina points as normal.

:

### Stamina Burn (Meditative Recovery)
Stamina Burn allows a creature to convert physical endurance into magical endurance during moments of calm focus.

:
As a **10-minute uninterrupted meditation**, a creature may convert stamina into magic points.

**Rules for Stamina Burn:**
- Can only be performed **out of combat**
- Requires **10 uninterrupted minutes**
- Cannot be performed while:
  - In difficult terrain
  - In extreme temperatures
  - While Weather Exhaustion checks are required
- Conversion rate: **2 Stamina Points → 1 Magic Point**
- Magic points recovered this way cannot exceed the creature's normal maximum
- **Stamina spent this way is burned.** It does not come back on a short rest the way ordinary Stamina does; it returns only on a long rest

:
Stamina Burn represents controlled breathing, ritual focus, or spiritual grounding rather than an adrenaline rush.

:
Stamina points expended this way do **not** recover until the creature completes a **long rest**.

{{footnote Mechanics | Stamina }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Called Shots

Just before making an attack roll with a weapon or an unarmed strike, a creature may attempt a **called shot** by expending **2 stamina points**.

:
A called shot targets a creature's momentary vulnerability: a gap in armor, a joint, an exposed eye, or an unstable stance.

:
On a hit, a called shot adds **one additional weapon damage die** to the damage roll.  
Starting at **10th level**, a called shot instead adds **two additional weapon damage dice**.

:
Only the weapon's base damage dice are increased. Additional damage from spells, class features, or magic items is rolled as normal.

:

### Exploitation Fatigue (Anti-Spam Rule)
Repeatedly exploiting the same opening is taxing.

After a creature makes a called shot against a target, any additional called shots made against that same target before the start of the attacker's next turn cost 1 additional stamina point.

This increase resets at the start of the attacker's next turn.

This rule encourages teamwork, timing, and precision rather than repeated brute-force exploitation.

### Weak Points
Some creatures in Hyrule possess **weak points**, specific body parts or vulnerabilities that can be exploited with a called shot.

:
Weak points are usually apparent through observation, prior knowledge, or successful ability checks, unless deliberately concealed.

:
When a called shot targets a creature's weak point, it triggers a **special effect** described in the creature's stat block, such as:
- Inflicting a condition
- Disabling an ability
- Causing additional damage
- Creating an opening for allies

:
**If a creature has no listed weak point,** the called shot still lands and still adds its extra damage die. For the effect, use the **Body Part Reference Table** in the DM Guide, which gives a default outcome for every part of the body. Most humanoid opponents in this book are handled that way.

:
**Called Shot Save DC.** Where a called shot forces a saving throw, the DC is:

**8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier you used for the attack**

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

{{classTable,wide

##### Called Shot Examples
| Target | | Example Effect | | Example Critical Hit Effect |
|:-----:|:-|:---------------|:-|:----------------------------|
| Eye | | The target has disadvantage on ranged attack rolls and sight-based ability checks until the end of its next turn. | | The target is blinded in that eye until it regains hit points or uses an action to succeed on a Constitution saving throw. |
| Hand | | The target is disarmed and must use its object interaction to retrieve the item. | | The target's weapon is flung up to 30 feet away. |
| Leg | | The target's walking speed is reduced by half until the end of its next turn. | | The target is knocked prone and its speed is halved until it regains hit points or succeeds on a Constitution saving throw as an action. |
| Arm | | No additional effect. | | The arm is injured; attacks or ability checks made with it have disadvantage until healed or a successful Constitution save is made as an action. |
| Head | | The target has disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma checks until the end of its next turn. | | The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be knocked unconscious. It may repeat the save at the end of each of its turns. |
}}

# Magic System

*"Magic in Hyrule is as old as the goddesses themselves. It whispers through the Lost Woods, shimmers at the edge of twilight, and hums in the silence between raindrops."*  
— *Viator Fortuitus, A Bard's Record*

---

### Essence of Magic
Magic in Zelda DnD is fueled by **Magic Points (MP)**, which represent a creature's attunement to the mystical forces of the world. MP completely replaces spell slots.

:
If a creature has enough MP to pay a spell's cost, it may cast that spell, regardless of spell level or prior use.

:
> ##### MP Is the Gate
> That sentence means what it says, and it is deliberate. There is no table here telling you that 3rd-level spells arrive at 5th level. **What a caster can cast is decided by what they can pay for**, and paying for a spell far above your station costs you the rest of your day.
>
> A 1st-level Sage has 9 MP. Spending all of it on one enormous spell is a legal choice and usually a bad one: it is the whole adventuring day for a single effect, with nothing left for the fight afterwards. That trade is the limit. A DM who wants a firmer ceiling can use the **Spell Level Cap** some classes already carry, or set one per class at the table.

:
> ##### New Rule: No Known Spells
> Classes in this book have a spell list but **no known-spells list**. A caster may cast any spell on their class's list at any time, provided they can pay the MP. There is no preparation step, no spells known, and no daily limit on which spells you use.
>
> This is deliberate. What limits a caster here is the size of their MP pool, **Arcane Strain** (repeating a spell costs more each time) and **Arcane Saturation** (expensive magic degrades your casting). Those three rules do the work that a known-spells list does in standard 5e, and they push a caster toward variety rather than toward one memorized answer.
>
> The exception is a table using the **spell slot alternative** table printed for each class. A DM who chooses that option runs preparation and spells known exactly as standard 5e does.

:
Different classes gain MP at different rates, determined by their class progression.

### Casting Spells with MP
Each spell has an **MP cost** based on its power. When you cast a spell, you expend MP equal to its cost.

:
You cannot normally cast a spell if you do not have enough MP. However, a desperate caster may attempt to push beyond their limits (see **Arcane Wounds**).

:
### Spell Save DC and Spell Attack Bonus
These work as they do in standard 5e. Stated here so nobody has to assume:

**Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier**

**Spell attack bonus = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier**

:
Your class entry names your spellcasting ability. Some classes define a **separate** DC for their own non-spell features (the Mask save DC, the Special Attack save DC, the Relic save DC); those are stated where they appear.

### Rituals
Around twenty spells in the Spell Compendium carry the **(Ritual)** tag. Under this system a ritual is not free.

:
**A ritual costs its full MP.** What the extra 10 minutes buys you is that **the casting is exempt from Arcane Strain**: casting the same ritual over and over never raises its cost, and a ritual never advances the Strain step of anything else you cast.

:
So a ritual is the slow, reliable, fully priced way to do something. It is the right choice when you have time and want certainty, and the wrong choice when you are being shot at.

:
### Recovery
Magic Points are fully restored after completing a **long rest**.

:
Some class features, relics, potions, or sacred locations may restore MP earlier, such as:
- Blue Potions  
- Light Temples  
- Sheikah meditation sites  

{{footnote Mechanics | Magic System }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Arcane Strain
Magic resists repetition. Channeling the same spell over and over causes arcane feedback that raises its cost.

### Escalating MP Cost
Each time you cast the **same spell** without casting a different spell in between, its MP cost increases:

| Cast Sequence | MP Cost |
|--------------|---------|
| First Cast | Normal cost |
| Second Cast | +50% MP (rounded up) |
| Third Cast | +100% MP |
| Fourth+ Casts | Cannot be cast again until the end of your next turn |

:
The MP cost resets when you:
- Cast a different spell  
- Skip a turn without casting a spell  

This rule discourages repetitive spell use while preserving tactical flexibility.

### Arcane Saturation
High-intensity magic places stress on a caster's arcane channels.

:
Each time you cast a spell that costs **5 MP or more**, you gain **1 level of Arcane Saturation**. Arcane Saturation is tracked openly by the player.

:
Arcane Saturation resets at the end of combat, or after **1 uninterrupted minute** without casting spells.

### Arcane Saturation Effects
| Saturation Level | Effect |
|-----------------|--------|
| 1 | No effect |
| 2 | Arcane Strain cost increases by an additional +25% |
| 3 | Disadvantage on spell attack rolls |
| 4 | Spell save DCs are reduced by 1 |
| 5+ | You cannot cast spells that cost 5 MP or more |

:
Arcane Saturation represents magical overload and naturally discourages nova casting without hard limits.

{{footnote Mechanics | Magic System }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Spell Chart Conversion Cost

| Spell Type | MP Cost   |
| :---------- | :--------- |
| Cantrip    | **1 MP**  |
| 1st-level  | **2 MP**  |
| 2nd-level  | **3 MP**  |
| 3rd-level  | **4 MP**  |
| 4th-level  | **5 MP**  |
| 5th-level  | **6 MP**  |
| 6th-level  | **7 MP**  |
| 7th-level  | **8 MP**  |
| 8th-level  | **9 MP**  |
| 9th-level  | **10 MP** |

\column

### Soft Concentration
 
Some sustained magical effects, notably the Goddess Chanter's Sacred Songs and the Champion's Aura of the Chosen, use **soft concentration** rather than standard concentration. Soft concentration works like standard concentration with the following differences:
 
**It does not conflict with standard concentration.** A creature maintaining a soft concentration effect can simultaneously maintain a standard concentration spell. Only one soft concentration effect can be maintained at a time, but it coexists freely with any number of concentration spells, provided those spells also coexist with each other.
 
**It uses a lower damage threshold before breaking.** When a creature maintaining a soft concentration effect takes damage, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or the effect ends. The DC is a flat 8, rather than the standard 10 or half the damage taken, whichever is higher. Minor disruptions (moving through difficult terrain, being shoved, taking a small hit) interrupt a sustained song or aura more easily than they would a focused spell.
 
**It ends immediately if the creature is incapacitated or silenced.** Standard concentration also ends on incapacitation, but soft concentration also ends on any silencing effect, because the effects that use it are vocal or harmonic.
 
**It cannot be maintained while casting a spell with a casting time of 1 minute or longer.** Lengthy ritual casting interrupts the sustained harmonic or divine focus that soft concentration requires.
 
In all other respects, soft concentration follows the standard concentration rules: it can be ended voluntarily as a free action, only one soft concentration effect can be active at a time, and features that provide advantage on concentration checks also provide advantage on soft concentration checks.

{{footnote Mechanics | Magic System }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Magical Overchanneling
Spellcasters may attempt to empower spells beyond their normal limits, similar to upcasting in traditional magic systems.

:
When casting a spell, you may choose **one** Overchanneling tier:

| Tier | Extra MP | Effect |
|------|----------|--------|
| Minor | +1 MP | +1 damage die or +10 feet range |
| Major | +2 MP | +2 damage dice or +20 feet range |
| Extreme | +3 MP | +3 damage dice or a secondary effect (DM approval) |

### Overchanneling Rules
- You may only choose **one tier** per casting
- Overchanneling always counts as **one additional Arcane Strain step**
- Extreme Overchanneling requires a **Constitution saving throw**
  - On a failure, you gain **1 Arcane Wound**
- A spell cannot be overchanneled more than once per casting


Overchanneling allows lower-level spells to remain relevant while preserving risk and balance.

:
> ##### Spells Brought In From Elsewhere
> **Overchanneling replaces upcasting completely.** If you use a spell from the Player's Handbook or any other source that has an *At Higher Levels* entry, ignore that entry: the spell is cast at its printed effect for its MP cost, and Overchanneling is how you make it bigger.
>
> The one exception is a spell in this book that names its own MP cost for an upgrade. Where a spell says what extra MP buys, that instruction wins.

### Magical Desperation (MP Burn)
When a creature attempts to cast a spell without sufficient MP, it may do so through sheer desperation. The spell takes effect normally, and afterwards the creature gains **1 Arcane Wound**.

### Arcane Wounds
An Arcane Wound is lasting damage to a caster's magical channels, taken whenever they force magic they cannot pay for. Wounds stack, and their effects are cumulative.

#### Arcane Wound Effects
| Arcane Wounds | Effect |
|:--------------|:--------|
| 1 | −1 maximum MP |
| 2 | −2 maximum MP |
| 3+ | Disadvantage on spell attack rolls, and your spell save DC is reduced by 1 |

Arcane Wounds represent damage to a creature's magical channels. They stack, cannot reduce maximum MP below 0, and do not cause exhaustion.

::::

### Treating Arcane Wounds
Arcane Wounds are not easily healed.

- **Long Rest:** Removes 1 Arcane Wound  
- **Blue Potion:** Removes 1 Arcane Wound  
- **Sacred Springs or Light Temples:** Remove 1–2 Arcane Wounds (DM discretion)  
- **Great Fairy Blessing:** Removes all Arcane Wounds  
- **Rare Ritual (10 minutes):** Consumes special reagents and removes 1 Arcane Wound  

---

### Schools of Magic in Hyrule
Magic manifests in many traditions:

- **Light Magic:** Radiant, sacred power  
- **Shadow Magic:** Twilight and Interloper arts  
- **Nature Magic:** Elemental and primal forces  
- **Time Magic:** Rare, dangerous manipulation of causality  
- **Divine Magic:** Songs, prayers, and blessings  
- **Arcane Magic:** Learned spellcraft and Sheikah technology  

---

### Triforce Alignment
Magic often reflects one of the Triforce's aspects:

- **Power:** Destruction and domination  
- **Wisdom:** Control and foresight  
- **Courage:** Protection and enhancement  

---
Triforce alignment has no inherent mechanical effect unless stated otherwise.

### Magic Items & Relics
Some magic items require MP to function. Unless stated otherwise, activating such an item does not trigger Arcane Strain or Arcane Saturation.

{{footnote Mechanics | Magic System }}

# Adventurer

*"Not every hero is chosen by fate. Some earn their legend step by step, blister by blister, mile by mile."*

Adventurers are wanderers, treasure hunters, scouts, and survivors who thrive in Hyrule's most dangerous regions. Where others rely on divine favor or arcane mastery, the Adventurer depends on preparation, adaptability, and grit.

They know how to stretch a waterskin in the desert, read the wind in the mountains, and turn a moment's distraction into victory. In a land shaped by ruins and monsters, Adventurers endure.

---

> ##### A Turn as an Adventurer
> You move, attack twice with whatever you picked up last, and spend a Stamina Point to get somewhere the terrain says you shouldn't be. From 3rd level you may also have a spell or a song for the moment that calls for one.

## Class Features
As an Adventurer, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Adventurer level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, rapiers, shortswords, longbows  
- **Tools:** Thieves' tools, navigator's tools, one musical instrument  
- **Saving Throws:** Dexterity, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Athletics, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a shortbow and 20 arrows, or (b) a shortsword and a shield, or (c) two simple weapons  
- (a) explorer's pack or (b) dungeoneer's pack  
- (a) leather armor or (b) scale mail  
- (a) navigator's tools or (b) thieves' tools  
- (a) a lute or (b) any musical instrument

##### The table below uses the traditional spell slots of D&D 5e, for players or DMs who would rather run this class the standard way.

> ##### Using the Spell Slot Alternative
> Swapping a class to this table swaps out the whole MP economy, including the **No Known Spells** rule. A class run on spell slots prepares and knows spells as its nearest 5e counterpart does: **Adventurer** as a Bard (Minstrel) or Ranger (Wild Scout); **Blightbound** as a Warlock; **Champion** as a Paladin; **Goddess Chanter** as a Bard; **Interloper** and **Sage** as a Wizard; **Ranger** as a Ranger; **Shaman** as a Druid.
>
> Draw from this book's spell list for the class rather than the Player's Handbook's. **Arcane Strain, Arcane Saturation and Overchanneling do not apply** when using spell slots; the slot economy limits the caster instead.
>
> **How many spells you know.** Champion, Interloper, Sage and Shaman map to prepared casters (Paladin, Wizard, Wizard, Druid), so they prepare a number of spells the standard way and need no extra column. The other four map to known casters, and use their counterpart's Spells Known progression from the 2014 Player's Handbook: **Adventurer** the Bard's (Minstrel) or the Ranger's (Wild Scout), **Blightbound** the Warlock's, **Goddess Chanter** the Bard's, **Ranger** the Ranger's.

### Core Class Features

#### 1st Level: Well-Traveled
You gain advantage on ability checks using one Charisma or Wisdom skill of your choice while interacting with common folk, merchants, or travelers.

In addition, you always know the local rumors within a settlement after spending 10 minutes listening or observing.

#### 1st Level: Cunning Tricks
You learn a number of **Cunning Tricks** that allow you to turn stamina into tactical advantages.

- You know **2 tricks** at 1st level.
- You learn **1 additional trick** at 5th, 9th, and 13th level.
- Using a trick costs **Stamina Points (SP)** as noted.
- You may use only **one trick per turn**, unless otherwise stated.

**Example Tricks**
- **Distracting Taunt (1 SP):** Bonus action. One creature you can see within 30 feet has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
- **Quick Getaway (1 SP):** Bonus action. You may Dash or Disengage.
- **Lucky Shot (1 SP):** When you miss an attack, reroll the attack roll.
- **Pocket Sand (1 SP):** Bonus action. A creature within 5 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of its next turn.

| Adventurer Level | Tricks Known |
|:----------------:|:------------:|
| 1st | 2 |
| 5th | 3 |
| 9th | 4 |
| 13th | 5 |

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you may replace one Cunning Trick you know with another.

#### 1st Level: Adaptive Training
You add **half your proficiency bonus (rounded up)** to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

#### 2nd Level: Stamina Surge
As a bonus action, you may expend **1 SP** to gain advantage on **one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw** you make before the end of your turn.

\column

#### 3rd Level: Path of the Wanderer
You choose a path that reflects how you survive and thrive:

- **Path of the Treasure Hunter**
- **Path of the Minstrel**
- **Path of the Wild Scout**

Your path grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.


#### 3rd Level: Minor Magic
You gain access to a small pool of Magic Points (MP), which represent tricks, charms, and a latent knack for magic.

You may only use MP to cast spells or activate class features granted by your Adventurer Path.

#### 5th Level: Extra Attack
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

#### 5th Level: Reactive Dodge
When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you may use your reaction and expend **1 SP** to halve the damage.

#### 7th Level: Evasion
When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure.

#### 9th Level: Reliable Talent
Whenever you make an ability check using a skill you are proficient in, you may treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

#### 11th Level: Stroke of Luck
Once per long rest, when you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may treat the roll as a 20.

#### 13th Level: Improved Evasion
When you fail a Dexterity saving throw, you take only half damage instead of full damage.

#### 15th Level: Slippery Mind
You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

#### 17th Level: Masterful Prowess
Once per turn, when you expend SP for a class feature or trick, you may reduce its SP cost by 1 (minimum 0).

#### 20th Level: Legendary Wanderer
When you start your turn with **0 SP or 0 MP**, you regain **1 SP and 1 MP**.

In addition, you learn one **Ultimate Trick**, a powerful ability defined by your path, usable once per long rest.

{{footnote Classes | Adventurer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Treasure Hunter

Treasure Hunters are dungeon-delvers and relic seekers who survive by wit, reflex, and hard-earned experience in ancient ruins.

#### 3rd Level: Relic Delver
- You gain **Sneak Attack (1d6)**. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a finesse or ranged weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d6 damage if you have advantage on the attack roll, or if an ally is within 5 feet of the target and you don't have disadvantage.
- You have advantage on Investigation checks made to detect traps, secret doors, or hidden compartments.
- You may attempt to disarm traps as a bonus action by spending **1 SP**.

#### 6th Level: Dungeon Instincts
- You gain darkvision out to 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.
- When you roll initiative in a dungeon, ruin, or enclosed hostile area, you may spend **1 SP** to gain advantage on the roll.
- Your Sneak Attack damage increases to **2d6**.


#### 6th Level: Relic Sense
 
Years spent in ruins and tombs have sharpened your instinct for what's magical, valuable, or dangerous before you've even touched it.
 
- As an action, spend 2 MP to sense the presence and general direction of magic within 60 feet of you, as though you had cast *Detect Magic*. This effect lasts until the end of your next turn and does not require concentration.
- As an action, spend 2 MP to instantly learn the properties of one magic item you are holding or touching, as though you had cast *Identify*. This does not require an hour of study; your knowledge of relics lets you read it in the moment.
- As a bonus action, spend 1 MP to gain advantage on an Investigation check made to detect traps, secret doors, or hidden compartments.

You may use each of these benefits a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest, and each use still costs the MP listed.

#### 10th Level: Evasive Explorer
- When you succeed on a Dexterity saving throw that would normally deal half damage, you take no damage and may move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
- When you fail such a saving throw, you may spend **1 SP** to take half damage instead.
- Your Sneak Attack damage increases to **3d6**.

\column

#### 14th Level: Master of Relics
- You gain proficiency with all tools.
- When you fail a saving throw caused by a magic item you are attuned to, you may spend **1 SP** to reroll the saving throw and take the new result.
- Your Sneak Attack damage increases to **4d6**.

#### 18th Level: Legendary Delver
- You automatically detect nonmagical traps and secret doors within 10 feet.
- Once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you instead drop to 1 hit point and may immediately Disengage without using an action.
- Your Sneak Attack damage increases to **5d6**.

{{footnote Classes | Adventurer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Minstrel

Minstrels are performers and storytellers who bolster allies through music, charm, and subtle magic.

#### 3rd Level: Bardic Inspiration
- You gain a pool of Inspiration Dice (d6).
- As a bonus action, you may spend **1 SP** to grant one creature within 60 feet an Inspiration Die.
- Within 10 minutes, the creature may add the die to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw.

Your Inspiration Die becomes a d8 at 10th level and a d10 at 18th level.

#### 3rd Level: Spellcasting

You cast spells by spending Magic Points (MP). You must meet all normal casting requirements. This spellcasting counts as limited spellcasting and does not grant access to high-level spell effects outside your Path.

- You learn two cantrips and two 1st-level spells from the Bard spell list.
- Charisma is your spellcasting ability.
- You cast spells by spending **MP equal to the spell's level + 1** (cantrips cost 1 MP).

#### 6th Level: Encouraging Performance
- When you grant Bardic Inspiration, the target gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.
- As a reaction, when a creature within 30 feet fails a saving throw, you may spend **1 SP** to allow it to reroll the save and take the new result.

#### 10th Level: Versatile Performer
- When you grant Bardic Inspiration, you may also allow the creature to:
  - Move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, or
  - Gain advantage on its next Charisma-based ability check.
- You may have up to two active Inspiration Dice at one time.

#### 14th Level: Resonant Magic
- When you cast a spell that targets allies, you may spend **1 SP** to extend its duration by 1 round, if applicable.
- When you cast a spell that restores hit points, add your Charisma modifier to one target's healing.

#### 18th Level: Song of Legends
- Once per long rest, as an action, you may inspire up to six creatures of your choice within 60 feet.
- Each creature gains an Inspiration Die, temporary hit points equal to your Adventurer level, and advantage on its next attack roll or saving throw.

{{footnote Classes | Adventurer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Wild Scout

Wild Scouts are trackers and hunters who blend martial skill with light primal magic and an intimate knowledge of the land.

#### 3rd Level: Favored Terrain
Choose one favored terrain: forest, mountain, desert, swamp, plains, or coast.

While in your favored terrain:
- You have advantage on Survival and Nature checks.
- You cannot become lost by nonmagical means.
- You and your allies ignore difficult terrain caused by natural features.

#### 3rd Level: Spellcasting

You cast spells by spending Magic Points (MP). You must meet all normal casting requirements. This spellcasting counts as limited spellcasting and does not grant access to high-level spell effects outside your Path.

- You learn two cantrips and two 1st-level spells from the Druid or Ranger spell list.
- Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.
- You cast spells by spending **MP equal to the spell's level + 1** (cantrips cost 1 MP).

#### 6th Level: Hunter's Awareness
- You gain advantage on initiative rolls while in your favored terrain.
- As a bonus action, you may spend **1 SP** to mark a creature you can see for 1 minute. You have advantage on the first attack you make against that creature each round.

#### 10th Level: Natural Adaptation
- You gain resistance to one damage type associated with your favored terrain (DM approval).
- Difficult terrain does not slow your movement while you are traveling stealthily.
- When you cast a spell that affects terrain or movement, its area subtly increases (DM adjudication).

#### 14th Level: Relentless Tracker
- You always know the direction of a creature you are tracking if it has passed through your favored terrain within the last 24 hours.
- Opportunity attacks you make against marked creatures are made with advantage.

#### 18th Level: Avatar of the Wilds
- While in your favored terrain, you have advantage on all saving throws.
- Once per long rest, you may spend **3 SP** to gain a climbing speed and swimming speed equal to your walking speed for 10 minutes.
- When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you regain **1 SP**.

# Blightbound

*"Power does not beg. Power takes."*

Blightbound are warriors infused with corruptive arcane force, who channel blight, fear, and domination through sheer force of will. They wade into battle expecting harm, <br> because harm is fuel. Pain becomes <br> power. Suffering becomes <br> command.

Where others cast spells from afar, <br> a Blightbound stands at the center of the storm.

---

> ##### A Turn as a Blightbound
> You close the distance, hit twice, and spend Demonic Power Points to make one of those hits far worse than it looked. When things go badly you stop holding the curse back and change shape.

## Class Features
As a Blightbound, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Blightbound level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor, medium armor  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
- **Tools:** Disguise kit  
- **Saving Throws:** Constitution, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Persuasion, Religion  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to equipment granted by your background:
- (a) a greatsword or (b) two martial one-handed weapons  
- (a) scale mail or (b) leather armor  
- (a) a cursed arcane focus or (b) a component pouch  
- A black cloak and ceremonial mask
