### Core Features

#### 1st Level: Demonic Might
Your body is a conduit of blight.
- Your unarmed strikes deal **1d6 necrotic damage** (1d10 at 10th level).
- When wielding a two-handed weapon, you may use **Charisma** instead of Strength for damage rolls.

#### 1st Level: Blight Engine (DPP)
You generate **Demon Power Points (DPP)** through violence and suffering.

- DPP starts at **0**
- DPP resets to **0** on a short or long rest
- You cannot exceed your maximum DPP

#### Gaining DPP
- **Once per turn**, when you hit with a melee weapon or unarmed strike: **+1 DPP**
- When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 HP, you gain **+1 DPP**
- When you deal a Critical hit with an unarmed strike, you gain an additional **+1 DPP**
- When you take damage from a hostile creature:

| Level | Damage Required | DPP Gained |
|------|-----------------|------------|
| 1–6 | Every 6 damage | +1 |
| 7–13 | Every 5 damage | +1 |
| 14–20 | Every 4 damage | +1 |

Damage is tracked cumulatively. Self-inflicted damage does not count. Damage tracked is reset upon a short/long rest.

#### 3rd Level: Spellcasting
You gain spellcasting fueled by **Demon Power Points (DPP)**.

- **Spellcasting Ability:** Charisma
- **Spell Lists:** Warlock and Paladin  
- **Spell Cost:** Spell level + 1 DPP (cantrips cost 1 DPP)  

#### 2nd Level: Blight Invocations
You learn **two Blight Invocations**, and you learn more at higher levels.
- You gain additional invocations at 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level
- You may replace one invocation when you gain a level

Invocations enhance melee, durability, and spellcasting.


#### 5th Level: Extra Attack
You can attack twice when you take the Attack action.

#### 5th Level: Crushing Blows
When you hit with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, you may spend **2 DPP** to deal extra necrotic damage equal to **your Blightbound level + Charisma modifier**.

You can use Crushing Blows **once per turn**. Because Extra Attack arrives at the same level, without this limit a 5th-level Blightbound could spend their entire pool on a single round and a 20th-level one could add well over a hundred points of necrotic damage in six seconds.

#### 6th Level: Malice Unbound
Once per long rest, you may transform as a bonus action for 1 minute:
- Gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Blightbound level
- Increase your reach by 5 feet
- Damage-based DPP thresholds are reduced by 1

#### 7th Level: Hardened Fury
Your damage threshold for gaining DPP from damage is reduced by 1. This reduction is already built into the table above.

#### 9th Level: Warlord's Wrath
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone.

When you reduce a creature to 0 HP, enemies within 10 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be frightened until the end of their next turn.

#### 10th Level: Demonic Overlord
- Creatures frightened by you have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.
- Your unarmed strikes ignore resistance to necrotic damage.

#### 13th Level: Aura of Domination
Hostile creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saving throws against fear and charm effects.

#### 14th Level: Apex Demon Form
Once per long rest, you may enter an apex form for 1 minute:
- Regain 10 HP at the start of each turn while below half HP
- Gain advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws
- Your size counts as Large for grappling

{{footnote Classes | Blightbound }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

#### 20th Level: True Blight Sovereign
Once per long rest, you become an avatar of domination for 1 minute:
- Regain **1 DPP** at the start of each turn
- Spell costs are reduced by 1 DPP (minimum 1)
- Your melee attacks deal an additional **1d10 necrotic damage**

### Path of Dominion

Blightbound who walk the Path of Dominion are after control rather than chaos. Their power manifests as an oppressive presence that breaks the will of enemies and turns pain into authority.

#### 3rd Level: Tyrant's Presence
Your very presence weighs heavily on your foes.

- When you gain DPP from hitting a creature, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.
- Once per turn, when you spend DPP on a feature or spell, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

#### 6th Level: Iron Supremacy
You learn to convert suffering into resilience.

- When you gain DPP from taking damage, you also reduce the triggering damage by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus.
- While you have at least 1 DPP, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.

#### 10th Level: Crushing Authority
Your domination becomes physically undeniable.

- When you hit a creature with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, you may spend **2 DPP** to force it to make a Strength saving throw.
  - On a failure, the creature is **knocked prone or pushed up to 10 feet** (your choice).
  - On a success, its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
- Large or smaller creatures automatically fail this save if they are frightened of you.

#### 14th Level: Sovereign Form
Your Malice Unbound and Apex Demon Form become expressions of calculated supremacy.

- When you activate **Malice Unbound** or **Apex Demon Form**, you immediately gain **2 DPP**.
- While transformed, hostile creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you.

This effect ends if you are incapacitated.

\column

#### 18th Level: Absolute Dominion
Your power bends the battlefield to your will.

- At the start of your turn, if you have **0 DPP**, you gain **1 DPP**.
- Once per turn, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you may spend **3 DPP** to drop to **1 hit point instead**.
- Creatures frightened by you have disadvantage on Constitution saving throws against your spells and features.

{{footnote Classes | Blightbound }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of Desolation

Blightbound of Desolation channel their accumulated malice into ruinous spellcraft, and break armies before blades ever meet.

#### 3rd Level: Blighted Casting
You learn to convert dominance into spellpower.

- When you spend DPP to cast a spell, you may reduce its cost by **1 DPP** (minimum 1).
- Once per turn, when you deal spell damage to a creature, you gain **1 DPP**.

#### 6th Level: Tyrant's Gaze
Your magic crushes resistance.

- Creatures frightened by you have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.
- As a bonus action, you may spend **2 DPP** to force one creature you can see within 60 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw.
  - On a failure, the creature is frightened of you until the end of its next turn.

#### 10th Level: Shadow Cleave
Your destructive magic bleeds outward.

- When you deal spell damage to a creature, you may choose a second creature within 10 feet of it.
- The second creature takes necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
- You may use this feature a number of times per turn equal to your proficiency bonus.

#### 14th Level: Doom of Ruin
You can focus all your malice into a single catastrophic spell.

- Once per long rest, when you cast a spell that deals damage, you may treat all damage dice as having rolled their maximum value.
- Casting a spell this way costs **3 additional DPP**.

#### 18th Level: Cataclysm Incarnate
Your presence turns the battlefield into a dead zone.

- At the start of your turn, you gain **1 DPP** if at least one hostile creature is within 30 feet of you.
- When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.

\column

### Path of the Dreadnought

Blightbound of the Path of the Dreadnought fuse arcane corruption directly into muscle and bone, becoming unstoppable engines of destruction.

#### 3rd Level: Arcane Physiology
Your body becomes a conduit for magic.

- When you spend DPP to cast a spell that targets only yourself, you gain **1 DPP**.
- Your unarmed strikes deal **1d8 necrotic or fire damage** (your choice). This increases to **1d10** at 10th level.

#### 6th Level: Demon's Charge
You turn momentum into devastation.

- When you take the Dash action, you may spend **1 DPP** to move through enemy spaces.
- Each creature you pass through must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
- You do not provoke opportunity attacks during this movement.

#### 10th Level: Ruinous Might
Your physical presence is overwhelming.

- You count as one size larger for the purposes of grappling, shoving, and carrying capacity.
- When you successfully grapple a creature, you gain **1 DPP**.
- While grappling a creature, you have advantage on attack rolls against it.

#### 14th Level: Monstrous Armament
Your limbs become weapons of annihilation.

- Your unarmed strikes deal **2d10 necrotic or fire damage**.
- When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you may spend **2 DPP** to force it to make a Constitution saving throw.
  - On a failure, the creature is stunned until the end of its next turn.
  - On a success, it is restrained until the end of its next turn.

#### 18th Level: Apex Predator
You are no longer merely humanoid.

- At the start of each of your turns, you gain **1 DPP** if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature.
- When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you may immediately make one additional unarmed strike as part of the same action.

{{footnote Classes | Blightbound }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Champion

*Divine warriors who carry the will of the Golden Goddesses. No holy order appointed them; belief, courage, and action did.*

Champions are warriors empowered by devotion to Din, Nayru, or Farore. Whether they wield blade or bow, they channel divine power through conviction rather than doctrine. They are what Hyrule's ideals look like in a fight.

:

> ##### A Turn as a Champion
> You mark an enemy as the goddess's business, hit it twice, and spend your reaction or bonus action lifting whoever near you needs it most. From 3rd level a spell replaces one of those attacks when healing matters more than damage.

## Class Features
As a Champion, you gain the following class features.

:

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d10 per Champion level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 10 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier  

:

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** All armor, shields  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
- **Tools:** None  
- **Saving Throws:** Strength, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose 2 from Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, Persuasion, Survival  

:

### Spellcasting
Beginning at 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells.

**Spellcasting Ability:** Charisma  
**Spell Lists:** Cleric and Paladin  
**Spell Level Cap:** 6th level (Overchanneling required for spells above 5th level).  

You cast spells by expending **Magic Points (MP)** equal to the spell's level + 1 (cantrips cost 1 MP).

:

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a martial weapon and a shield, or (b) two martial weapons  
- (a) five javelins or (b) any simple melee weapon  
- (a) chain mail or (b) leather armor, a longbow, and 20 arrows  
- (a) a priest's pack or (b) an explorer's pack  
- A holy symbol of your chosen goddess

### Core Class Features

#### 1st Level: Divine Spark
You carry the divine essence of the Golden Goddesses.

- You use **Charisma** for spellcasting and Champion features.
- You have advantage on Persuasion checks when dealing with members of your own faith or culture.

#### 1st Level: Fighting Style
Choose one Fighting Style:

- **Defense.** +1 AC while wearing armor  
- **Dueling.** +2 damage with a one-handed weapon  
- **Great Weapon Fighting.** Reroll 1s and 2s on damage dice with two-handed weapons  
- **Blessed Warrior.** Learn two Cleric cantrips, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability. If you take this style before you gain Magic Points at 3rd level, you have an MP pool of 2 at 1st and 2nd level, usable only for these cantrips  
- **Archery.** +2 bonus to attack rolls with ranged weapons  

#### 2nd Level: Heroic Presence
Twice per short rest, as a bonus action, choose one creature within 30 feet.  
That creature gains a bonus equal to your Charisma modifier on its next attack roll or saving throw.

#### 3rd Level: Divine Mark
As a bonus action, mark a creature you can see within 60 feet for 1 minute.

Once per turn, when you hit the marked creature with a **weapon attack (melee or ranged)**, you deal an extra **1d6 radiant damage**.

#### 3rd Level: Sacred Mantle
You dedicate yourself to one of the Golden Goddesses:

- **Mantle of Din: Flame of Power**
- **Mantle of Nayru: Shield of Wisdom**
- **Mantle of Farore: Grace of Courage**

Your mantle grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

#### 5th Level: Extra Attack
You can attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.

\column

#### 7th Level: Aura of the Chosen
You project a divine aura in a 10-foot radius while conscious.

As a bonus action, choose one mode. This aura uses **soft concentration** (see the Magic System chapter). It does not conflict with any concentration spell you are currently maintaining, but it ends if you are incapacitated or fail the DC 8 Constitution saving throw triggered by taking damage.

- **Aura of Resolve.** Allies gain +CHA to saving throws  
- **Aura of Might.** Allies gain +CHA to damage rolls  

You may switch modes as a bonus action.

#### 9th Level: Relentless Advance
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack while below half your hit point maximum, you regain **1 MP**.

#### 11th Level: Divine Strikes
Once per turn, when you hit with a **weapon attack (melee or ranged)**, deal an extra **1d8 radiant damage**.

At 17th level, this damage increases to **2d8**.

#### 13th Level: Indomitable Spirit
Once per long rest, when you fail a saving throw, you may reroll it and take the new result.

#### 15th Level: Legendary Resistance
Once per long rest, when you fail a saving throw, you may choose to succeed instead.

#### 20th Level: Avatar of the Goddess
Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you become an avatar of divine power for 1 minute:

- At the start of each turn, regain **1 MP**
- Spell costs are reduced by **1 MP** (minimum 1)
- Your weapon attacks deal an extra **1d10 radiant damage**

{{footnote Classes | Champion }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Sacred Mantles

At 3rd level, a Champion swears themselves to one of the Golden Goddesses and takes on her aspect through a **Sacred Mantle**.  
Your mantle functions much like a paladin's oath: a living expression of belief rather than strict dogma.

You gain features from your chosen mantle at **3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level**.

:

### Mantle of Din: Flame of Power
*Goddess of Power*

Champions of Din are living weapons who advance relentlessly and break foes through overwhelming force.

#### 3rd Level: Flamebrand
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you may deal an extra **1d8 fire or radiant damage** (your choice).

- You may use this feature once per turn.
- This extra damage applies to **melee or ranged weapon attacks**.

#### 6th Level: Crimson Wrath
When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you may make **one weapon attack as a bonus action**.

- You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), and you regain all uses on a long rest.

#### 10th Level: Burning Aura
Your divine fury radiates outward.

- Enemies of your choice within **10 feet** of you take **fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier** at the start of their turn.
- A creature can only take this damage once per turn.

#### 14th Level: Avatar of Din
Your attacks burn through all defenses.

- Your weapon attacks **ignore resistance** to fire and radiant damage.
- Creatures immune to fire or radiant damage are instead treated as resistant to it.

#### 18th Level: Devastating Blows
Your strikes carry apocalyptic force.

- Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of **19–20**.
- When you score a critical hit, you roll **one additional weapon damage die**.

\column

### Mantle of Nayru: Shield of Wisdom
*Goddess of Wisdom*

Champions of Nayru stand immovable and defend allies through insight, patience, and divine protection.

#### 3rd Level: Sacred Shield
When you or a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you may use your reaction to reduce that damage by **1d10 + your Charisma modifier**.

- You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 6th Level: Divine Bastion
Your resilience deepens under pressure.

- While you are at **half your hit point maximum or lower**, you gain **resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage**.

#### 10th Level: Ward of Nayru
Your protective presence bolsters allies.

- While your **Aura of the Chosen** is active, allies within the aura gain a **+1 bonus to AC**.

#### 14th Level: Still as Stone
You are an unyielding bulwark.

- You cannot be **forcibly moved**, knocked prone, or teleported against your will.
- You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would restrain or paralyze you.

#### 18th Level: Perfect Guard
Your defense borders on the absolute.

- Critical hits against you become **normal hits**.
- When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you may use your reaction to impose disadvantage on its next attack before the end of its next turn.

{{footnote Classes | Champion }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Mantle of Farore: Grace of Courage
*Goddess of Courage*

Champions of Farore inspire hope and persistence. They pull allies back from the brink and keep moving forward against impossible odds.

#### 3rd Level: Emerald Touch
As an action, you may touch a creature to restore **1d8 + your Charisma modifier** hit points.

- This ability costs **MP** and follows your Champion spellcasting rules.
- This healing increases by **1d8** at 11th level.

#### 6th Level: Vital Pulse
Your encouragement carries restorative power.

- When you use **Heroic Presence**, the affected creature also gains **temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier**.

#### 10th Level: Cleanse Spirit
You can purge lingering afflictions.

- As an action, you may touch a creature and end **one condition** affecting it (charmed, frightened, poisoned, blinded, deafened, or paralyzed).
- This feature costs **2 MP**.

#### 14th Level: Song of Restoration
Your presence renews the battlefield.

- As an action, you may heal all allied creatures of your choice within **10 feet** for **2d8 + your Charisma modifier** hit points.
- Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend **3 MP** to use it again.

#### 18th Level: Divine Return
You refuse to let heroes fall.

- Once per long rest, when a creature you can see within 30 feet drops to 0 hit points, you may use your reaction to restore it to **1 hit point**.
- That creature may immediately stand up without spending movement.

{{footnote Classes | Champion }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Champion Spell List

Champions are warriors empowered by the goddesses to channel divine force in battle. Their magic reflects the Cleric's divine mandate and the Paladin's warrior faith: healing, protection, and divine wrath delivered through a fighter's body.

**Spellcasting Ability:** Charisma
**Spell Lists:** Cleric and Paladin

Spells marked with ✦ are **Zelda-original spells** found in the Zelda Spells compendium; all others are drawn from the standard 5e spell list or named variants thereof, and use standard 5e statistics unless the compendium provides a Hyrule-flavored version.

# Goddess Chanter

*"Our voices weave the threads of fate. Where we sing, the Goddess listens."*

Goddess Chanters are sacred performers and ritual leaders who channel the will of Hylia and the Golden Goddesses through song. Their music heals wounds, strengthens resolve, and condemns those who stand against balance.

A Champion is handed divine might. A Chanter builds it out of melody, rhythm, and devotion.

---

> ##### A Turn as a Goddess Chanter
> You sing. One song heals or shields the people around you, another lands on an enemy as judgment, and your ocarina or harp is the focus you do it through. You are rarely the one being hit, and always the reason someone is still standing.

## Class Features
As a Goddess Chanter, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Goddess Chanter level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, shortswords  
- **Tools:** One musical instrument (harp, ocarina, or ceremonial bell)  
- **Saving Throws:** Wisdom, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose three from Performance, Persuasion, Insight, Religion, Medicine, Arcana  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) mace or (b) shortsword  
- (a) leather armor or (b) shield  
- (a) harp, (b) ocarina, or (c) ceremonial bell  
- (a) holy text or (b) prayer wheel  
- Fine robes and a vial of sacred water

### Core Class Features

#### 1st Level: Harmonic Divinity
Your magic is shaped through sacred music.

- Charisma is your spellcasting ability.
- You may use your instrument as a spellcasting focus.

---

#### 1st Level: Sacred Songs
 
You learn divine songs that empower allies or weaken foes. Each Sacred Song is a sustained harmonic effect rather than a spell: a continuous expression of divine attunement that lasts as long as you maintain it.
 
- Activating a Sacred Song costs **MP** as listed in the table below.
- Sacred Songs use **soft concentration** (see Magic System chapter). Unlike standard concentration, a Sacred Song does not conflict with a concentration spell you are also maintaining, so you may sustain one Sacred Song and one concentration spell at the same time. However, you may only maintain one Sacred Song at a time unless a class feature explicitly allows more.
- A Sacred Song ends early if you are **incapacitated or silenced**, if you choose to end it as a **free action**, or if you fail the soft concentration saving throw triggered by taking damage (DC 8 Constitution).
- You do not need to keep your instrument in hand once a Sacred Song is active, but you must have used it to activate the song.
{{table,
| Song | Effect | MP Cost |
|:-----|:--------|:-------:|
| Ballad of Nayru | Allies within 30 feet gain +1d4 to saving throws (10 min) | 1 |
| Ballad of Farore | Allies within 30 feet gain +1d4 to attack rolls | 1 |
| Ballad of Din | Allies within 30 feet gain +1d4 damage | 1 |
| Requiem of Twilight | Foes within 30 feet suffer −1d4 to saving throws | 2 |
| Aria of the Storm | Allies within 30 feet ignore damage resistance (1 min) | 3 |
}}

---

#### 2nd Level: Blessed Refrain
When you restore hit points to a creature with a spell, that creature regains an additional **1d4 hit points** at the start of its next turn.

---

#### 2nd Level: Hylian Hymn
You know *Guidance* and *Sacred Flame*, and casting either costs no MP.

\column

#### 3rd Level: Choir of the Goddess
At 3rd level, you choose a divine choir that shapes your sacred calling:

- **Keeper of Grace**
- **Herald of Power**
- **Voice of Judgment**

#### 5th Level: Resonant Healing
Your healing echoes with divine resonance.

- Blessed Refrain increases to **1d4 + your Charisma modifier**.
- Sacred Songs affect creatures within **60 feet**.

#### 7th Level: Divine Cadence
Your rhythm steadies your magic.

- Damage equal to or less than your Charisma modifier does not break concentration.
- As a bonus action, you may spend **1 SP** to extend a Sacred Song by 1 minute.

#### 9th Level: Celestial Chorus
Once per long rest, you may cast *Mass Cure Wounds* or *Greater Restoration* without expending MP.

#### 11th Level: Eternal Refrain
- Blessed Refrain lasts **3 rounds**.
- Sacred Songs grant **+1d6** instead of +1d4.

#### 13th Level: Hylia's Benediction
Once per long rest, you may perform a 10-minute ritual to cast *Heroes' Feast* without material components.

#### 15th Level: Symphony of the Goddess
- You may maintain **two Sacred Songs** simultaneously.
- Blessed Refrain affects all allies within 30 feet.

#### 17th Level: Avatar of Song
- Allies within 30 feet have advantage on death saving throws.
- Magical silence fails within 60 feet of you.

#### 20th Level: Incarnation of Hylia
You embody divine harmony.

- You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
- Once per long rest, you may cast *Wish*, but only for healing, restoration, or resurrection effects.

{{footnote Classes | Goddess Chanter }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Keeper of Grace

Keepers of Grace are devoted healers and ritual singers who refuse to let hope die. Their songs linger like gentle echoes. They mend wounds and call lost souls back from the brink.

#### 6th Level: Lullaby of Life
- You may perform a **10-minute requiem** to cast *Revivify* without expending MP or material components.
- A creature restored this way regains additional hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.

#### 10th Level: Gentle Continuance
- Whenever **Blessed Refrain** triggers on a creature, that creature also gains **advantage on its next saving throw** before the end of its next turn.
- If the saving throw succeeds, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.

#### 14th Level: Eternal Grace
- Once per long rest, you may cast *True Resurrection* as a **1-hour ritual**, ignoring material components.
- Creatures restored by this ritual are cured of all diseases, curses, and conditions affecting them.

#### 18th Level: Mercy Beyond Death
- When an ally within **30 feet** is reduced to 0 hit points, you may use your reaction to restore that ally to **half its maximum hit points**.
- Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

\column

### Herald of Power

Heralds of Power sing of triumph, never of rest. Their voices harden resolve, sharpen blades, and turn courage into momentum.

#### 6th Level: Aria of Victory
- When a creature benefiting from your **Sacred Songs** scores a critical hit, it deals an additional **2d8 radiant damage**.
- This damage increases to **4d8** at 18th level.

#### 10th Level: Battle Hymn
- At the start of each of their turns, allies affected by your Sacred Songs gain **temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier**.
- These temporary hit points do not stack.

#### 14th Level: Divine Fanfare
- Once per long rest, you may unleash a triumphant refrain.
- As an action, choose any number of allies within **30 feet**. Each chosen creature may immediately take **one additional action**.
- This effect does not require concentration.

#### 18th Level: Crescendo of Triumph
- While at least one Sacred Song is active, allies affected by your songs have **advantage on the first attack roll they make each round**.
- If an ally already has advantage, it instead gains a bonus equal to your Charisma modifier on the damage roll.

}}

{{footnote Classes | Goddess Chanter }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Voice of Judgment

Voices of Judgment channel the Goddess as a witness rather than a comfort. Their songs condemn the wicked, unravel defenses, and hold foes still under divine scrutiny.

#### 6th Level: Requiem of Condemnation
- You learn the Sacred Song **Requiem of Twilight**.
- While this song is active, enemies within range suffer a **−1d4 penalty to saving throws**.

#### 10th Level: Judging Echo
- When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, it takes **radiant damage equal to your Charisma modifier**.
- This damage can occur once per turn.

#### 14th Level: Chorus of Chains
- Once per long rest, as an action, you may invoke binding judgment.
- Creatures of your choice within **30 feet** must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become **restrained for 1 minute**.
- A restrained creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.

#### 18th Level: Verdict of the Goddess
- Once per long rest, when a creature fails a saving throw against your spell, you may treat the result as a **natural 1**.
- If the spell deals damage, it deals maximum damage instead.

# Interloper
*"We were not cast out for wickedness. We were cast out for daring to learn what the gods would not share."*
:::::
> ##### A Turn as an Interloper
> You put an illusion somewhere useful, step through shadow to somewhere better, and leave an enemy attacking a version of you that was never there. You win fights by deciding where they happen.

## Class Features
As an Interloper, you gain the following class features.
:

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Interloper level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  
:

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, rapiers, shortswords  
- **Tools:** Disguise kit, one gaming set  
- **Saving Throws:** Intelligence, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, Stealth  

:

### Spellcasting
- **Spellcasting Ability:** Intelligence (you may choose Charisma at 1st level instead)  
- **Spellcasting Type:** Full caster  
- **Spell List:** Interloper spell list (illusion, enchantment, force, psychic, control)  
- You cast spells by spending **MP equal to the spell's level + 1** (cantrips cost 1 MP).
- **Spell Level Cap:** 9th level (Overchanneling required for spells above 5th level).

:

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a rapier or (b) a shortsword  
- (a) leather armor or (b) scholar's robes and a component pouch  
- (a) a disguise kit or (b) any gaming set  
- (a) a scholar's pack or (b) a dungeoneer's pack  
- A twilight focus (a shard of mirror, a black glass lens, or a shadow-etched sigil)

### Core Features

#### 1st Level: Forbidden Arts
You wield arcane knowledge rejected by divine orthodoxy.
- Choose **Intelligence or Charisma** as your spellcasting ability.
- You may use a one-handed weapon as a spellcasting focus.

#### 1st Level: Hex of the Depths (Soft Concentration)
As a bonus action, you afflict a creature you can see within 60 feet.  
The Hex lasts 1 minute and does not require full concentration.

Choose one effect:
- **Binding Hex:** Target's speed is reduced by 10 feet.
- **Fracturing Hex:** The first time each round the target fails a saving throw, it takes **Hex damage** (see below) as psychic damage.
- **Withering Hex:** Target has disadvantage on the first attack it makes each round.

**Hex Damage.** Your Hex deals psychic damage that scales with your level, without spending anything further:

| Interloper level | Hex damage |
|:--:|:--:|
| 1st–4th | 1d6 |
| 5th–10th | 2d6 |
| 11th–16th | 3d6 |
| 17th–20th | 4d6 |

Only the **Fracturing Hex** deals damage on its own. Path features and other abilities that refer to Hex damage use the same table.

#### 2nd Level: Eldritch Insight
- You gain double proficiency on Arcana checks related to ancient or forbidden magic.
- You can sense invisible or ethereal creatures within 30 feet (no action).

#### 3rd Level: Path of the Interloper
At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes your thirst for power:

- **Cyclone Tyrant**
- **Bladebound Paragon**
- **Twilight Dominator**

#### 5th Level: Malefic Surge
- Your Hexes may be moved to a new target as a bonus action.
- Add your spellcasting modifier to Hex damage once per turn.

#### 7th Level: Shadow Pact
Once per long rest, you may summon a lesser arcane minion (spectral construct, animated shadow, or bound spirit) for 1 minute.  
The minion obeys your commands and cannot harm your allies.

#### 9th Level: Corrupted Knowledge
Once per long rest, when you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you may choose to succeed instead.


#### 11th Level: Master of Hexes
You may maintain **two Hexes simultaneously**.

#### 13th Level: Arcane Defiance
You have advantage on concentration checks, and damage cannot break your concentration unless it exceeds your spellcasting modifier + proficiency bonus.

#### 15th Level: Veilbreaker
Your spells ignore resistance to psychic, force, and necrotic damage.

#### 17th Level: Twilight Ascension
Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you enter a heightened arcane state for 1 minute:
- Advantage on concentration checks  
- Spells ignore resistance  
- Once per turn, when a creature fails a save against your spell, it takes extra psychic or force damage equal to your spellcasting modifier  
- Movement does not provoke opportunity attacks from Hexed creatures

#### 20th Level: Master of the Twilight
- Twilight Ascension refreshes on a **short rest**
- While ascended:
  - Hexes cost 0 MP
  - You may maintain **two Hexes**
  - Once per turn, when a creature fails a saving throw by 5 or more, you may **stun, restrain, or knock it prone**

{{footnote Classes | Interloper }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Cyclone Tyrant

*The storm does not negotiate. It does not pause. It simply arrives.*

Cyclone Tyrants are scholars of raw arcane devastation, Interlopers who have turned their study of forbidden magic toward pure destructive force. Where the Bladebound Paragon fights through bound servants and the Twilight Dominator wins through misdirection, the Cyclone Tyrant wins by being the most dangerous thing in the room. They do not hide what they are. They simply make sure nothing survives long enough to care.

#### 3rd Level: Windlash

When you cast a spell that deals force or thunder damage, you may choose one creature affected by the spell and push it up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. If this movement forces the creature into a wall, another creature, or solid terrain, it takes an additional 1d6 force damage and the push stops immediately.

In addition, you have advantage on the Strength saving throw rolled to avoid being pushed, knocked prone, or otherwise forcibly moved by your own area spells, should you choose to stand within them.

#### 6th Level: Tempest Shaping

Your mastery over force and air lets you sculpt your own devastation with precision. When you cast a spell that affects an area (a line, cone, cube, sphere, or cylinder), you may exclude a number of unoccupied or occupied spaces from the spell's effect equal to your spellcasting modifier (minimum 1). Excluded spaces are treated as if outside the spell's area entirely. Creatures within them take no damage or effect and are not considered targeted.

You decide which spaces to exclude when you cast the spell, before any saving throws are rolled.

#### 10th Level: Arcane Overpressure

The air around your spells crackles with leftover force, looking for somewhere to go. When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, it takes additional force damage equal to your proficiency bonus, and the ground, walls, or unsecured objects within 5 feet of it are buffeted hard enough to extinguish unprotected flames and scatter loose, unattended items.

In addition, once per turn, when a creature fails a saving throw against your spell by 5 or more, you may immediately push it up to 10 feet using the same rules as Windlash, even if the spell does not normally deal force or thunder damage.

#### 14th Level: Sovereign of Storms

You no longer walk through your own devastation. You ride above it. While concentrating on a spell, you gain a flying speed of 30 feet, and you do not provoke opportunity attacks when you fly out of a creature's reach.

In addition, while flying, your spells that deal force or thunder damage have their range increased by 30 feet, as the open air carries your power further and with greater precision.

#### 18th Level: Ascended Cyclone

While your Twilight Ascension is active, you become the storm given purpose:

- Your spells that deal force or thunder damage have their range increased by 60 feet (in place of the 14th level bonus) and their area of effect increases by 5 feet in every relevant dimension (radius, cube size, cone length, or line length and width).
- Whenever you deal force or thunder damage to a Large or smaller creature with a spell, that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone, in addition to any push effects from Windlash or Arcane Overpressure.
- Once per turn, when you push a creature into another creature using Windlash, both creatures take the force damage from the collision, and the second creature must also succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

{{footnote Classes | Interloper }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Bladebound Paragon

*The blade does not tire. The blade does not hesitate. The blade is exactly as merciless as you ask it to be.*

Bladebound Paragons are masters of bound constructs and animated weaponry, Interlopers who have learned to pour a fragment of twilight essence into steel and stone until it moves with a purpose of its own. Unlike the Cyclone Tyrant's raw devastation or the Twilight Dominator's illusions, the Bladebound Paragon fights through extension: a spectral arsenal that moves at their command and strikes with their will, even when their own hands are otherwise occupied.

#### 3rd Level: Bound Arsenal

As a bonus action, you may summon one **Bound Weapon** (a spectral construct shaped from twilight energy and the memory of a real weapon) in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. When you summon it, choose one of the following forms. The Bound Weapon uses your spell attack modifier for its attack rolls and your spellcasting modifier where relevant.

| Form | Attack | Damage | Special |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Sword Spirit** | Melee, reach 5 ft. | 1d8 + spellcasting modifier slashing | Can make an attack as part of the action that summons it |
| **Spear Spirit** | Melee, reach 10 ft. | 1d10 + spellcasting modifier piercing | Can attack two different creatures within reach once per round (one attack roll each) |
| **Bow Spirit** | Ranged, 60 ft. | 1d8 + spellcasting modifier piercing | Does not require ammunition; ignores half and three-quarters cover |

A Bound Weapon has AC 13 + your proficiency bonus, hit points equal to 5 × your Interloper level, and a flying or hovering speed of 20 feet (it has no need to touch the ground). It acts on your turn, immediately after you, and can move and attack each round on your command, which costs you no action. If it is destroyed, the link is severed and you cannot summon a new Bound Weapon until you finish a short or long rest, unless you spend 2 MP to resummon it early.

#### 6th Level: Enhanced Pact

Your bond with the twilight deepens enough to sustain a second presence. You may maintain two Bound Weapons (of the same or different forms) simultaneously, or one Bound Weapon and one minion summoned by Shadow Pact at the same time. Each acts on your turn and is directed independently, so you may give them different commands in the same round.

#### 10th Level: Living Armory

Your Bound Weapons grow sharper with your own mastery of forbidden arts. Each Bound Weapon's damage increases by an amount equal to your spellcasting modifier (added on top of the modifier already included in its damage), and its hit points increase to 8 × your Interloper level.

In addition, you may now switch a Bound Weapon's form (from Sword Spirit to Bow Spirit, for example) as a bonus action, causing it to dissolve and instantly reform in its new shape in the same space.

#### 14th Level: Greater Constructs

Your Shadow Pact minion and your Bound Weapons alike grow stronger as they draw on a deeper well of twilight power. Your Shadow Pact summon's hit points and damage dice both increase by 50% (round up), and it may now be maintained for 10 minutes instead of 1, without requiring concentration.

Your Bound Weapons gain a fourth available form:

| Form | Attack | Damage | Special |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Twin Fang Spirit** | Melee, reach 5 ft. | 1d6 + spellcasting modifier slashing, twice | Each attack that hits applies a stacking −1 to the target's AC until the end of your next turn (maximum −3) |

#### 18th Level: Perfect Symbiosis

While your Twilight Ascension is active, every construct bound to you (your Bound Weapons and any Shadow Pact minion) fights as a perfect extension of your will:

- They have advantage on all attack rolls.
- They have advantage on all saving throws.
- When a Bound Weapon or Shadow Pact minion reduces a creature to 0 hit points, you immediately regain 1 MP (maximum once per round).
- You may maintain three Bound Weapons simultaneously (up from two), or two Bound Weapons and one Shadow Pact minion, all acting independently on your turn.

{{footnote Classes | Interloper }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Twilight Dominator

*Why fight the truth when you can simply offer them a more convincing lie?*

Twilight Dominators are masters of misdirection, doubling, and the unsettling space between what is real and what only appears to be. Where the Cyclone Tyrant overwhelms with raw force and the Bladebound Paragon fights through bound weapons, the Twilight Dominator rarely needs to be where the danger is at all. They scatter false images of themselves across the battlefield and punish enemies for striking the wrong one. At the height of their power they step out of reality altogether, leaving a perfect copy to finish the fight.

#### 3rd Level: Veil of Many

As a bonus action, you may conjure an illusory duplicate of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. The duplicate is intangible, occupies its space, and lasts until the start of your next turn or until it is targeted by an attack or a spell that requires a check or save against it, whichever comes first.

While at least one duplicate is active, attacks made against you by creatures that have not seen you act since the duplicate appeared are made with disadvantage, as the attacker is uncertain which image is real.

You may have up to one duplicate active at a time. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting modifier (minimum 1) per long rest, and you regain one use whenever you apply a Hex.

#### 6th Level: Misdirection's Price

When a creature targets your illusory duplicate with an attack, spell, or other harmful effect, you may use your reaction to cause the duplicate to immediately vanish and reappear in a new unoccupied space within 10 feet of its previous location. The triggering attack or effect automatically misses or fails against the duplicate, and the creature that was fooled has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn, as it struggles to relocate you.

In addition, your Hexes may now be applied to a creature standing adjacent to your duplicate as if it were adjacent to you.

#### 10th Level: Fractured Reality

When you cast a spell that requires a saving throw, you may conjure a second illusory duplicate as part of the same action at no additional cost (this does not require a bonus action and does not count against your normal use of Veil of Many). 

In addition, when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells while at least one of your duplicates is active, you may have a duplicate flicker into the same space as the target for an instant. The target takes extra psychic damage equal to your Interloper level as the real and the illusory blur together in front of them.

#### 14th Level: The Unseen Hand

Your duplicates are no longer purely decorative. Once per turn, when an enemy creature ends its turn within 5 feet of one of your active duplicates, you may use your reaction to make the duplicate deliver a phantom strike: the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or take psychic damage equal to 2d8 + your spellcasting modifier and have disadvantage on its next attack roll, convinced for a moment that the blow was real.

In addition, you may now have up to two duplicates active simultaneously.

#### 18th Level: Sovereign of the Unreal

Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you step fully into the Twilight Realm for 1 minute while a perfect illusory copy of yourself continues to act in your place on the battlefield:

- You become invisible and incorporeal, and you cannot be targeted, detected, or harmed by any means while in this state. You can still see, hear, and direct your duplicate's actions.
- Your duplicate occupies your space, has your statistics, and acts on your turn exactly as you direct it. It can move, take the Attack action (using your weapon and spell attack bonus), cast your spells (expending your MP normally), and apply your Hexes.
- If the duplicate would take damage that would reduce it to 0 hit points, it instead vanishes, you are immediately ejected from the Twilight Realm into the space it last occupied, and you take no damage from the triggering attack.
- While ascended (Twilight Ascension active simultaneously), your duplicate's spells ignore resistance and its Hexed targets cannot benefit from cover against it.

You may end this effect early as a free action. When the effect ends (by choice, duration, or your duplicate's defeat), you reappear in the space your duplicate last occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space.

{{pageNumber,auto}}

# Masked Wanderer

*"The faces of the fallen become my strength. Their memories, my weapons."*

::::::

> ##### A Turn as a Masked Wanderer
> You put on a different face and become something else: you gain that people's body and traits, throw three unarmed strikes at 11th level, and use that mask's Signature Technique. Then you change again when the fight changes.

## Class Features
As a Masked Wanderer, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Masked Wanderer level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** None  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, shortswords  
- **Tools:** Disguise kit, one musical instrument  
- **Saving Throws:** Strength, Charisma  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Acrobatics, Athletics, Insight, Perception, Stealth, Survival  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:
- (a) two shortswords or (b) one simple weapon  
- (a) explorer's pack or (b) dungeoneer's pack  
- an ocarina  

### Masks Known
At 1st level, you know **three transformation masks** of your choice.

You may only be transformed into **one mask at a time**.

At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (10th, 15th, and 20th), you learn **one additional mask**.
:
**Available Masks:**

- Deku
- Goron
- Gerudo
- Hylian
- Rito
- Sheikah
- Twili
- Zora

### Core Class Features

#### 1st Level: Mask Transformation
Starting at 1st level, you can assume the form granted by one of your known masks.

- **Action:** Transform into a chosen mask  
- **Duration:** Until you end it (no action required) or are incapacitated  
- **Uses:** Unlimited  

While transformed:
- You gain **all racial traits** of the mask, including its size, speed, movement modes, senses and resistances. These **replace** your own race's traits.
- Your **Strength, Dexterity and Constitution** are adjusted by the mask race's increases in place of your own race's.
- You keep your Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, alignment, personality, class features, proficiencies, hit points and Hit Dice.
- Equipment **merges into the form**, cannot be used while transformed, and reappears unchanged when you revert.

**Mask save DC** equals **8 + proficiency bonus + Strength or Dexterity modifier**, chosen when you transform.

#### Unarmored Defense
While not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your AC equals:

**10 + Dexterity modifier + Wisdom modifier**

The exception is Goron form, where the Goron racial AC applies instead.

Because your equipment merges into the form, you are always unarmored while transformed and this feature is always active there. It also applies in your own form on any occasion when you wear no armor and wield no shield.

#### 2nd Level: Martial Arts
Beginning at 2nd level:
- You may use Dexterity instead of Strength for unarmed strikes
- Your unarmed strike damage is **1d6** (1d8 at 11th level)
- When you take the Attack action, you may make one unarmed strike as a bonus action

#### 2nd Level: Signature Technique
At 2nd level, you learn one Signature Technique tied to any mask you know.
You learn additional techniques at **9th and 17th level**.

The table below lists the technique attached to each mask. Learning a technique means choosing one row from that table; you can use a technique only while wearing the mask it belongs to.

- Signature Techniques may be used **once per turn**
- They do **not** cost SP
- Saving throws use your Mask save DC

#### 3rd Level: Wandering Discipline
At 3rd level, you adopt a wandering discipline reflecting your philosophy of combat.
Your discipline grants features at **3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level**.

#### 5th Level: Extra Attack
Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.

#### 7th Level: Adaptive Forms
At 7th level, when you roll initiative, you may immediately transform into a known mask without using an action.

You may do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

{{classTable,frame,wide
#### Signature Techniques
| Mask Equipped | Technique | 
|:----------------|:----------------------|
| **Deku** | Your jump-based movement increases by 10 feet. Once per turn, when you land after moving at least 15 feet, one creature within 5 feet must succeed on a Strength save or be pushed 10 feet. |
| **Goron** | You gain resistance to bludgeoning damage. When you use Dash, you may choose to move through enemy spaces; creatures you pass through must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone. | 
| **Zora** | You may make a fin-blade throw as a ranged unarmed attack (30/60), dealing unarmed strike damage. If the attack hits, the blade returns to you automatically. | 
| **Rito** | While flying, your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. Once per turn, when you move at least 10 feet while airborne, your next attack deals +1d6 damage. | 
| **Sheikah** | You may Hide as a bonus action. When you attack a creature that has not taken a turn in combat yet, you deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. | 
| **Twili** | You gain resistance to necrotic damage. Once per turn, when you move from dim light into darkness (or vice versa), you gain advantage on your next attack or saving throw. |
| **Gerudo** | You gain resistance to fire damage. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you may reduce its speed by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. |
| **Hylian** | You gain a +1 bonus to all saving throws. Once per long rest, when you miss an attack, you may reroll it and take the new result. |
}}

{{footnote Classes | Masked Wanderer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

#### 9th Level: Mask Mastery
At 9th level:
- You have advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration while transformed
- Ending a transformation does not end grapples, movement modes, or stances you initiated

#### 11th Level: Improved Extra Attack
At 11th level, while transformed, you may make **three attacks** instead of two whenever you take the Attack action. In your own form you still make two.

#### 13th Level: Deepened Masks
At 13th level, every mask you know deepens. While transformed, you gain the benefit below in addition to that mask's racial traits and Signature Technique.

- **Deku:** Your jump distance is doubled and you take no falling damage. The push from your technique becomes 20 feet, and a creature that fails the save is also knocked prone.
- **Goron:** Your resistance to bludgeoning damage becomes immunity to nonmagical bludgeoning damage. As a bonus action you may curl and roll up to your speed in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks.
- **Zora:** Your fin-blade throw has a range of 60/120 and you may throw it twice as part of the same Attack action. You can breathe water, and your swim speed equals your walking speed plus 20 feet.
- **Rito:** Your flying speed increases by 10 feet, and the extra damage from your technique becomes 2d6.
- **Sheikah:** While hidden you are also invisible, until you attack or move within 5 feet of a creature that can see you. The extra damage from your technique becomes twice your proficiency bonus.
- **Twili:** Your resistance to necrotic damage becomes immunity. Once per turn you may teleport up to 15 feet as part of your movement, provided you begin or end that movement in dim light or darkness.
- **Gerudo:** Your resistance to fire damage becomes immunity. The speed reduction from your technique becomes 20 feet and lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
- **Hylian:** Your bonus to saving throws becomes +2, and you may use the reroll once per short rest rather than once per long rest.

#### 13th Level: Instinctive Guard
At 13th level, when you are hit by an attack, you may use your reaction and spend **1 SP** to reduce the damage by an amount equal to **1d10 + your Dexterity modifier**.

#### 15th Level: Avatar of Termina
At 15th level:
- You gain a **+2 bonus to AC** while transformed
- You are immune to exhaustion caused by forced movement or transformations

#### 17th Level: Legendary Masks
At 17th level, your Signature Techniques reach their fullest expression. Your Mask save DC increases by 2, and the technique of the mask you are wearing gains the effect below.

- **Deku:** The push affects every creature in a 15-foot cone rather than one creature within 5 feet.
- **Goron:** Creatures you pass through with your Dash take 3d6 bludgeoning damage in addition to making the save against being knocked prone.
- **Zora:** A creature hit by the fin-blade has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
- **Rito:** You may make the airborne attack as a bonus action once on each of your turns.
- **Sheikah:** The extra damage applies to any creature that has not yet taken a turn this round, not only in the first round of combat.
- **Twili:** The advantage you gain applies to every attack and saving throw you make until the end of your turn.
- **Gerudo:** The unarmed strike also deals 2d6 fire damage.
- **Hylian:** The reroll may be used on a failed saving throw or ability check as well as a missed attack.

#### 20th Level: Fierce Deity Ascension
At 20th level, you embody the perfected Wanderer:

- You may change masks as a **bonus action**
- You have advantage on **all saving throws** while transformed
- Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 hit points, you instead drop to 1 HP and immediately transform into a mask of your choice

{{footnote Classes | Masked Wanderer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Wandering Disciplines

Masked Wanderers follow different philosophies in how they honor the memories within their masks. These disciplines shape instinct, movement, and survival rather than granting rigid techniques.

### Discipline of the Guardian
*You stand between danger and those who cannot.*

#### 3rd Level: Steadfast Presence
While transformed:
- You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws.
- When a creature within 5 feet of you is targeted by an attack, you may impose disadvantage on that attack roll.

You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 6th Level: Anchored Form
When you would be moved or knocked prone against your will, you may spend **1 SP** to negate the movement.

In addition, while transformed, you have advantage on checks and saves made to resist grapples, shoves, and forced movement.

#### 10th Level: Protective Shift
When an ally within 30 feet takes damage, you may use your reaction to immediately switch to a different mask and reduce the damage by **1d10 + your Wisdom modifier**.

This reaction costs **1 SP**.

#### 14th Level: Unyielding Avatar
While transformed:
- You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (choose when you transform).
- Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

#### 18th Level: Bastion of Memories
Once per long rest, when you or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 hit points, that creature instead drops to 1 hit point and gains temporary hit points equal to your Masked Wanderer level.

{{footnote Classes | Masked Wanderer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Discipline of the Skirmisher
*You survive by never being where the blow lands.*

#### 3rd Level: Fluid Motion
While transformed:
- Your movement speed increases by 10 feet.
- You may move through hostile creatures' spaces as if they were difficult terrain.

#### 6th Level: Opportunistic Strike
Once per turn, when you hit a creature after moving at least 10 feet, you deal an additional **1d8 damage**.

You may spend **1 SP** to add this damage even if you did not move this turn.

#### 10th Level: Evasive Shift
When a creature misses you with an attack, you may use your reaction to move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

If you spend **1 SP**, you may immediately make one unarmed strike against a creature you pass.

#### 14th Level: Uncatchable
While transformed:
- You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
- Difficult terrain does not slow your movement.

#### 18th Level: Dance of Masks
Once per long rest, for 1 minute:
- You may change masks once per turn without using an action.
- Your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
- The first attack you hit each round deals an additional **2d8 damage**.

\column

### Discipline of the Trickster
*Victory comes from confusion, not strength.*

#### 3rd Level: Misdirecting Presence
While transformed:
- You gain proficiency in Deception and Stealth.
- Creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you.

#### 6th Level: Masked Feint
When you take the Attack action, you may spend **1 SP** to force a creature you hit to make a Wisdom saving throw.

On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on its next attack roll and saving throw before the end of its next turn.

#### 10th Level: Confounding Shift
When you change masks, you may choose one creature within 15 feet.

That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be **blinded or frightened** (your choice) until the end of its next turn.

#### 14th Level: Unreliable Target
While transformed:
- Attack rolls against you have disadvantage if you moved at least 10 feet on your previous turn.
- Illusions you create or abilities that obscure you last one additional round.

#### 18th Level: Master of the Many Faces
Once per long rest, for 1 minute:
- Enemies have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
- When a creature misses you, you may immediately switch masks without using an action.
- You regain **1 SP** at the start of each of your turns.

{{footnote Classes | Masked Wanderer }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Ranger

*"The wild does not forgive hesitation. It rewards those who learn its patterns."*

Rangers are expert hunters, scouts, and survivalists who read the battlefield like a living map. They work by precision and preparation, and by finding a foe's weakness before the foe knows it has been found.

Where others see chaos in nature, Rangers see systems.

---

> ##### A Turn as a Ranger
> You mark a creature and learn where it is weak, then shoot it, then spend a Focus Point to make the shot do exactly the thing the weakness allows. Your magic is for reaching places and reading ground, not for damage.

## Class Features
As a Ranger, you gain the following class features.

---

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d10 per Ranger level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 10 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor, medium armor, shields  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
- **Tools:** Herbalism kit  
- **Saving Throws:** Strength, Dexterity  
- **Skills:** Choose three from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to equipment granted by your background:
- (a) a longbow and quiver of 20 arrows or (b) two martial weapons  
- (a) scale mail or (b) leather armor  
- (a) a shortsword or (b) any simple weapon  
- (a) explorer's pack or (b) dungeoneer's pack  
- Herbalism kit

| 19th | +6 | Ability Score Improvement                     | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| 20th | +6 | Living Hunt                                   | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |

{{footnote Classes | Ranger }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Core Features

#### Spellcasting
You gain the ability to cast spells using **Magic Points (MP)**.

- **Spellcasting Ability:** Wisdom  
- **Spell List:** Ranger spell list (utility-focused, exploration, control, enhancement)  
- MP costs and MP recovery are the same as for every other caster: see the **Magic System** chapter. Your MP returns on a long rest, and a cantrip costs 1 MP.
- **Spell Level Cap:** 5th level (no Overchanneling access).

Rangers are not dedicated casters. Their magic sharpens perception, mobility, and survival instead of replacing weapon combat.

#### Focus System
You gain **Focus Points (FP)** representing battlefield awareness, timing, and precision.

- Your maximum Focus Points is shown in the **Focus Points** column of the Ranger table. It is 3, and rises to 4 at 15th level with Perfect Focus.
- You start each combat encounter with your maximum Focus Points
- Focus Points reset at the start of each combat encounter
- You can spend Focus Points to enhance attacks, reactions, and special techniques
- You regain Focus Points through combat performance (see below)

#### Gaining Focus Points
You regain Focus Points in the following ways, up to your maximum:

- Once per turn, when you hit a creature you have marked or analyzed: **+1 FP**
- When you score a critical hit: **+1 FP**
- When a creature you damaged drops to 0 HP: **+1 FP**

#### 1st Level: Hunter's Insight
At 1st level, you can analyze a creature and identify exploitable weaknesses.

As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet. It becomes **Marked** for 1 minute.

While marked, you learn one of the following (DM's choice or revealed gradually):

- Lowest saving throw
- Highest saving throw
- Damage resistances
- Damage immunities
- One tactical weakness (environmental or behavioral)

Only one creature can be marked at a time.

\column

#### 2nd Level: Ranger Techniques
At 2nd level, you learn specialized combat techniques fueled by Focus Points.

You learn 3 techniques of your choice. You learn more at higher levels.

You can use only one technique per attack unless otherwise stated.

###### Pinning Shot (1 FP)
Make a ranged weapon attack. On hit, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or:

- Its speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn

###### Crippling Shot (1 FP)
On a hit:

- Target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until end of next turn
- If already slowed, it instead becomes restrained until end of next turn

###### Disarming Shot (1 FP)
On hit:

- Target must make a Strength saving throw or drop one held item

###### Precise Strike (1 FP)
When you make an attack roll:

- Gain advantage on that attack roll

###### Exploit Opening (2 FP)
After hitting a marked creature:

- Deal additional weapon damage equal to your Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus

###### Hunter's Burst (2 FP)
After hitting a creature:

- Make one additional weapon attack against the same target as part of the same action

#### 3rd Level: Ranger Paths
At 3rd Level you pick one of the four below Ranger Paths;

- **Beastmaster**
- **Shadow Scout**
- **Monster Slayer**
- **Elemental Archer**

{{footnote Classes | Ranger }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

#### 5th Level: Extra Attack
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

#### 6th Level: Improved Hunter's Insight
Your study of a quarry becomes faster and more complete.

- Marking a creature with **Hunter's Insight** now costs no action. You may do it as part of any attack you make, or as a free action on your turn.
- You learn **two** of the listed facts about a marked creature instead of one.
- You may have **two** creatures marked at once. Features that trigger against a marked creature work against either.
- If a marked creature drops to 0 hit points, you may immediately mark a new creature you can see within 60 feet.

#### 9th Level: Survival Instinct
Your awareness makes you nearly impossible to catch off guard.

- You cannot be surprised while conscious
- You gain advantage on initiative rolls
- Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement

#### 10th Level: Marked Precision
When you attack a marked creature:

- You ignore half cover and three-quarters cover
- You add +1d6 damage once per turn to the first hit against a marked target

#### 11th Level: Relentless Focus
Your Focus Points become more efficient in combat.

- When you spend a Focus Point, you may roll a d6
- On a 5–6, that Focus Point is not expended

#### 13th Level: Master Tracker
You can track and predict movement with near-supernatural accuracy.

- You always know the direction of a marked creature as long as it is on the same plane
- You have advantage on checks to track or locate creatures

#### 15th Level: Perfect Focus
Your precision reaches its peak.

- Your maximum Focus Points becomes **4 instead of 3**
- When you start combat, you begin with maximum Focus Points

#### 17th Level: Apex Hunter
When you hit a marked creature:

- You may spend 1 Focus Point to force it to reroll a saving throw it just made

#### 18th Level: Unerring Strike
Your attacks rarely miss their mark.

- Once per turn, if you miss an attack roll, you may add +10 to the roll, potentially turning it into a hit


#### 20th Level: Living Hunt
You become the embodiment of the hunt itself.

- You always have advantage on attack rolls against marked creatures
- When a marked creature drops to 0 HP, you immediately regain 2 Focus Points (ignoring the cap)
- Once per turn, you may make one weapon attack as a bonus action without spending resources

{{footnote Classes | Ranger }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Beastmaster

Beastmasters fight alongside a bonded spirit companion, a manifestation of wilderness instinct rather than a permanent physical animal.

#### 3rd Level: Spectral Companion
You summon a spirit companion as a bonus action.

- The companion is a spectral beast (wolf, hawk, serpent, bear, etc.)
- It acts on your initiative
- It uses your proficiency bonus and scales with Ranger level
- It does not require tracking or feeding

You may change its form during a long rest.

#### 7th Level: Coordinated Hunt
When your companion hits a creature:

- You gain 1 Focus Point (once per turn)
- You may use your reaction to make one weapon attack against that creature

#### 11th Level: Shared Instinct
You and your companion act as one hunting unit.

- While within 30 feet of your companion:
  - You both gain advantage on Perception and Stealth checks
  - Your Focus Point gain triggers also apply to your companion's hits

#### 14th Level: Predator's Bond
Your companion becomes more resilient.

- It gains resistance to all damage while within 30 feet of you
- When it drops to 0 HP, it disappears instead of dying and can be resummoned after a short rest

#### 18th Level: Twofold Kill
When you hit a creature:

- Your companion may immediately make one attack against the same target (no action required)

\column

### Path of the Shadow Scout

Shadow Scouts specialize in infiltration, ambush, and eliminating targets before combat truly begins.

#### 3rd Level: Veil Walker
You gain the ability to move unseen.

- You can take the Hide action as a bonus action
- You gain darkvision (if you already have it, its range increases by 30 feet)
- While hidden, your first attack against a creature has advantage

#### 7th Level: Silent Execution
When you hit a surprised or unseen creature:

- Add extra damage equal to your Ranger level
- You regain 1 Focus Point (once per turn)

#### 11th Level: Phantom Step
You may teleport short distances.

- As a bonus action, you may teleport up to 30 feet to a space you can see
- If you end adjacent to a marked creature, your next attack has advantage

#### 14th Level: Deathmark
When you mark a creature:

- It cannot benefit from invisibility against you
- It cannot take reactions against you

#### 18th Level: One With the Shadow
You become nearly untouchable in darkness.

- You can become invisible in dim light or darkness as a bonus action
- While invisible, attacks against you have disadvantage

{{footnote Classes | Ranger }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Monster Slayer

Monster Slayers specialize in exploiting weaknesses and dismantling powerful foes.

#### 3rd Level: Weak Point Analysis
When you mark a creature:

- You learn its lowest saving throw
- Your attacks against it ignore resistance to one damage type of your choice

#### 7th Level: Exploit Weakness
When you hit a marked creature:

- You may spend 1 Focus Point to impose disadvantage on its next saving throw

#### 11th Level: Hunter's Edge
When a marked creature fails a saving throw:

- It takes additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus

#### 14th Level: Execution Window
When a creature is below half HP:

- Your attacks against it score critical hits on a 19–20

#### 18th Level: No Escape
Marked creatures cannot:

- Become invisible against you
- Teleport away from you unless they succeed on a Charisma saving throw

\column

### Path of the Elemental Archer

Elemental Archers infuse their shots with primal elemental force.

#### 3rd Level: Elemental Arrows
You can change your damage type when you attack:

- Fire, Cold, Lightning, Thunder, or Poison
- Once per turn, change damage type without cost

#### 7th Level: Elemental Reaction
When you hit a creature with elemental damage:

- You may apply a secondary effect based on element pairing:
  - Fire + Cold = Stun (1 turn)
  - Lightning + Water/Cold = Paralysis (1 turn)
  - Poison + Fire = Burst damage

#### 11th Level: Arc Shot
Your arrows can arc to additional targets.

- When you hit, you may target a second creature within 10 feet for half damage

#### 14th Level: Elemental Overload
Once per short rest:

- All attacks deal max damage dice for 1 minute

#### 18th Level: Avatar of the Hunt
You embody elemental mastery.

- Your attacks ignore resistance to elemental damage
- Once per turn, you may apply two elemental effects on a single hit

{{footnote Classes | Ranger }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Ranger Spell List

The Ranger draws from a focused well of survival, exploration, and battlefield-control magic. The Adventurer's Ranger path is a generalist dabbling in the same tradition. A dedicated Ranger has spent years on their connection to the wild and their precision in a fight, and their spell list is a deeper version of the same foundation. Ranger magic is never the centerpiece of a fight. It sharpens perception, mobility, and survival, and leaves weapon combat and the Focus and Technique system as the Ranger's primary tools.

**Spellcasting Ability:** Wisdom
**Spell Level Cap:** 5th level (no Overchanneling access).

# Sage
*"The ancient powers of Hyrule flow through us. We are the keepers of sacred knowledge and the weavers of elemental fate."*
:::::

> ##### A Turn as a Sage
> You cast, and the battlefield is different afterward. You have the largest Magic Point pool in the book and no list of prepared spells, so your turn is a choice from everything your affinity can reach, tempered by how much magic you have already spent this fight.

## Class Features
As a Sage, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d6 per Sage level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 6 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier  

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** None  
- **Weapons:** Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, light crossbows  
- **Tools:** Calligrapher's supplies  
- **Saving Throws:** Intelligence, Wisdom  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Religion  

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:
- (a) a quarterstaff or (b) a dagger  
- (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus (medallion)  
- (a) calligrapher's supplies or (b) ancient scrolls  
- Fine robes and a ceremonial sage mask

### Core Features

#### 1st Level: Elemental Affinity
At 1st level, choose one elemental affinity: **Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Spirit, or Light**.

You gain:
- Resistance to the affinity's damage type  
- Two affinity spells added to your class spell list  
- **Elemental Shift:** Once per turn, when you cast a spell that deals damage, you may change its damage type to your affinity  

#### 1st Level: Invoke Blessings (1 MP)
As a bonus action, choose one:
- **Elemental Surge:** Add 1d4 to the damage of your next spell  
- **Guided Casting:** Reroll one spell attack roll  
- **Soothing Aura:** Allies within 10 feet gain 1d4 temporary hit points  

#### 1st Level: Sage Insight
You have advantage on Arcana and History checks related to ancient magic, ruins, or divine artifacts.

#### 5th Level: Empowered Blessings
Starting at 5th level, Invoke Blessings can affect **two creatures** instead of one.

#### 7th Level: Dual Affinity
At 7th level, choose a second affinity.
- You gain its bonus spells
- You may combine affinities narratively (fire + wind = lightning, etc.)

#### 9th Level: Triforce Resonance
At 9th level, once per long rest, choose one:
- **Power:** +CHA or INT modifier to spell damage for 1 minute  
- **Wisdom:** Regain MP equal to your proficiency bonus  
- **Courage:** Automatically succeed on one saving throw  

#### 11th Level: Master of Elements
At 11th level:
- Your spells ignore resistance to your affinity damage types  
- Elemental Shift applies to **all** spells you cast  

#### 13th Level: Arcane Apotheosis
At 13th level, you may concentrate on one additional **affinity-based spell** that targets only enemies.

#### 15th Level: Elemental Mastery
At 15th level, when you cast an affinity spell, you may reduce its MP cost by 1 (minimum 1).

\column

#### 17th Level: Sage's Transcendence
At 17th level:
- You may cast 1st-level affinity spells at will (no MP)
- When you roll initiative, regain 1 MP

#### 20th Level: Avatar of the Sages
At 20th level, you embody the ancient Sages:
- Gain a permanent elemental movement feature based on your primary affinity  
- Once per long rest, for 1 minute:
  - All affinity spells cost 1 less MP  
  - You gain advantage on spell attack rolls and saving throws

## Oracle Paths

### Oracle of Ages
*Masters of raw elemental devastation.*

#### 3rd Level: Temporal Overchannel
When you cast a damaging spell, you may add your proficiency bonus to one damage roll.

#### 6th Level: Accelerated Casting
Once per turn, when you cast a spell, you may deal half damage to a second creature within 10 feet of the original target.

#### 10th Level: Relentless Power
When you roll damage dice for a spell, you may reroll one die and take the new result.

#### 14th Level: Apex Destruction
Your affinity spells score critical hits on a 19–20.

#### 18th Level: Cataclysm
Once per long rest, maximize the damage of one affinity spell.

---

### Oracle of Seasons
*Controllers of terrain, weather, and flow.*

#### 3rd Level: Seasonal Shift
When you cast an affinity spell, you may create difficult terrain in a 10-ft radius.

#### 6th Level: Elemental Control
Creatures that fail saves against your spells have their speed reduced by 10 feet until your next turn.

#### 10th Level: Environmental Mastery
You are immune to difficult terrain created by your spells, and allies ignore it.

#### 14th Level: Dominant Climate
Once per long rest, create a 30-ft zone for 1 minute that imposes disadvantage on enemy saves against your spells.

#### 18th Level: World in Balance
Enemies in your affected terrain have disadvantage on concentration checks.

::::::::::::::::

### Oracle of Secrets
*Keepers of hidden knowledge and divine guidance.*

#### 3rd Level: Veiled Casting
When you cast a spell on an ally, they gain advantage on their next saving throw.

#### 6th Level: Shared Insight
Allies affected by your spells gain temporary HP equal to your spellcasting modifier.

#### 10th Level: Hidden Paths
When an ally fails a save, you may spend 1 MP to allow them to reroll it.

#### 14th Level: Divine Intercession
Once per long rest, cast a spell of 5th level or lower without expending MP.

#### 18th Level: Chorus of the Sages
Allies within 30 feet gain advantage on saves while you maintain concentration.

# Shaman
*A conduit between the mortal world and the primal forces that shape it.*

Shamans do not study magic.  
They bargain with it.

Through whispered pacts with elemental spirits, a Shaman shapes flame, bends frost, commands storm, and calls the earth to answer. Their power is deliberate rather than explosive. Each spell leaves a trace, and each trace can be exploited.

Where others cast and forget, the Shaman layers and reacts.

> ##### A Turn as a Shaman
> You put an Elemental Mark on something, then put a second Mark on it, and the two elements meeting is the actual attack. Frost into Flame, Storm into Root. Your turn is a setup and a payoff, and from 13th level you can pay for both payoffs at once.

## Class Features

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Shaman level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per Shaman level after 1st  

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor, shields  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, quarterstaff  
- **Tools:** Herbalism kit  
- **Saving Throws:** Wisdom, Constitution  
- **Skills:** Choose two from Arcana, Nature, Insight, Survival, Medicine, Perception  

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- Leather armor and a shield  
- A quarterstaff or any simple weapon  
- An explorer's pack  
- An herbalism kit

### Magic Points (MP)

You use **Magic Points (MP)** to cast Shaman spells.

- You regain all MP on a long rest.
- **Exception to the general rule:** you also regain half your MP (rounded up) on a short rest. Every other caster in this book recovers MP only on a long rest. The Shaman draws from the elements around them rather than from a personal reserve, so their magic returns faster, and their spell list is built for sustained pressure rather than burst.
- You cannot exceed your maximum MP.
- Your spellcasting ability is **Wisdom**.
- **Spell Level Cap:** 6th level (Overchanneling required for spells above 5th level).
