#### 1st Level: Elemental Channeling

When you cast a Shaman spell that deals elemental damage (fire, cold, lightning, thunder, or nature/poison), you may apply an **Elemental Mark** to one creature damaged by the spell.

A creature may only have **one Mark at a time** (until level 11).

Marks last until the end of your next turn.

Once per turn, you may add your Wisdom modifier to elemental damage dealt by a Shaman spell.

#### 1st Level: Elemental Marks

- **Flame Mark**
Target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of its turn.

- **Frost Mark**
Target's speed is reduced by 10 feet.

- **Storm Mark**
Target has disadvantage on its next attack roll.

- **Root Mark**
Target must succeed on a Strength save or its speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.

### Elemental Reactions

If you apply a Mark to a creature that already has a Mark you applied, trigger an **Elemental Reaction** instead.

- The previous Mark is removed.
- The reaction occurs.
- No new Mark is applied.
- A creature can only trigger one Elemental Reaction per turn. This is not the ordinary D&D reaction and does not use one.

### Opposing Elements

{{classTable
| Existing Mark | New Mark | Reaction |
|---------------|----------|----------|
| Flame | Frost | Remove Flame. Target is **Stunned** until end of its next turn (1/combat per creature). |
| Frost | Flame | Remove Frost. Target takes bonus fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus. |
| Storm | Root | Target is knocked **Prone**. |
| Root | Storm | Target is lifted 10 feet and falls, taking 1d6 damage. |
}}

### Synergistic Extensions

{{classTable
| Existing Mark | New Mark | Reaction |
|---------------|----------|----------|
| Flame | Storm | Burning increases to 1d6 and lasts 1 extra round. |
| Flame | Root | Target becomes **Restrained** until end of its next turn. |
| Frost | Root | Target becomes **Restrained** (ice binds). |
| Frost | Storm | Target's speed is halved and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves until end of next turn. |
| Root | Flame | Target takes bonus damage and must succeed on STR save or fall prone. |
| Storm | Flame | Target has disadvantage on its next saving throw against your spells. |
}}

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

#### 2nd Level: Elemental Ward

When you take damage, you may use your reaction and spend 1 MP to reduce the damage by:

**1d10 + your Wisdom modifier**

If the attacker has one of your Marks, you may immediately trigger a valid Elemental Reaction without spending additional MP.

#### 3rd Level: Shaman Path

Choose a path that defines your bond with the elements:

- Path of the Flamecaller  
- Path of the Worldshaper  
- Path of the Stormspeaker  
- Path of the Frostbinder

#### 5th Level: Elemental Flow

When you trigger an Elemental Reaction, you regain 1 MP.

You may only regain MP this way once per turn.

#### 7th Level: Spirit Drift

As a bonus action, spend 2 MP to become semi-ethereal for 1 round:

- Resistance to non-magical weapon damage  
- You may move through creatures  
- Your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks  

#### 9th Level: Elemental Attunement
The elements begin to answer before you call them.

- Your Marks last until the end of your **second** turn after you apply them, rather than the end of your next turn.
- When you cast a Shaman spell that damages more than one creature, you may apply your Mark to **two** creatures damaged by it instead of one.
- You have resistance to the damage type of the Mark you most recently applied, until you apply a Mark of a different type.

#### 11th Level: Dual Mark

You may maintain **two Marks** on a creature at the same time.

If you would apply a third Mark, you choose which existing Mark ends.

#### 13th Level: Twinned Reaction
You can set two elements against each other at once.

- When you trigger an Elemental Reaction against a creature carrying two of your Marks (see **Dual Mark**), you may spend **2 MP** to immediately trigger a second valid Elemental Reaction against that creature using its remaining Mark.
- This is the one exception to the rule that a creature can only trigger one Elemental Reaction per turn. A creature still cannot be affected by the *same* Elemental Reaction twice in a turn.
- **Elemental Flow** refunds MP for only one Elemental Reaction per turn, as normal, so the second one always costs you 2 MP net.

#### 15th Level: Elemental Cascade

When you trigger an Elemental Reaction, you may apply one of the involved Marks to a different creature within 15 feet.

#### 17th Level: Elemental Sovereignty
The four elements no longer resist your hand.

- Creatures have **disadvantage** on saving throws against your Elemental Reactions.
- Your Marks ignore resistance to their damage type. A creature immune to that damage type still takes none, but still suffers the Mark's other effects.
- Once per long rest, when you would apply a Mark, you may instead apply **all four Marks** to that creature at once. It suffers all four. At the start of its next turn, every valid Elemental Reaction between them triggers, in an order you choose, without spending MP and without the once-per-turn limit.

#### 20th Level: Avatar of the Elements

Once per long rest, as an action, you embody elemental harmony for 1 minute:

- Marks last 2 rounds.
- You may trigger one Elemental Reaction per creature per turn.
- At the start of your turn, if at least one creature has your Mark, regain 1 MP.

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Shaman Paths

At 3rd level, you choose a path that defines how you channel elemental spirits and wield the Mark system in combat. Your path grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

All four paths work with any combination of Elemental Marks. Your path defines *how* you fight, not which element you reach for.

### Path of the Flamecaller

*The fire does not wait. Neither do you.*

Flamecallers are the most aggressive Shamans: high-risk, high-reward casters who accelerate the Mark system into rapid detonations. Where other Shamans build layered pressure, a Flamecaller turns every reaction into an explosion and every explosion into the next opening. They are the first into the fray and they hit like a thunderclap.

#### 3rd Level: Detonation

When you trigger an Elemental Reaction, you may add your Wisdom modifier to the reaction's damage (if it deals damage) or increase a condition's duration by 1 round (if it does not).

In addition, once per turn when you apply a Mark, you may spend 1 MP to **Ignite** the Mark, so that it takes effect at the start of the target's *current* turn rather than the next.

#### 6th Level: Chain Detonation

When you trigger an Elemental Reaction, you may immediately apply a new Mark of any type to the same target (no spell required, no action cost).

This Mark lasts until the end of your next turn and can trigger a second Reaction if conditions are met. This second Reaction cannot trigger a third.

#### 10th Level: Reactive Surge

When you score a critical hit with a Shaman spell, you immediately trigger a free Elemental Reaction on the target as if it had been double-marked, choosing any valid Reaction from the tables. No Mark is consumed or applied.

You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 14th Level: Living Pyre

You become a conduit for raw elemental discharge. As a bonus action, you enter a **Pyre State** for 1 minute (usable once per short rest):

- When you apply a Mark, the target takes bonus fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
- The first Reaction you trigger each round deals maximum damage dice.
- If you trigger two or more Reactions on the same turn, you regain 1 MP for each Reaction after the first.

#### 18th Level: Inferno Ascendant

Once per long rest, as an action, you call a pillar of elemental fire down upon a point you can see within 60 feet.

Each creature within a 20-foot radius must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 10d8 fire damage and receives all four Elemental Marks simultaneously. On a successful save, it takes half damage and receives one Mark of your choice.

Reactions triggered by any of these Marks occur immediately at the start of the affected creature's next turn, in an order of your choice.

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Stormspeaker

*You don't destroy your enemies. You make them destroy themselves.*

Stormspeakers are the tacticians of the Shaman paths: masters of control, misdirection, and cascading debuffs. They use Marks to unravel what makes an enemy effective, one piece at a time, until the target has no speed, no accuracy, and no turn worth taking. By the time a Stormspeaker is done, their opponents are stumbling through a fog of their own making.

#### 3rd Level: Stormweave

When you apply a Mark to a creature, you may choose to **weave** a secondary effect into it at no additional cost. Choose one:

- **Howling Mark:** The target has disadvantage on Perception checks until the Mark ends.
- **Rattling Mark:** The target cannot take reactions until the Mark ends.
- **Gusting Mark:** The target's movement speed is reduced by 5 feet until the Mark ends (in addition to any other Mark effects).

You may use Stormweave a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 6th Level: Eye of the Storm

When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells or Marks, you may spend 1 MP to impose one of the following until the start of your next turn:

- It cannot move toward you willingly.
- It must spend its action on its next turn repeating the failed save or doing nothing (Wisdom save negates, DC equals your spell save DC).
- It has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes.

You choose the effect after seeing the failed save.



#### 10th Level: Pressure System

When you maintain concentration on a Shaman spell, hostile creatures that start their turn within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals your spell save DC). On a failure, they cannot take reactions until the start of their next turn.

This effect does not require an action. It is an aura that persists as long as you concentrate.

#### 14th Level: Stormcaller's Dominion

As a bonus action, you may spend 2 MP to unleash a wave of disrupting force. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet that has one of your Marks must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure:

- All Marks on that creature are simultaneously triggered as if a Reaction had occurred for each (resolve opposing-element Reactions first, then synergistic ones).
- The creature is stunned until the end of its next turn.
- You regain 1 MP for each creature that fails.

On a success, the target's Marks are removed with no Reaction.

#### 18th Level: The Storm Speaks

Once per long rest, as an action, you channel the storm's voice directly. For 1 minute:

- All creatures of your choice within 60 feet that you can see must make a Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of their turns. On a failure, they are incapacitated until the start of their next turn.
- When a creature within 60 feet triggers one of your Elemental Reactions, all other marked creatures within 30 feet of the triggering creature take psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.
- Your Marks can no longer be removed by effects that normally dispel conditions. They can only be removed by triggering a Reaction.

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Worldshaper

*The land remembers. You only remind it.*

Worldshapers are the heart of the Shaman tradition: nature-bonded mediums who channel the deep, patient power of root and soil. They favor the Root Mark above all others, but their real strength is in reshaping the battlefield. They raise barriers, coax growth, and heal allies through the same channels they turn against enemies.

#### 3rd Level: Root Communion

Your bond with the Root Mark deepens. When you apply a Root Mark, choose one additional effect:

- The ground in a 5-foot radius around the target becomes difficult terrain until the end of your next turn (vines, roots, or earth rising underfoot).
- An ally of your choice within 30 feet regains hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier.
- The target is outlined in faint bioluminescent growth. It cannot benefit from invisibility or half-cover until the Mark ends.

In addition, while you are on natural ground (earth, stone, grass or sand, but not constructed floors), your Root Marks last until the end of your turn *after* your next, instead of until the end of your next turn.

#### 6th Level: Living Terrain

As a bonus action, you may spend 2 MP to shape a 10-foot square of terrain you can see within 60 feet. Choose one:

- **Undergrowth:** The area becomes difficult terrain for hostile creatures until the end of your next turn. Allies are unaffected.
- **Root Barrier:** A 5-foot-tall wall of woven roots rises along one edge of the square. The wall has AC 12 and 20 HP. It lasts for 1 minute or until destroyed.
- **Fertile Ground:** Any creature that starts its turn in the area regains hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. Lasts until the end of your next turn.

You may use Living Terrain a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 10th Level: Verdant Flow

When you trigger an Elemental Reaction involving a Root Mark, you may choose one allied creature within 30 feet to gain one of the following until the start of your next turn:

- Resistance to one damage type of your choice.
- Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.
- A climbing speed equal to their walking speed and the ability to move through difficult terrain without cost.

You may only grant each option once per round, but different allies may receive different options.

#### 14th Level: Spirit of the Grove

You may call upon the deep spirits of the land. As an action, spend 3 MP to summon a **Grove Guardian**, a massive elemental construct of root, stone, and living wood, in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. The Guardian uses your spell save DC and spell attack bonus, and acts on your initiative. It lasts for 1 minute or until reduced to 0 hit points.

**Grove Guardian:**
- AC 15, HP equal to 3 × your Shaman level
- Speed 30 ft.
- **Slam:** Melee weapon attack, +your Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus to hit, reach 5 ft. On hit: 2d8 + your Wisdom modifier bludgeoning damage, and the target gains a Root Mark.
- **Barrier Stance (Reaction):** When an ally within 5 feet of the Guardian takes damage, the Guardian may interpose, reducing the damage by 1d10 + your Wisdom modifier.

You may have only one Grove Guardian active at a time.

#### 18th Level: World Root

Once per long rest, as an action, you plant your staff or hand into the ground and speak to the deep root. For 1 minute:

- A 60-foot radius around you becomes **living terrain**. It shifts, rises, and responds to you. You may reshape the terrain within this radius as a bonus action each turn (raising walls, creating difficult terrain, opening pits; the DM adjudicates structural limits).
- All Root Marks you apply during this time also count as Flame Marks (you may trigger Synergistic Reactions using either).
- At the start of each of your turns, you may choose up to three allies within the radius. Each regains hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier.
- When a creature within the radius triggers a Reaction involving a Root Mark, the Reaction's effect spreads to all other Root-Marked creatures within 15 feet of the original target.

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Frostbinder

*It does not need to kill you. It only needs to make sure you never move again.*

Frostbinders are the patient predators of the Shaman paths: methodical, cold, and relentless. They do not burst. They accumulate. They layer Frost Marks, slow everything around them to a crawl, and pick apart enemies who can no longer get away. Against a Frostbinder the only strategy is not to be caught, and once you have been caught it is already over.

#### 3rd Level: Permafrost

When you apply a Frost Mark to a creature, it must immediately make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, its speed is reduced by an additional 10 feet until the Mark ends (stacking with the Mark's base 10-foot reduction, for a total of −20 feet).

In addition, when you trigger a Reaction that removes a Frost Mark, the target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, even after the Mark is gone. The cold lingers.

#### 6th Level: Glacial Shell

You learn to encapsulate yourself or an ally in reactive frost. As a reaction when you or an ally within 30 feet takes damage, spend 1 MP to form a glacial shell around them:

- Reduce the triggering damage by 1d10 + your Wisdom modifier.
- The shell lasts until the start of your next turn. While it lasts, any creature that hits the shelled target with a melee attack takes cold damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
- If the target is already Frost-Marked when you activate this, the shell's duration extends to the end of your next turn instead.

#### 10th Level: Absolute Zero

When you reduce a creature's speed to 0 through any combination of Frost Mark effects, it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is **Restrained** until the end of its next turn. If it was already Restrained, it is instead **Paralyzed** until the end of its next turn.

A creature cannot be Paralyzed by this feature more than once per combat.

#### 14th Level: Encasing Cold

As a bonus action, spend 2 MP to extend your frost through the battlefield. Choose up to three creatures you can see within 60 feet that are Frost-Marked. Each must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

On a failure: The creature takes 4d8 cold damage, its speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn, and if it was already at 0 speed, it is instead Incapacitated until the start of your next turn.

On a success: The creature takes half damage and its Frost Mark is removed.

This feature may be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

#### 18th Level: The Long Winter

Once per long rest, as an action, you call upon the oldest cold. For 1 minute:

- All creatures of your choice within 60 feet automatically receive a Frost Mark at the start of their turn if they do not already have one. This costs no MP and requires no action.
- Your Frost Marks stack. A single creature can carry up to two Frost Marks simultaneously, each applying their −10 ft. speed reduction separately (maximum −20 ft. total from Marks alone).
- When a creature within 60 feet fails a saving throw against any of your spells or features, it cannot regain movement speed by any means until the start of its next turn.
- When a creature within 60 feet drops to 0 hit points, you may immediately apply a Frost Mark to any other creature within 15 feet of it at no cost.

{{footnote Classes | Shaman }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Shaman Spell List

The Shaman channels the voice of the spirit world: ancestral memory, elemental temperament, and the quiet intelligence of wind, root, flame, and frost. While the Shaman's Elemental Mark and Reaction system carries most of their combat identity, their spellcasting is broader than pure damage: a Shaman speaks with spirits, reads omens, calls on nature's protection, and channels the elements as readily for healing and guidance as for harm.

**Spellcasting Ability:** Wisdom

# Veilblade

*"The unseen hand guides the battlefield."*

Veilblades are masters of precision warfare: tacticians who dismantle their enemies with calculated strikes, crippling status effects, and no wasted motion.

Where others overwhelm with force, <br>
a Veilblade controls the flow of battle <br>
through timing, positioning, and execution.

They do not fight fair. <br>
They fight to win.

---

> ##### A Turn as a Veilblade
> You attack twice, land a Sneak Strike on the one that counts, and spend Energy on a Special Attack that leaves a condition behind. Next turn that condition makes everything you do land harder.

## Class Features
As a Veilblade, you gain the following class features.

### Hit Points
- **Hit Die:** 1d8 per Veilblade level  
- **Hit Points at 1st Level:** 8 + your Constitution modifier  
- **Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier  

---

### Proficiencies
- **Armor:** Light armor  
- **Weapons:** Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords  
- **Tools:** Thieves' tools  
- **Saving Throws:** Dexterity, Intelligence  
- **Skills:** Choose four from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, Survival  

---

### Starting Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to equipment granted by your background:

- (a) a rapier or (b) two shortswords  
- (a) leather armor or (b) studded leather armor  
- (a) a burglar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack  
- Thieves' tools and a hooded cloak

### Core Features

#### Sneak Strike
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a finesse weapon and have advantage on the attack roll, or when an ally is within 5 feet of the target, you deal extra damage.

This damage is shown in the Sneak Strike column of the Veilblade table. It rises by 1d6 every four levels, to a maximum of 5d6 at 17th.

> ##### Why the Veilblade Is Not a Rogue
> A Veilblade gains Extra Attack at 5th level, which a 5e Rogue never does. Sneak Strike is scaled to half a Rogue's progression to pay for it. The class's damage comes from three places at once (two attacks, one Sneak Strike, and a Special Attack) rather than from one enormous hit, and the Energy pool means the third of those is available every round.

#### 1st Level: Tactical Precision
At 1st level, choose Intelligence or Charisma.  
This becomes your **Tactician modifier** for your Veilblade features.

Your Special Attack save DC equals:

**8 + proficiency bonus + your Tactician modifier**

#### 2nd Level: Energy Pool
You fuel your techniques through disciplined combat flow.

- You have a maximum number of Energy points shown in the class table.
- You begin every combat with full Energy.
- You regain **1 Energy at the start of each of your turns in combat.**
- You regain all Energy at the end of a short or long rest, and whenever combat ends.
- You cannot exceed your maximum Energy.

Energy is a combat resource. Outside of combat you are always assumed to be at your maximum, so there is nothing to track between fights.

#### 2nd Level: Special Attacks
You learn three Special Attacks of your choice.

- Each Special Attack costs **1 Energy**.
- You may use only **one Special Attack per turn**, unless otherwise stated.
- Special Attacks require a weapon hit unless specified.
- You learn additional Special Attacks at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

#### 6th Level: Tactical Flow
When you make an attack against a creature suffering from a condition you inflicted:

- You have advantage on the attack roll.
- On a hit, add your Tactician modifier to the damage.

#### 9th Level: Relentless Pressure
You may use two Special Attacks on your turn, but they must target the same creature.

#### 13th Level: Exploit Weakness
When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Special Attacks, it has disadvantage on its next saving throw before the end of your next turn.


#### 17th Level: Master Execution
When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points:

- You regain 2 Energy.
- You may immediately apply a Special Attack to another creature within 30 feet without spending Energy.

#### 20th Level: Apex Predator
Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you enter a perfected state for 1 minute:

- You regain 2 Energy at the start of each turn.
- Special Attacks no longer require saving throws.
- You have advantage on attack rolls against creatures suffering a condition.

{{footnote Classes | Veilblade }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Veilblade Combo Reference

A Veilblade thrives on layered pressure.  
When you apply a Special Attack to a creature already suffering a condition you inflicted, consult the chart below.

Conditions only count if **you** applied them.


#### Condition Key

- **Slowed:** Speed reduced  
- **Bleeding:** Takes damage at start of turn  
- **Dazed:** Disadvantage on next attack  
- **Poisoned:** Disadvantage on attack rolls  

---

#### Combo Rules Clarification

- Only one combo upgrade may trigger per attack.
- Conditions do not stack unless stated.
- A creature cannot be stunned by Dazing Blow more than once per combat.
- Energy regained from combos cannot exceed your maximum Energy.

{{classTable,frame
#### Combo Condition Chart
| Applied Attack | If Target Already Has | Combo Result | Tactical Benefit |
|:----------------|:----------------------|:-------------|:------------------|
| **Crippling Strike** | Slowed | Target falls **Prone** (DEX save negates) | Gain advantage on your next melee attack |
| **Hemorrhage** | Bleeding | Increase bleed to 1d6 and extend 1 round | Regain 1 Energy |
| **Dazing Blow** | Dazed | Target becomes **Stunned** until end of its next turn (1/combat) | Add Tactician mod to damage |
| **Venom Cut** | Poisoned | Target has disadvantage on saving throws until end of its next turn | You gain advantage on next attack |
| **Shadow Feint** | Any Condition | Deal +1d6 additional damage | Does not count against 1/turn Special Attack limit |
| **Mark for Death** | Any Condition | Target's resistances are suppressed for 2 rounds | Regain 1 Energy (max once per turn) |
}}

\column

### Special Attacks

#### Crippling Strike
The target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

If the target is already slowed, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

#### Hemorrhage
The target takes 1d4 bleed damage at the start of its next turn.

If the target is already bleeding, increase the damage to 1d6 and extend the duration by 1 round.

Bleed does not stack beyond this increase.

#### Dazing Blow
The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll.

If the target is already dazed, it is stunned until the end of its next turn.  
A creature cannot be stunned this way more than once per combat.

#### Shadow Feint
You gain advantage on your next attack roll this turn.

If you were hidden when activating this ability, the attack deals an additional 1d6 damage.

#### Venom Cut
The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become poisoned until the end of its next turn.

If already poisoned, it has disadvantage on its next saving throw before the end of its next turn.

#### Mark for Death
Until the end of your next turn:

- You ignore the target's resistance to weapon damage.
- Allies add your proficiency bonus to damage against that target.

If the target is suffering from a status condition when you hit it, you regain 1 Energy (cannot exceed maximum).

{{footnote Classes | Veilblade }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Veilblade Rogue Paths

At 3rd level, you choose a Rogue Path that defines your approach to the hunt. Your path grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

None of the paths below add new Special Attacks to the Veilblade Combo Reference chart. All three work by enhancing how you apply, trigger, and capitalize on the existing six Special Attacks (Crippling Strike, Hemorrhage, Dazing Blow, Venom Cut, Shadow Feint, Mark for Death) and the conditions they create.

---

### Path of the Assassin

*One strike. One target. One certainty.*

The Assassin path is built for the opening move, the strike that ends a fight before it has properly begun. Where other Veilblades grind an enemy down through layered conditions, an Assassin wants the fight over in the first exchange. They are patient before combat and merciless the instant it starts.

#### 3rd Level: Killing Window

If you hit a creature with a weapon attack before it has taken a turn in combat (including a surprise round), your attack automatically triggers as a Sneak Strike, and any Special Attack applied as part of that hit deals maximum damage on its first instance of damage dice (this does not apply to ongoing damage from conditions like bleed).

In addition, you have advantage on initiative rolls.

#### 6th Level: Marked for the End

When you apply **Mark for Death** to a creature, you may immediately make one additional weapon attack against it as part of the same action, without expending an additional Special Attack or Energy. This bonus attack cannot itself apply a new Special Attack.

#### 10th Level: No Second Chances

When a creature you have hit with a Special Attack this combat is below half its hit point maximum, your Special Attack save DC against that creature increases by 2.

In addition, once per turn, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a weapon attack or Special Attack, you may immediately move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

#### 14th Level: Precision of the First Cut

Your first attack against a creature each combat ignores resistance to the damage type of your weapon, and if it hits, the target cannot regain hit points from any source until the end of its next turn.

#### 18th Level: The Inevitable Strike

Once per long rest, as an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet that is unaware of you or has not yet acted in the current combat. Make a single weapon attack against it with advantage. This attack:

- Automatically counts as a Sneak Strike, regardless of position or allies.
- May apply two Special Attacks simultaneously at no additional Energy cost (resolving any combo interactions in your chosen order).
- Deals maximum damage on all weapon and Special Attack damage dice.

If this attack reduces the target to 0 hit points, you regain all expended Energy.

{{footnote Classes | Veilblade }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Saboteur

*Poison does not need to be fast. It only needs to be thorough.*

Saboteurs are the patient corrupters: Veilblades who treat every condition they inflict as a thread in a larger snare. They favor Hemorrhage and Venom Cut above the rest of the combo chart, and they are happiest when an enemy is too busy failing saving throws to notice it's already lost.

#### 3rd Level: Lingering Toxin

Conditions you inflict through Special Attacks last 1 round longer than normal before requiring a new save or instance to maintain (where applicable). In addition, when a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your Special Attacks, it still suffers the condition's effects until the end of its current turn before the condition ends.

#### 6th Level: Compounding Affliction

The normal combo rule limiting one combo upgrade per attack does not apply to you. When you apply a Special Attack to a creature that already has two or more conditions you inflicted, you may trigger up to two combo results from the Combo Condition Chart on the same attack (you choose which two, in any order).

#### 10th Level: Septic Pressure

While a creature has two or more conditions you have inflicted active on it simultaneously, it has disadvantage on Constitution saving throws, and any bleed or poison damage it takes from your Special Attacks increases by your Tactician modifier.

#### 14th Level: Total Breakdown

When a creature under the effect of three or more of your conditions starts its turn, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Special Attack save DC or be poisoned and have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn, as its body fails under the compounded strain.

A creature can only be affected by Total Breakdown once per combat.

#### 18th Level: The Slow Collapse

Once per long rest, as a bonus action, choose one creature within 30 feet that you have inflicted at least one condition on this combat. For the next minute:

- Every condition you inflict on that creature lasts until the end of your next turn rather than its normal duration, and does not require maintenance to persist.
- At the start of each of the target's turns, it takes necrotic damage equal to the number of distinct conditions you have currently inflicted on it (minimum 1).
- If at any point the target is suffering from all four condition types you can inflict (Slowed, Bleeding, Dazed/Stunned, Poisoned) simultaneously, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw at the start of each of its turns or fall unconscious until the effect ends or it takes damage.

{{footnote Classes | Veilblade }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Path of the Shadowdancer

*By the time they realize where you are, you are already somewhere else.*

Shadowdancers trade raw damage for total battlefield control of their own position. They are the hardest Veilblades to pin down, slipping between shadows, striking from impossible angles, and vanishing before a counterattack can land. A Shadowdancer doesn't win fights through attrition or burst. They win by never being where the danger is.

#### 3rd Level: Step Between Shadows

As a bonus action, you may teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is in dim light or darkness. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest, regaining one use whenever you apply **Shadow Feint**.

#### 6th Level: Dancing Strike

When you use Shadow Feint, in addition to its normal effect, you may immediately use Step Between Shadows as part of the same bonus action at no additional cost (this does not expend a use of Step Between Shadows if you have none remaining; it instead requires you to wait until your next turn to use Shadow Feint this way again).

In addition, attacks of opportunity against you have disadvantage.

#### 10th Level: Untouchable Flow

When a creature misses you with an attack, you may use your reaction to immediately use Step Between Shadows, even if you have no light requirement met at your destination (you may teleport into an unlit space normally inaccessible to this feature).

You regain one use of Step Between Shadows whenever you start combat undetected by all enemies.

#### 14th Level: Where the Shadows Lead

You may use Step Between Shadows to teleport to any unoccupied space within 15 feet of any creature you can see, regardless of light conditions at the destination, as long as the creature itself is in dim light or darkness. In addition, when you arrive adjacent to a creature this way, your next attack against it this turn has advantage.

#### 18th Level: One With the Dark

Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you become one with shadow for 1 minute:

- You may use Step Between Shadows without expending a use, as many times per turn as you have movement available to justify (DM adjudicates reasonable frequency).
- While in dim light or darkness, you are invisible until you attack, cast a spell, or the effect ends.
- The first attack you make each turn while this feature is active automatically counts as a Sneak Strike and applies a Special Attack at no Energy cost.

{{footnote Classes | Veilblade }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Backgrounds

> *"Before the sword, before the call to adventure, there was a life. A trade. A home. A reason to wake up each morning that had nothing to do with saving the world. That life is still part of you."*
> — Viator Fortuitus, A Bard's Record

Your background represents what your character did before adventuring began: the skills you picked up, the people you knew, and the doors that are open to you because of where you came from. Every background grants two skill proficiencies, proficiency with tools or an additional language, a package of starting equipment, and a special feature that opens up roleplaying and story opportunities specific to your history.

This chapter presents thirteen classic backgrounds reimagined for Hyrule, followed by six backgrounds original to this setting. Work with your DM to decide which backgrounds fit your campaign. Not every background needs to appear in every story, and your DM may have specific factions or settings in mind that make certain backgrounds especially relevant (see the Hyrule Factions & NPCs chapter for ideas).

---

### Acolyte

You have spent your life in service to a temple of the Golden Goddesses: tending sacred springs, performing rites, and learning the old hymns passed down through generations of clergy. Whether you served Din, Nayru, Farore, or Hylia herself, you carry that devotion with you still.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Insight, Religion
**Languages:** Two of your choice
**Equipment:** A holy symbol (a gift from your temple), a prayer book or prayer wheel, 5 sticks of incense, vestments, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: Shelter of the Faithful

You and your companions can receive free healing and care at any temple, shrine, or sacred spring dedicated to the Golden Goddesses, though you may need to provide your own material components for spells. Those who share your faith offer you assistance (a place to stay, a meal, or guidance) at a modest lifestyle, free of charge.

---

### Charlatan

You've always had a gift for telling people exactly what they want to hear. Maybe you ran a fortune-telling stall in Castle Town's market, sold "authentic" Zonai relics to gullible travelers, or talked your way out of more trouble than you've talked your way into.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Deception, Sleight of Hand
**Tool Proficiencies:** Disguise kit, forgery kit
**Equipment:** A disguise kit, tools of the con of your choice (ten stoppered bottles filled with colored liquid, a set of weighted dice, a deck of marked cards, or a signet ring of an imaginary noble), a set of fine clothes, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: False Identity

You have created a second identity that includes documentation, established acquaintances, and disguises that allow you to assume that persona. In addition, you can forge documents, provided you have seen an example of the kind of document or the handwriting you are trying to copy.

---

### Criminal

You have a history of breaking the law, whether as a black-market smuggler running goods past Gerudo checkpoints, a tomb robber who's emptied one too many ancient ruins, or simply someone who's done what they had to do to survive.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Deception, Stealth
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of gaming set, thieves' tools
**Equipment:** A crowbar, a set of dark common clothes including a hood, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: Criminal Contact

You have a reliable and trustworthy contact who acts as your liaison to a network of other criminals. You know how to get messages to and from your contact, even over great distances. Specifically, you know the local messengers, corrupt caravan masters, and seedy taverns where messages can be left and found.

---

### Entertainer

You've made your living bringing joy to others: performing in Castle Town's plazas, traveling between Goron City and Kakariko Village as a wandering musician, or telling stories of legendary heroes to wide-eyed children in village squares.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Acrobatics, Performance
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of musical instrument or disguise kit
**Equipment:** A musical instrument of your choice, the favor of an admirer (love letter, lock of hair, or trinket), a costume, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: By Popular Demand

You can always find a place to perform (an inn, tavern, festival, or noble's court) and receive free lodging and modest meals in exchange for your nightly performance. In addition, your fame precedes you in some small way; common folk in the region may recognize your name or have heard tales of your talent.

{{footnote Backgrounds }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Folk Hero

You're known in your home village as the person who stood up when no one else would. Perhaps you faced down a Bokoblin warband, exposed a corrupt official, or simply did something everyone agreed needed doing and nobody else was brave enough to attempt.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Animal Handling, Survival
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of artisan's tools, vehicles (land)
**Equipment:** A set of artisan's tools (one of your choice), a shovel, an iron pot, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Rustic Hospitality

Since you come from the ranks of the common folk, you fit in among them with ease. You can find a place to hide, rest, or recuperate among other commoners unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them. They will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives for you.

---

### Guild Artisan

You belong to one of Hyrule's craft guilds (perhaps the Goron Smiths' Circle, the Hylian Weavers' Hall, or the Zonai Researchers' Compact), a formal organization that grants you status, training, and connections wherever its members are recognized.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Insight, Persuasion
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of artisan's tools
**Equipment:** A set of artisan's tools (one of your choice), a letter of introduction from your guild, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: Guild Membership

As an established member of your guild, you can rely on certain benefits. Your fellow guild members will provide you with lodging and food if necessary, and pay for your funeral if needed. In some regions, your guild has more formal political power: guild leaders may petition the Royal Court directly on guild business, and a guild membership marks you as a trustworthy tradesperson.

---

### Hermit

You spent a long period of your life in seclusion, whether in a mountain shrine, a remote part of the Lost Woods, or a forgotten ruin, for religious contemplation, scholarly study, or simply to escape a world that had become too much to bear.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Medicine, Religion
**Tool Proficiencies:** Herbalism kit
**Languages:** One of your choice
**Equipment:** A scroll case stuffed with notes from your studies or prayers, a winter blanket, a set of common clothes, an herbalism kit, and 5 rupees

#### Feature: Discovery

The quiet seclusion of your extended hermitage gave you access to a unique and powerful discovery. The exact nature of this revelation depends on the nature of your seclusion. It might be a great truth about Hyrule's deep history, a previously unknown relic location, or a fundamental truth about the nature of the Calamity. Work with your DM to determine the details.

---

### Noble

You were born to status: a minor noble house sworn to the Royal Family, perhaps, or a Gerudo chieftain's lineage, or a Zora family of old standing. You know how to move through court politics, even if you've left that world behind for the road.

**Skill Proficiencies:** History, Persuasion
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of gaming set
**Languages:** One of your choice
**Equipment:** A set of fine clothes, a signet ring, a scroll of pedigree, and a purse containing 25 rupees

#### Feature: Position of Privilege

People are inclined to think the best of you. You are welcome in high society, and people assume you have the right to be wherever you are. Common folk go out of their way to accommodate you and avoid your displeasure, and other nobles treat you as a member of the same social sphere, regardless of your actual station.

---

### Outlander

You grew up away from the safety of settled Hyrule: in the deep wilderness, the high mountains, or territory that civilization hasn't fully claimed. You learned to survive on terms the land set, not the other way around.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Athletics, Survival
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of musical instrument
**Languages:** One of your choice
**Equipment:** A staff, a hunting trap, a trophy from an animal you killed, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Wanderer

You have an excellent memory for maps and geography, and you can always recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other features around you. In addition, you can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day, provided the land offers berries, small game, water, and so forth.

{{footnote Backgrounds }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Sage

You have spent years in dedicated study: elemental lore, ancient Sheikah technology, the history of the Sacred Realm, or some other field of arcane and academic knowledge most people never encounter.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Arcana, History
**Languages:** Two of your choice
**Equipment:** A bottle of black or blue-black ink, a quill, a small knife, a letter from a deceased mentor posing a question you have not yet answered, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Researcher

When you attempt to learn or recall a piece of lore, if you do not know that information, you often know where and from whom you can obtain it. Usually, this information comes from a library, scriptorium, university, sage's archive, or a learned person or creature. Your DM might rule that the knowledge you seek is secreted away in some hard-to-reach location, or that it simply cannot be found.

---

### Sailor

You've spent years working the waters of Hyrule (the Lanayru Sea, the rivers that wind through Zora territory, or the coastal waters near the Faron region) as a deckhand, navigator, or member of a trading vessel's crew.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Athletics, Perception
**Tool Proficiencies:** Navigator's tools, vehicles (water)
**Equipment:** A belaying pin (club), 50 feet of silk rope, a lucky charm (such as a carved fishbone, a polished river stone, or a tattoo), a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Ship's Passage

When you need to, you can secure free passage on a sailing ship or river barge for yourself and your companions, in exchange for performing duties during the voyage. You might also be called upon to repay this generosity in some way if you later encounter the captain or crew who helped you.

\column

### Soldier

You served in an organized military force: the Hylian Royal Guard, a Gerudo warband, the Goron militia, or another formal fighting body. You learned discipline, tactics, and the particular camaraderie that comes from shared danger.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Athletics, Intimidation
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of gaming set, vehicles (land)
**Equipment:** An insignia of rank, a trophy taken from a defeated enemy (a dagger, broken blade, or piece of banner), a set of bone dice or deck of cards, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Military Rank

You have a military rank from your career as a soldier. Soldiers loyal to your former military organization still recognize your authority and influence, and they defer to you if they are of a lower rank. You can invoke your rank to exert influence over other soldiers and requisition simple equipment or horses for temporary use. You can also usually gain access to friendly military encampments and fortresses where your rank is recognized.

---

### Urchin

You grew up on the streets of a major settlement: Castle Town, Kakariko, or one of Hyrule's other large towns. You lived on quick wits, quicker hands, and whatever shelter you could find.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Sleight of Hand, Stealth
**Tool Proficiencies:** Disguise kit, thieves' tools
**Equipment:** A small knife, a map of the town you grew up in, a pet mouse, a token to remember your parents by, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: City Secrets

You know the secret patterns and flow of the settlement you grew up in and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you and companions you lead can travel between any two locations in that settlement twice as fast as your speed would normally allow.

{{footnote Backgrounds }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Hyrule-Original Backgrounds

The six backgrounds below are original to this setting, built to reflect roles and histories specific to life in Hyrule. They follow the same structure as the backgrounds above: two skill proficiencies, tool or language proficiencies, a starting equipment package, and a unique feature.

---

### Ranch Hand

You grew up working the land: tending cuccos, breaking in horses at a ranch like Lon Lon, or driving goats through mountain pastures below Death Mountain. The work was hard, the hours were long, and you learned to read animals and weather better than you ever learned to read people.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Animal Handling, Survival
**Tool Proficiencies:** Vehicles (land)
**Equipment:** A set of riding gear, a horse whistle or animal call, a coil of sturdy rope (50 feet), a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Steady Hand with Beasts

Animals trust you on sight. You have advantage on Animal Handling checks made to calm, befriend, or ride an unfamiliar creature of CR 2 or lower, and wild herd animals (horses, goats, cuccos, and similar creatures) will not flee from your approach unless directly threatened. In addition, you know how to recognize a good mount from a poor one. When purchasing or evaluating a horse or similar animal, you always learn its true temperament and any hidden flaws before committing to the deal.

**Suggested Characteristics**

*You can use the Folk Hero tables for Personality Trait, Ideal, Bond, and Flaw, or work with your DM to create options tied specifically to ranch life: a stubborn cucco you raised from a chick, a prize horse you trained yourself, or a ranch family who took you in when you had nowhere else to go.*

\column

### Shrine Keeper

You served as caretaker of a sacred shrine, Spirit Spring, or ancient temple: maintaining its grounds, performing the rites that keep its blessing active, and guiding pilgrims and travelers who came seeking the spring's gift. Whether your shrine was a grand temple or a single quiet spring deep in the forest, you know what it means to guard something sacred.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Insight, Religion
**Languages:** One of your choice
**Equipment:** A set of ceremonial robes, a small bell or chime used in your shrine's rites, a vial of water from your shrine (treat as holy water), a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 12 rupees

#### Feature: Keeper's Welcome

You know the proper rites and customs for nearly any shrine, sacred spring, or temple you encounter, even ones belonging to traditions other than your own. Other Shrine Keepers, priests, and temple staff recognize you as a fellow caretaker of sacred spaces. This grants you respectful welcome and basic hospitality (shelter, a meal, access to non-restricted areas) at any shrine or temple you visit, and you can communicate the urgency of a situation to temple staff in a way that travelers without this background cannot.



|**Suggested Characteristics**||
| d6 | Personality Trait |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | I speak slowly and deliberately, as though every word should be considered sacred. |
| 2 | I see omens and meaning in small, everyday occurrences. |
| 3 | I've grown so used to solitude that I find crowds and noise genuinely uncomfortable. |
| 4 | I treat every stranger with the same patient hospitality I once gave to pilgrims. |
| 5 | I quietly judge those who show no reverence for sacred places. |
| 6 | I've memorized hundreds of old prayers and find myself reciting them under stress. |

| d6 | Ideal |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | **Devotion.** My duty to the sacred spring outweighs my own comfort. (Lawful) |
| 2 | **Welcome.** No one should be turned away from a place of healing. (Good) |
| 3 | **Stillness.** The world moves too fast; sacred places remind us to slow down. (Neutral) |
| 4 | **Guardianship.** What I protect, I protect absolutely, even from those who claim good intentions. (Lawful) |
| 5 | **Renewal.** Everyone deserves a chance to start over, and my shrine offers that. (Good) |
| 6 | **Independence.** I left my shrine because I came to believe faith shouldn't require walls. (Chaotic) |

{{footnote Backgrounds }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Traveling Merchant

You made your living on the road: buying low in one region and selling high in another, hauling goods between Goron City, Zora's Domain, Gerudo Town, and everywhere in between. You know the roads, the rest stops, and which merchants in every town can be trusted.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Persuasion, Investigation
**Tool Proficiencies:** Navigator's tools, one type of gaming set
**Equipment:** A merchant's scale, a ledger book, a set of fine traveler's clothes, a locked strongbox (no key; you lost it years ago), and a pouch containing 20 rupees

#### Feature: Trade Network

You have established contacts among merchants in most major settlements across Hyrule. You can typically buy and sell goods at a fair price (your DM may grant a discount of 10–20% when purchasing common goods, at their discretion), and you always know where to find a legitimate buyer for unusual or hard-to-place items, even ones other merchants might be suspicious of. In addition, you can usually arrange safe passage for yourself and companions along established trade routes by traveling with or alongside a caravan.


|**Suggested Characteristics**||
| d6 | Personality Trait |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | I size up the value of everything I see, out of habit more than greed. |
| 2 | I have a story or a connection for almost every town in Hyrule. |
| 3 | I haggle reflexively, even when it isn't necessary or appropriate. |
| 4 | I'm an excellent judge of character. I had to be, to survive on the road. |
| 5 | I collect small, unusual trinkets from every place I visit. |
| 6 | I talk a great deal, filling silences that make me uncomfortable. |

| d6 | Bond |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | A rival merchant ruined my reputation in one town, and I mean to set the record straight. |
| 2 | My caravan was attacked by monsters years ago; I lost someone I loved that day. |
| 3 | An old trade partner in a distant region still owes me a debt I intend to collect. |
| 4 | I owe my start in trading to a mentor I haven't seen in years. |
| 5 | I'm searching for a rare item a client commissioned long ago and never paid for. |
| 6 | I left a family business behind, and I think about them every time I pass through a market. |

\column

### Monster Hunter

You've made a living tracking and eliminating dangerous creatures: Bokoblin camps threatening a village, a Lynel terrorizing mountain trade routes, or whatever else needed killing before it killed someone else first. It isn't glamorous work, but it's necessary, and you're good at it.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Survival, Nature
**Tool Proficiencies:** Herbalism kit
**Equipment:** A trophy from your most dangerous kill (a fang, a horn, a scale; DM's choice or your own), a set of traveler's clothes, a hunting knife, a vial of monster-repelling herbs, and a pouch containing 15 rupees

#### Feature: Bounty Board Reputation

You are a known and trusted name among those who post and pay out monster bounties: village elders, stable keepers, and regional authorities. You can reliably find paying monster-hunting work in nearly any settlement, and you have advantage on Charisma checks made to negotiate payment for a completed bounty. In addition, you have a working knowledge of monster behavior patterns; you always know the general danger level of a creature type before engaging it, even if you've never personally fought that specific monster before.

**Suggested Characteristics**

*You can use the Soldier or Outlander tables for Personality Trait, Ideal, Bond, and Flaw, or work with your DM to develop options tied to a specific dangerous hunt in your past: a Lynel that got away, a village you couldn't save in time, or the first monster you ever successfully tracked down alone.*

{{footnote Backgrounds }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Ruins Delver

You've spent your career exploring Hyrule's countless ancient ruins: Sheikah technology sites, sunken Zonai structures, forgotten temples lost to time. You know how to read old architecture, spot a trap before it springs, and recognize when a "ruin" still has something dangerous living in it.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Investigation, History
**Tool Proficiencies:** Thieves' tools
**Equipment:** A set of climbing gear (50 feet of rope, a grappling hook, and spikes), a lantern, a journal full of your own ruin-sketches and notes, a set of traveler's clothes, and a pouch containing 12 rupees

#### Feature: Ancient Eye

You have a trained eye for the architecture and warning signs of ancient ruins. You automatically notice obvious structural hazards (unstable floors, collapsing ceilings, and similar dangers) without needing to make a check, and you have advantage on Investigation checks made to identify the purpose, age, or origin of ancient architecture, mechanisms, or inscriptions. In addition, you can often make an educated guess about a ruin's general layout or purpose based on its exterior architecture and surrounding terrain alone.

|**Suggested Characteristics**||
| d6 | Personality Trait |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | I touch old stone and metal like I'm greeting an old friend. |
| 2 | I narrate my own discoveries out loud, even when no one is listening. |
| 3 | I'm compulsively thorough. I won't leave a ruin until I've checked every room. |
| 4 | I distrust "obvious" solutions; the real answer is always more interesting. |
| 5 | I sketch everything I find, whether or not it turns out to matter. |
| 6 | I get genuinely upset when I see ruins being looted carelessly or destroyed. |

| d6 | Flaw |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | My curiosity has gotten me trapped, cursed, or badly hurt more than once. |
| 2 | I undervalue danger in places I've convinced myself I understand. |
| 3 | I have a habit of taking "just one more" relic than I should. |
| 4 | I'm dismissive of anyone who doesn't share my fascination with old things. |
| 5 | I've kept secrets about a discovery I knew was too dangerous to share. |
| 6 | I judge a person's worth by how carefully they treat historical sites. |

\column

### Castle Town Guard

You served as a member of the watch in Castle Town or another major settlement: patrolling streets, settling disputes, and keeping the peace among nobles, merchants, and commoners alike. You've seen the kingdom's beating heart up close, for better and for worse.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Insight, Intimidation
**Tool Proficiencies:** One type of gaming set
**Equipment:** A set of guard's manacles, a whistle or signal horn, an insignia marking your former post, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 rupees

#### Feature: Eyes of the Watch

You know the rhythms of city life and can spot when something is wrong before most people notice. You have advantage on Insight checks made to detect suspicious behavior or lies in a settlement, and you have a working relationship with the local watch in any major settlement. Guards recognize you as one of their own (or as someone who once was), and are more inclined to share information, overlook minor infractions, or grant you access to restricted areas in the course of an investigation. This goodwill does not extend to settlements where you have a poor reputation or active conflict with local authority.

|**Suggested Characteristics**||
| d6 | Personality Trait |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | **Order.** A kingdom without law is a kingdom that devours itself. (Lawful) |
| 2 | **Justice.** Everyone deserves fair treatment, noble and commoner alike. (Good) |
| 3 | **Duty.** I swore an oath to protect this place, and I intend to keep it. (Lawful) |
| 4 | **Cynicism.** I've seen how the law actually gets applied, and who it protects. (Chaotic) |
| 5 | **Protection.** The people in my city are mine to look after, full stop. (Good) |
| 6 | **Authority.** I believe in the chain of command, even when I disagree with where it leads. (Lawful) |

| d6 | Bond |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | I left the watch after a corrupt superior forced me to choose between my badge and my conscience. |
| 2 | A fellow guard died protecting me, and I carry that debt everywhere I go. |
| 3 | I still consider my old watch-house my true home, more than anywhere I've lived since. |
| 4 | I once let a criminal go free for reasons I've never told anyone, and I still wonder if it was right. |
| 5 | My family has served in the Castle Town watch for three generations; I'm the first to leave. |
| 6 | I'm searching for someone who slipped through my fingers during my last case on the force. |

# Feats
