# Feats

> *"Talent is what the goddesses give you. What you do with it after that is entirely your own."*
> — Viator Fortuitus, A Bard's Record

Feats represent special talents, training, or aptitudes beyond what your race, class, and background provide. In most campaigns, feats are an optional reward made available at certain levels in place of an Ability Score Improvement, at your DM's discretion.

This chapter reprints the standard feat list in alphabetical order for ease of reference at the table. Flavor text has been lightly adapted to fit Hyrule where it made sense to do so.

**Five feats have been changed mechanically,** because they referred to systems this book replaces. Each is marked with a ✦ and carries a short note explaining what changed: **Magic Initiate**, **Martial Adept**, **Ritual Caster**, **Shield Master**, and **Spell Sniper**. Every other feat works exactly as it does in the 2014 Player's Handbook.

**Using this chapter:** Most characters gain access to feats through the standard rule of trading an Ability Score Improvement for a feat at the levels your class permits. **Hylian characters are the exception.** Every Hylian gains a feat for free at 1st level through the Great Learners racial trait. Because that feat comes at no cost, Hylians draw from a separate, intentionally restricted list. That list is printed under **Great Learners** in the Hylian entry of the **Races of Hyrule** chapter.

### Actor
**Prerequisite:** None

You have honed your ability to mimic the speech and behavior of others.

- Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks when trying to pass yourself off as a different person.
- You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by other creatures. You must have heard the person speaking, or heard the creature make the sound, for at least 1 minute. A successful Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check allows a listener to determine the effect is faked.

### Alert
**Prerequisite:** None

Always on the lookout for danger, you gain the following benefits:

- You gain a +5 bonus to initiative.
- You can't be surprised while you are conscious.
- Other creatures don't gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.

### Athlete
**Prerequisite:** None

You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of your movement.
- Climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
- You can make a running long jump or running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

### Charger
**Prerequisite:** None

When you use your action to Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to shove a creature.

If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

### Crossbow Expert
**Prerequisite:** None

Thanks to extensive practice with the crossbow, you gain the following benefits:

- You ignore the loading quality of crossbows with which you are proficient.
- Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.
- When you use the Attack action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a hand crossbow you are holding.

### Defensive Duelist
**Prerequisite:** Dexterity 13 or higher

When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Dual Wielder
**Prerequisite:** None

You master fighting with two weapons, gaining the following benefits:

- You gain a +1 bonus to AC while you are wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand.
- You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one-handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light.
- You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

### Dungeon Delver
**Prerequisite:** None

Alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many ancient ruins and ancient ruins across Hyrule, you gain the following benefits:

- You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to detect the presence of secret doors.
- You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid or resist traps.
- You have resistance to the damage dealt by traps.
- Traveling at a fast pace doesn't impose the normal penalty on your passive Wisdom (Perception) score.

### Durable
**Prerequisite:** None

Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum number of hit points you regain from the roll equals twice your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

### Elemental Adept

**Prerequisite:** The ability to cast at least one spell

When you gain this feat, choose one damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.

Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.

You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.

### Grappler

**Prerequisite:** Strength 13 or higher

You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits:

- You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are grappling.
- You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you. To do so, make another grapple check. If you succeed, you and the creature are both restrained until the grapple ends.

### Great Weapon Master

**Prerequisite:** None

You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits:

- On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.
- Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a −5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

### Healer
**Prerequisite:** None

You are an able physician, allowing you to mend wounds quickly and get your allies back into the fight.

- When you use a healer's kit to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point.
- As an action, you can spend one use of a healer's kit to tend to a creature and restore 1d6 + 4 hit points to it, plus additional hit points equal to the creature's maximum number of Hit Dice. The creature can't gain the benefit of this feature again until it finishes a short or long rest.

### Heavily Armored

**Prerequisite:** Proficiency with medium armor

You have trained to master the use of heavy armor, gaining the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

### Heavy Armor Master

**Prerequisite:** Proficiency with heavy armor

You can use your armor to deflect strikes that would kill others. You gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- While you are wearing heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 3.

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Inspiring Leader

**Prerequisite:** Charisma 13 or higher

You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you.

Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

### Keen Mind
**Prerequisite:** None

You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision.

- Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You always know which way is north.
- You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
- You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

### Lightly Armored
**Prerequisite:** None

You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You gain proficiency with light armor.

### Linguist
**Prerequisite:** None

You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits:

- Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You learn three languages of your choice.
- You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

### Lucky
**Prerequisite:** None

You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment.

You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional d20. You can choose to spend one of your luck points after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You choose which of the d20s is used for the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

You can also spend one luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Roll a d20, and then choose whether the attack uses the attacker's roll or yours.

If more than one creature spends a luck point to influence the outcome of a roll, the points cancel each other out, and the roll proceeds normally.

You regain your expended luck points when you finish a long rest.

### Mage Slayer
**Prerequisite:** None

You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters, gaining the following benefits:

- When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.
- When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its concentration.
- You have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet of you.

### Magic Initiate ✦

**Prerequisite:** None

Choose a class from any caster in this document's class list. You learn two cantrips of your choice from that class's spell list.

In addition, choose one 1st-level spell from that same list. You learn that spell.

You gain an **MP pool of 3**, usable only for the spells this feat grants. It returns on a long rest. If you already have MP from a class, add 3 to your maximum instead, and you may spend MP from your normal pool on these spells as well.

Casting these spells follows every ordinary rule in the **Magic System** chapter: a cantrip costs 1 MP, the 1st-level spell costs 2, and Arcane Strain applies if you repeat one.

*Changed from the standard rules: this feat originally granted one casting per long rest at the spell's lowest level, which is spell slot language. This book has no spell slots, and a Veilblade or Masked Wanderer taking the feat had no MP to cast with.*

Your spellcasting ability for these spells depends on the class you chose: Charisma for Adventurer (Minstrel path), Blightbound, Champion, or Goddess Chanter; Intelligence for Interloper or Sage (Interlopers may use Charisma instead if they chose it at 1st level; Sages may use Wisdom if their Elemental Affinity uses it); Wisdom for Adventurer (Wild Scout path), Ranger, or Shaman.

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Martial Adept ✦

**Prerequisite:** None

You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat maneuvers. You gain the following benefits:

- You learn two **Special Attacks** of your choice from the **Special Attacks** list in the Veilblade Combo Reference.
- You gain **2 Energy**, which you spend to use them, exactly as a Veilblade does. Each Special Attack costs 1 Energy, and you may use only one per turn. You regain all spent Energy when you finish a short or long rest, and at the end of any combat.
- If you are a Veilblade, you instead add 1 to your maximum Energy and learn two additional Special Attacks.
- Your save DC for these Special Attacks is **8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength, Dexterity, or Intelligence modifier**, chosen when you take this feat.

*Changed from the standard rules: this feat originally used Battle Master maneuvers and superiority dice, neither of which exists in this book. It now uses the Veilblade's Special Attacks and Energy.*

### Medium Armor Master

**Prerequisite:** Proficiency with medium armor

You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits:

- Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
- When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

### Mobile
**Prerequisite:** None

You are exceptionally swift and agile, gaining the following benefits:

- Your speed increases by 10 feet.
- When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn.
- When you make a melee attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or not.

---

### Moderately Armored

**Prerequisite:** Proficiency with light armor

You have trained to master the use of medium armor and shields, gaining the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

---

### Mounted Combatant

**Prerequisite:** None

You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't incapacitated, you gain the following benefits:

- You have advantage on melee attack rolls against any unmounted creature that is smaller than your mount.
- You can force an attack targeted at your mount to target you instead.
- If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

---

### Observant
**Prerequisite:** None

Quick to notice details others might miss, you gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- If you can see a creature's lips while it speaks a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips.
- You have a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.

### Polearm Master

**Prerequisite:** None

You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons, gaining the following benefits:

- When you take the Attack action and attack with only a halberd, spear, quarterstaff, drillshaft, or trident, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage.
- While you are wielding a halberd, spear, quarterstaff, drillshaft, or trident, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.

---

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Resilient
**Prerequisite:** None

Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:

- Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.

---

### Ritual Caster ✦

**Prerequisite:** Intelligence or Wisdom 13 or higher

You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals. Choose a class that has access to the ritual tag for spells in this document (any of the full casters at your DM's discretion). You learn two 1st-level spells of your choice from that class's spell list that have the ritual tag.

You can cast these spells as rituals, but you can't cast them any other way unless you have learned them through other means. You can also add ritual spells to this collection as you find them throughout Hyrule. Copying a ritual into your book takes **2 hours and 50 rupees per spell level**, spent on rare inks and materials, and the spell must be one your chosen class can cast as a ritual.

*Changed from the standard rules only in currency: the cost is the Player's Handbook's, priced in rupees.*

---

### Savage Attacker
**Prerequisite:** None

Once per turn, when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

### Sentinel
**Prerequisite:** None

You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits:

- When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
- Creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach.
- When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.

### Sharpshooter

**Prerequisite:** None

You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:

- Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.
- Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
- Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a −5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

### Shield Master ✦

**Prerequisite:** None

You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a shield:

- If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to shove a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield. This is the only way to move a creature with a shield; the general **Shield Bash** rule in the Items chapter deals damage only.
- If you aren't incapacitated, you can add **+2**, or your shield's Guard value if it is higher, as a bonus to Dexterity saving throws made against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

*Changed from the standard rules: the Dexterity saving throw bonus can exceed +2 when you carry an exceptional shield.*
- If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.

### Skilled
**Prerequisite:** None

You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

### Skulker

**Prerequisite:** Dexterity 13 or higher

You are expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits:

- You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.
- When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
- Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight.

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Spell Sniper ✦

**Prerequisite:** The ability to cast at least one spell

You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits:

- When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.
- Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
- You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll, chosen from any caster class's spell list in this document. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the class you choose it from. If you have no MP pool, you gain one of 1 MP, usable only for this cantrip, which returns on a long rest.

*Changed from the standard rules: the cantrip may come from any caster class in this book rather than the Player's Handbook's four named lists, and a character with no MP is given just enough to cast it.*

### Tavern Brawler
**Prerequisite:** None

Accustomed to rough-and-tumble fighting, you gain the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You are proficient with improvised weapons.
- Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage.
- When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

### Tough
**Prerequisite:** None

Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

### War Caster

**Prerequisite:** The ability to cast at least one spell

You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits:

- You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage.
- You can perform the somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a shield in one or both hands.
- When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a spell at the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack, provided the spell has a casting time of 1 action and can target only that creature.

### Weapon Master
**Prerequisite:** None

You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:

- Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
- You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice.

{{footnote Feats }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Spell Compendium

{{pageNumber,auto}}

  ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnthonyEllisDev/Zelda-DnD/main/images/QrukhZY.png){top:320px,right:180px,height:40%}
}}

{{logo ![](/assets/naturalCritLogoRed.svg)}}

\page

# Zelda DnD Spell Compendium

Spells in this compendium are listed alphabetically. Each spell includes its school, MP cost, casting time, range, duration, components, and full description with Hyrule-appropriate flavor. Spells marked ✦ are original to the Zelda DnD setting. Spells that have class-specific renamed versions note those variants at the end of their entry.

MP costs follow the Spell Chart Conversion: Cantrips 1 MP, 1st-level 2 MP, 2nd-level 3 MP, 3rd-level 4 MP, 4th-level 5 MP, 5th-level 6 MP, 6th-level 7 MP, 7th-level 8 MP, 8th-level 9 MP, 9th-level 10 MP. Overchanneling is an optional upcasting mechanic layered on top of any spell's normal cost, not a replacement cost for high-level spells, see the Magic System chapter for full Overchanneling rules.

---

### Absorb Elements
**School:** Abjuration
**MP Cost:** 3
**Casting Time:** 1 Reaction (when you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage)
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** 1 round
**Components:** S

You channel the incoming energy into your body, drawing it into your hands. You gain resistance to the triggering damage type until the start of your next turn. On your next turn, the first melee attack you make deals an additional 1d6 damage of the triggering type.

*Used by Sages and elemental adventurers who have learned to turn the world's energies against their source.*

---

### Abyssal Barrier ✦
*(Renamed: Shield)*
**School:** Abjuration
**MP Cost:** 2
**Casting Time:** 1 Reaction (when hit by an attack or targeted by magic missile)
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** 1 round
**Components:** V, S

You conjure a barrier of writhing shadow or molten energy in an instant. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a +5 bonus to AC, including against the triggering attack. You also take no damage from magic missile.

The spell flares as a red or violet sigil in the air that pulses once before vanishing.

*Blightbound variant of Shield.*

---

### Aid
**School:** Abjuration
**MP Cost:** 3
**Casting Time:** 1 Action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** 8 hours
**Components:** V, S, M (a feather from a divine bird or blessed string)

You bolster up to three creatures with divine encouragement. Each target's hit point maximum and current hit points increase by 5 for the duration.

*Spend an additional 2 MP to increase the bonus by 5 or target one additional creature.*

You may animate or reassert control over up to two creatures at once (three if you spend an additional 2 MP).

These servants resemble bloated or coral-crusted spirits, their movements rippling unnaturally as though still underwater.

- You instantly make a flower bloom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud.
- You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect: the rustle of leaves, a puff of wind, a distant bird call.
- You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

*The signature catastrophic spell of Earth Sages who have fully mastered their element. Goron Juggernauts invoke it as the culmination of their geomantic power.*

**Components:** V, S

Spells can't extend into the Ethereal Plane, so you can't take damage from spells while ethereal. **Components:** V, S, M (a shard of volcanic glass, storm crystal, or similar)
**Save:** Dexterity
**Damage:** Lightning

You release a crackling bolt of lightning in a 100-foot line, 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 8d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

*Spend 2 additional MP to add 1d6 damage.*

**Stormpiercer's Strike (Rito Marksman variant):** Fired from altitude, this bolt drops straight down from the caster's position, piercing through any number of targets in a vertical line below them.

**Components:** V, S, M (a thread from the object or a similar item)

You sense the direction of a specific object within 1,000 feet that you are familiar with. You can also describe a specific kind of object (a red gem, a Sheikah slate, a longsword) and sense the nearest one of its kind.

**Components:** V, S, M (a pinch of dirt)

- Flames brighten or dim like celestial candles.
- The ground briefly glows with sacred runes.
- Windows or cloth rustle as if brushed by spirits.

## Unassigned Spells

The thirteen spells below appear in this compendium but on no class's spell list. That is deliberate, and it is worth explaining, because a caster in this book can normally use anything on their class list and these are the only spells nobody can reach that way.

An earlier draft of Zelda DnD used **Racial Classes**: a rule under which only one race could take a given class, and each of those pairings unlocked a small set of unique spells. The six lists were the Deku Thornweaver, the Gerudo Sandreaver, the Goron Juggernaut, the Rito Marksman, the Sheikah Phantom, and the Zora Tidecaller. That rule was cut, because tying a class to a single race turned out to be far more limiting than it was interesting. The spells written for it were kept.

**These thirteen are yours to place.** They have no owner and no class, and a DM should hand them out the way a Zelda game hands out an item: as something found, not something chosen at character creation.

| Spell | Level | Fits |
|:--|:--:|:--|
| Kelp Lash ✦ | 1st | Zora, water, coastal |
| Shape Coral ✦ | 1st | Zora, reef, building |
| Veil of the Deep ✦ | 2nd | Zora, stealth underwater |
| Wall of Pressure ✦ | 3rd | Zora, control |
| Oath of the Tides ✦ | 3rd | Zora, oath and binding |
| Spirits of the Sea ✦ | 4th | Zora, summoning |
| Drowned Servants ✦ | 5th | Zora, necromancy |
| Phantom Glider ✦ | 3rd | Rito, Sheikah, movement |
| Laughing Pressure Point ✦ | 2nd | Sheikah, subtlety |
| Conjure Woodland Beings | 4th | Deku, Kokiri, forest |
| Transport via Plants | 6th | Deku, Kokiri, forest |
| Contagion | 5th | Blight, corruption, curses |
| Antipathy/Sympathy | 8th | High magic, wards, traps |

**Ways to use them.** Any of these is a good reason for a party to go somewhere.

- **A spell tome.** The classic. A book in a ruin that teaches its reader one spell permanently, regardless of class. This is the closest thing this book has to a scroll, and it is a fine dungeon reward.
- **An item that casts it.** A coral rod that casts *Shape Coral* once per long rest. A Sheikah pressure-seal that casts *Laughing Pressure Point*. Attach the spell to an object and the spell becomes a treasure rather than a rules exception.
- **A subclass bonus.** Give a Sage's Elemental Affinity or Oracle Path one of these as a signature. A Water-affinity Sage who knows *Wall of Pressure* feels different from one who does not, and nothing in the rules breaks.
- **A teacher.** An NPC who will teach one of these in exchange for something. Slower than a tome and better for a campaign.
- **An enemy's trick.** Nothing says a spell has to be available to players at all. *Drowned Servants* in the hands of a river-cult necromancer is a whole adventure.

Balance them as you would any spell of their level. They were written for characters who had given up a great deal of flexibility to reach them, so if you hand one out freely, expect it to feel slightly stronger than a spell of the same level that everybody already has.

# The Blin

*Monstrous Humanoids of Hyrule*

> *"They are not mindless beasts. They cook. They sing. They argue. And when the drums begin, they march."*
> — Field Notes of a Sheikah Scout

Among the countless monsters that roam the lands of Hyrule, few are as widespread or as deceptively organized as the **Blins**. This extended family of horned humanoids forms the backbone of most monster forces encountered across Hyrule, ranging from ramshackle camps in open fields to fortified strongholds ruled by brutal champions.

Though often dismissed as nuisances, the Blins possess a crude yet functional society, complete with language (**Blin**), hierarchy, craftsmanship, and warfare traditions. Underestimating them has cost many adventurers their lives.

---

## Blin Society and Culture

### Language

All Blins speak **Blin**, a guttural tongue filled with sharp consonants, whistles, and rhythmic barking sounds. While simple in structure, Blin is capable of conveying tactics, insults, and surprisingly specific commands. Boss Bokoblins often communicate authority through whistles, horn blasts, and shouted phrases rather than complex speech.

### Diet and Sustenance

Blins are omnivorous scavengers with a preference for:

- Roasted meat (wild boar, deer, birds, and occasionally livestock)
- Seared fish
- Roasted mushrooms and roots
  They are notably fond of cooking, often grilling meat over open fires, sometimes excessively so. Food is communal but **rank dictates portion size**. Higher-status Blins eat first and most.

Cannibalism is rare but not unheard of during extreme famine or after internal power struggles.

### Camps and Architecture

Blin camps are highly recognizable:

- **Skull-shaped huts**, bone palisades, and wooden watchtowers
- Spiked barricades and crude alarm systems (metal plates, dangling bones)
- Central fire pits used for cooking and gatherings
- Weapon racks filled with clubs, spears, bows, and scavenged arms

Camps are often placed strategically (on hills, near roads, or overlooking bridges) and are frequently guarded by elevated archers or thrown projectiles.

---

## Hierarchy of the Blins

Blin society is rigidly hierarchical and enforced through violence.

1. **Boss Bokoblins** – Absolute leaders of mixed Blin groups
2. **Moblins** – Enforcers, shock troops, and overseers
3. **Bokoblins** – Common soldiers, hunters, and laborers
4. **Horriblins** – Specialists adapted for subterranean warfare

Color variants (Blue, Black, Silver) typically indicate both **strength and rank**.

:

## The Bokoblins

*The Common Footsoldiers*

Bokoblins are the most frequently encountered Blins. Shorter than Moblins but quick and aggressive, they rely on numbers, ambush tactics, and sheer enthusiasm for violence.

### Behavioral Traits

- Cowardly when alone, bold in groups
- Highly territorial
- Easily distracted by food or noise
- Celebrate victories with dancing, shouting, and crude music

### Variants

- **Red Bokoblins**: The weakest and most common. Poorly trained but numerous.
- **Green Bokoblins**: These variants of Bokoblin have wild magic which courses through their veins, turning their skin green. They typically take of shaman roles in their tribes and are able to cast very basic spells.
- **Blue Bokoblins**: More disciplined, tougher, and often serve as squad leaders.
- **Black Bokoblins**: Veteran warriors with hardened bodies and devastating horn attacks.
- **Silver Bokoblins**: Touched by Ganon's power; marked with purple patterns and glowing horns. Feared even by their own kind.

{{footnote Enemies | The Blin }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## The Moblins

*Brutes and Enforcers*

Towering over Bokoblins, Moblins are living battering rams. Their immense strength allows them to wield massive weapons, and even use smaller Blins as improvised projectiles.

### Role in Blin Society

- Enforce discipline
- Guard key positions
- Break enemy lines
- Punish disobedience

Moblin loyalty is usually purchased through violence or fear rather than respect.

### Variants

- **Red Moblins**: Strong but relatively simple-minded.
- **Blue Moblins**: More tactical, often armed with heavy polearms.
- **Black Moblins**: Extremely resilient; often serve as champions or lieutenants.
- **Silver Moblins**: Rare, terrifying juggernauts infused with overwhelming demonic magic.

---

## Boss Bokoblins

*Warlords of the Camps*

Boss Bokoblins are unmistakable: massive frames, razor-sharp horns, and an air of cruel confidence. They command through intimidation, whistles, and ritualized violence.

### Leadership Style

- Issue orders via whistled signals
- Use coordinated minion tactics
- Execute subordinates publicly to assert dominance

Boss Bokoblins often hoard the best weapons and armor and surround themselves with elite guards.

### Variants

- **Red & Blue Boss Bokoblins**: Common camp leaders.
- **Black Boss Bokoblins**: Tactical commanders capable of devastating combined assaults.
- **Silver Boss Bokoblins**: Walking engines of destruction, infused with the Demon King's essence and often guarding sites of great power.

\column

## The Horriblins

*Masters of the Deep*

Horriblins are a disturbing offshoot of the Blin family, adapted to Hyrule's caves and underground passages after the Upheaval.

### Physical Adaptations

- Powerful arms and gripping hands
- Horns suited for crushing stone
- Ability to cling to walls and ceilings
- Ambush predators by nature

### Behavior

- Prefer vertical combat
- Drop onto prey from above
- Coordinate rock-throwing attacks
- Rarely retreat unless overwhelmed

### Variants

- **Red Horriblins**: Opportunistic ambushers.
- **Blue Horriblins**: Capable of throwing massive stones.
- **Black Horriblins**: Deadly veterans with terrifying strength.
- **Silver Horriblins**: Cave lords marked by purple demonic sigils, feared even by Moblins.

---

## Relations with Other Species

- **Hylians & Allied Races**: Viewed as prey or enemies
- **Other Monsters**: Temporary alliances under Ganon's influence
- **Within Their Own Kind**: Constant power struggles, respect earned through strength

Blins are capable of cooperation, but betrayal is common, especially when leadership is weak.

# Guardian Constructs

*The Eternal Watchers*

> *"Kings perish. Kingdoms fall. The guardians remain."*
>
> — Inscription recovered from the Lanayru Archives

Scattered throughout Hyrule's oldest ruins are remnants of civilizations long forgotten. Among the most enduring of these relics are the **Guardian Constructs**, magical automatons created to protect sacred locations, powerful artifacts, and ancient secrets.

Unlike living creatures, Guardian Constructs do not hunger, tire, or age. They exist for a singular purpose determined by their creators. Centuries after the collapse of the kingdoms that forged them, many still stand watch over crumbling temples and buried sanctuaries.

Most Guardian Constructs operate according to ancient directives embedded deep within their magical cores. They rarely distinguish between friend and foe, instead responding to specific conditions such as trespassing, proximity to protected relics, or the opening of sealed chambers.

Many scholars consider them among the most dangerous relics of the ancient world. They are not malicious; they simply cannot abandon their duty.

---

## Shared Characteristics

Though their forms vary greatly, most Guardian Constructs possess several common traits:

- Bodies fashioned from stone, metal, or enchanted crystal
- Magical cores that serve as both power source and weakness
- Immunity to age, disease, and exhaustion
- Unwavering obedience to ancient commands
- Extraordinary durability

Many ancient builders intentionally incorporated hidden vulnerabilities into their creations. These weak points were intended to allow trusted guardians or priests to disable the constructs should they ever become uncontrollable.

\column

## Known Guardian Types

### Armos

Animated statues designed to patrol and physically eliminate intruders.

### Beamos

Stationary sentries equipped with magical eye-beams capable of striking targets from great distances.

### Sentinels

Massive guardian constructs responsible for protecting the most sacred locations.

### Relic Guardians

Rare constructs designed to protect specific treasures or royal tombs.

Most adventurers encounter only Armos and Beamos. Surviving encounters with stronger Guardian Constructs is considerably less common.

{{footnote Enemies | Guardians }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

# Armos

*Ancient Guardians of Forgotten Kingdoms*

> *"Many travelers have mistaken an Armos for a statue. Few survive long enough to repeat the mistake."*
>
> — Journal of the Royal Antiquarian Society

Throughout Hyrule's oldest ruins stand silent sentinels of stone known as **Armos**. To the untrained eye they appear to be little more than weathered statues placed beside forgotten roads, temple entrances, and sacred relics. Yet beneath their stone shells burns ancient magic that has endured for centuries.

No one agrees upon who first created the Armos. Some scholars claim they were forged by forgotten kingdoms to protect holy sites. Others believe they were animated by powerful sages during ages long lost to history. Whatever their origin, Armos continue to fulfill their purpose long after the civilizations that created them have crumbled into dust.

An inactive Armos can remain motionless for decades. Moss grows upon them. Birds nest atop their heads. Entire generations may pass believing them to be ordinary monuments.

Then an intruder draws near.

The statue's eyes ignite.

Stone cracks.

And the guardian awakens.

---

## Eternal Vigil

Unlike most monsters, Armos do not hunt, eat, sleep, or reproduce.

They exist solely to protect.

Each Armos is bound to a location, object, or command established by its creators. Some defend temple entrances. Others guard sacred treasures, hidden chambers, or royal tombs. Once activated, an Armos pursues intruders with unwavering determination until either the threat is eliminated or the guardian itself is destroyed.

Many adventurers have noted that Armos rarely show aggression outside their assigned territory. A traveler may walk safely past an inactive Armos for years, only to trigger its wrath by crossing an invisible boundary.

\column

## Ancient Construction

Most Armos are carved from enchanted stone and reinforced with powerful magical runes hidden beneath their outer shells.

Though their forms vary between regions, most share several traits:

- Heavy stone bodies resistant to mundane weapons
- Glowing magical cores that animate their movements
- Exceptional resistance to hostile magic
- Limited intelligence focused entirely on defense

Many Armos contain hidden weaknesses deliberately built into their construction. Ancient creators often included exposed runes, eyes, or magical cores that could be targeted should the guardians ever turn against their masters.

---

## Combat Behavior

Armos are terrifyingly direct combatants.

They do not taunt.
They do not retreat.
They do not negotiate.

Once awakened, they advance relentlessly toward perceived threats.

Common tactics include:

- Powerful leaping attacks
- Body slams and crushing strikes
- Coordinated formations with nearby Armos
- Blocking passages and escape routes

Veteran adventurers quickly learn that an Armos wins by persistence rather than speed.

---

## Weak Point: Core Rune

Beneath layers of enchanted stone lies the magical rune that powers an Armos.

A precise strike against this rune can temporarily disrupt the guardian's enchantments.

### Called Shot (Rune)

**Hit:** The Armos loses its Magic Resistance until the start of its next turn.

**Critical:** The Armos is stunned until the end of its next turn.

{{footnote Enemies | Armos }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Variants

### Armos

The most common form of Armos. These guardians are typically encountered protecting ruins, temple entrances, and forgotten pathways.

### Armos Knights

Larger and significantly more powerful than standard Armos, these elite guardians are often entrusted with protecting sacred relics, keys, and powerful artifacts.

Armos Knights frequently serve as commanders for groups of lesser Armos and display far greater tactical awareness.

### Death Armos

Ancient guardians corrupted by dark magic.

Their stone bodies crack with shadowy energy and their movements become unnaturally fast and violent. Many Death Armos unleash devastating magical blasts or explosive bursts when damaged.

Entire ruins have been abandoned after a single Death Armos awakened within them.

### Armos Sentinels

The rarest known form of Armos.

Towering over ordinary guardians, these colossal constructs were created to defend locations of immense importance. Some legends claim a Sentinel can remain active for thousands of years without its magic fading.

Entire armies have fallen attempting to breach a Sentinel's watch.

# Beamos

*Eyes of the Ancient Kingdoms*

> *"The statue never moved. The eye did."*
>
> — Last recorded words of an unidentified treasure hunter

Among the many Guardian Constructs left behind by forgotten civilizations, few inspire more dread than the **Beamos**. Unlike the lumbering Armos, Beamos are not designed to pursue intruders. They are executioners, built to identify threats and eliminate them with ruthless efficiency.

A Beamos consists primarily of a heavily armored pedestal supporting a magically empowered eye. This eye rotates endlessly, scanning halls, chambers, and passageways for signs of intrusion.

The moment a target is identified, the eye focuses.

Moments later, a beam of destructive magical energy follows.

---

### Eternal Sentries

Most Beamos are permanently anchored to a specific location.

Temple architects frequently positioned them:

- Along major corridors
- At chamber entrances
- Beside important treasures
- Over bridges and narrow passages

Many ruins contain multiple Beamos arranged to create overlapping fields of fire, forcing intruders to advance through a deadly gauntlet of magical attacks.

---

### The Living Eye

The eye of a Beamos serves as both weapon and weakness.

Ancient builders deliberately exposed the eye so that trusted temple guardians could disable malfunctioning constructs. Though heavily reinforced by enchantments, the eye remains significantly more vulnerable than the rest of the construct.

Many experienced adventurers learn to focus their attacks on the eye before attempting to destroy the construct itself.


### Weak Point: Eye

#### Called Shot (Eye)

**Hit:** The Beamos cannot use Eye Beam until the end of its next turn.

**Critical:** The Beamos is blinded for 1 minute.

---

### Variants

#### Beamos

The most common form. Designed to protect corridors, treasure rooms, and temple entrances.

#### Great Beamos

Larger sentries capable of projecting devastating beams across entire chambers.

#### Death Beamos

Corrupted guardian constructs empowered by dark magic. Their beams can disintegrate flesh and stone alike.

#### Beamos Overseer

Rare command constructs capable of coordinating multiple nearby guardian constructs simultaneously.

# ChuChus

*Living Slimes of Hyrule*

> *"Most travelers laugh when they first see a ChuChu. Few are still laughing after discovering the puddle beneath their boot was waiting to eat them."*
>
> — Journal of an Unnamed Adventurer

Few creatures in Hyrule are as widespread, adaptable, or bizarre as the **ChuChus**. Found in nearly every era and every corner of the world, ChuChus are gelatinous lifeforms composed of a mysterious magical slime known simply as **Chu Jelly**.

Though individually weak, ChuChus possess an uncanny ability to adapt to their environments. Over generations they absorb elemental energies, magical residue, and ambient forces, resulting in countless regional variants.

Some scholars classify ChuChus as oozes. Others argue they are primitive magical organisms. The truth remains unknown.

---

## A Family in Tiers

ChuChu colonies follow a clear progression, and understanding it is the key to understanding the species as a whole.

**Blue ChuChus** are the common base form, found almost anywhere in Hyrule with still or moving water nearby. **Green ChuChus** are a rarer and more dangerous variant: the only ChuChus capable of absorbing raw elemental energy directly from an attack and being permanently transformed by it, mid-combat, into an **Ember**, **Frost**, or **Spark ChuChu**. **Red, Yellow, and Purple ChuChus** are something different entirely: entire colonies that have lived for generations near a strong elemental or magical source, rather than individuals that transformed in battle, slowly developing true inherited resistance as a trait of their bloodline rather than a one-time event. **Dark ChuChus** remain the rarest and most dangerous known variant, born only from the death of one of their own.

This distinction matters a great deal to anyone who studies (or fights) ChuChus. A Green ChuChu's transformation is sudden, individual, and irreversible the moment it happens. A Red, Yellow, or Purple ChuChu was simply born that way, the inherited legacy of a colony that has lived beside fire, storm, or curse for longer than any single ChuChu's lifespan.

\column

## Biology of the ChuChu

ChuChus possess no bones, organs, or recognizable anatomy.

Instead, their bodies are composed entirely of semi-solid magical jelly surrounding a dense central nucleus. This nucleus acts as both brain and heart, directing the creature's movements despite its complete lack of skeletal structure.

### Reproduction

According to Sheikah observations, ChuChus reproduce through two distinct processes.

The first is ordinary growth and division during peacetime: large ChuChus gradually grow until unstable, at which point they divide into multiple smaller ChuChus. The second is far more sudden: a ChuChu struck by a bladed weapon will violently split apart on the spot, its body dividing into two smaller ChuChus that share what remained of its vitality between them. This reflexive defense explains why ChuChu populations recover so quickly after being culled, and why experienced monster hunters favor blunt weapons when they mean to finish the job in one strike.

### Colony Adaptation

Over many generations, an isolated ChuChu colony can slowly take on the character of its environment. A colony that has lived for generations beside a volcanic vent may gradually develop true fire resistance, passed down rather than acquired. Colonies near storm-wracked deserts or cursed ruins show similar patterns, Yellow and Purple ChuChus among them. This is a slow, inherited process, unrelated to anything a single ChuChu experiences in its own lifetime.

**Green ChuChus are the one known exception.** Rather than waiting for generations of inherited adaptation, a Green ChuChu can absorb a burst of elemental energy directly from a single attack and be permanently transformed by it, on the spot, mid-battle. No other variant has ever been observed doing this. Once transformed, the change cannot be undone, and a ChuChu that has already transformed once will never transform again. Whatever element claims it first is the element it carries for the rest of its life.

{{footnote Enemies | ChuChus }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Splitting

Every ChuChu in this family (Blue, Green, any of Green's elemental-transformed forms, Red, Yellow, Purple, and Dark alike) shares the following trait, printed identically in each stat block below:

> ***Splitting.*** Whenever the ChuChu takes slashing damage and has 2 or more hit points remaining afterward, it immediately splits into two new ChuChus of the same type. Each new ChuChu has hit points equal to half the parent's remaining hit points (rounded down), Armor Class 12, and uses the Hop action (*Melee Weapon Attack:* +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage) in place of its normal attacks, but otherwise retains all of the parent's traits, resistances, and immunities. If the ChuChu's remaining hit points after taking slashing damage would be 1 or fewer, it dies instead and does not split.
>
> A split ChuChu's reduced form can itself split again under the same rules, provided it still has 2 or more hit points remaining after taking slashing damage. There is no limit to how many times a single ChuChu lineage can split beyond this hit point floor.

### Amorphous

Every ChuChu also retains the following trait:

> ***Amorphous.*** The ChuChu can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

\column

## Behavior

Despite their simplistic appearance, ChuChus display several consistent behaviors:

- Wander aimlessly until prey approaches
- Ambush creatures by hiding as puddles
- Gather in colonies around sources of magic
- Divide reflexively into smaller specimens when cut
- Recognize movement, warmth, and magical energy, but show no sign of higher reasoning

## Chu Jelly

When a ChuChu is destroyed, its body collapses into a substance known as **Chu Jelly**.

Across Hyrule, alchemists prize Chu Jelly for its unusual magical properties.

Depending on the type of ChuChu, the jelly may contain:

- Healing properties
- Magical energy
- Elemental energy
- Alchemical reagents
- Potion ingredients

Many scholars believe the value of Chu Jelly is the primary reason ChuChus have never been fully eradicated despite their nuisance status.

{{footnote Enemies | ChuChus }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## ChuChu Variants

The color of a ChuChu is usually the easiest way to determine its abilities and, increasingly, its place in the family's tier structure.

### Blue ChuChus

The most common variety, and the family's base form.

Blue ChuChus are found in temperate regions: forests, grasslands, lakes, rivers, coastlines, and wetlands. They carry no elemental trait of their own. Most adventurers encounter these first, and most ChuChu colonies elsewhere in Hyrule began, generations ago, as ordinary Blue ChuChu populations that slowly adapted to wherever they settled.

### Green ChuChus

Thriving in the same forests and grasslands as their Blue cousins, Green ChuChus carry one extraordinary trait no other variant possesses: the ability to absorb raw elemental magic directly from an attack and be instantly, permanently transformed by it. A Green ChuChu struck by fire, frost, or lightning may, without warning and mid-combat, reform itself into an Ember, Frost, or Spark ChuChu before the fight is even over. Once this happens, it cannot happen again; whichever element claims a Green ChuChu first is the one it carries for the rest of its life.

### Ember, Frost, and Spark ChuChus

The transformed results of a Green ChuChu's elemental absorption. An **Ember ChuChu** has been permanently claimed by fire, its body warm to the touch, immune to flame, and dangerously vulnerable to cold. A **Frost ChuChu** has been claimed by cold in the same way, immune to its own element and vulnerable to fire. A **Spark ChuChu** carries a permanent electrical charge, immune to lightning and dangerous to touch with any metal weapon. None of these forms exist as their own independent colonies, every one was once a Green ChuChu, and every one is a permanent, individual transformation rather than an inherited trait.

### Red ChuChus

Where Ember ChuChus are individuals transformed in a single moment, Red ChuChus are something older: entire colonies that have lived for generations near volcanic regions, lava flows, and other sources of sustained fire magic, slowly developing true inherited fire resistance as a trait of their bloodline. Their bodies run warm even at rest, and an agitated Red ChuChu can ignite nearby flammable materials simply by touch.

\column

### Yellow ChuChus

Like the Red ChuChu, the Yellow ChuChu's lightning resistance is inherited rather than individually acquired, the legacy of colonies that have lived for generations in deserts, thunderstorm-wracked highlands, and regions saturated with electrical magic. When threatened, a Yellow ChuChu discharges bursts of lightning through its gelatinous body. Many inexperienced adventurers learn quickly that striking one with a metal weapon is a painful mistake.

### Purple ChuChus

Rare and poorly understood, Purple ChuChus represent colonies that have lived for generations near corrupted or cursed magical sources, slowly developing resistance to the same psychic disturbance their environment constantly produces. Their jelly causes dizziness, confusion, or strange hallucinations when improperly handled, and they are frequently found near cursed ruins and places touched by dark magic.

### Dark ChuChus

Among the rarest known variants, and the only one not born from environmental adaptation at all. Dark ChuChus appear as masses of nearly black slime with glowing eyes, and most researchers believe every Dark ChuChu in Hyrule was once something else, reborn from the destruction of an ordinary ChuChu under circumstances researchers still don't fully understand. Unlike every other variant, Dark ChuChus display genuine aggression and surprising resilience, and the death of a Dark ChuChu is rarely the end of the matter.

{{footnote Enemies | ChuChus }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Darknut

Darknuts are heavily armored warriors that stand among the most feared soldiers in Hyrule's history. Whether cursed spirits, enchanted suits of armor, or elite living warriors, Darknuts are known for their discipline and their swordsmanship.

### Behavior

- Guards important locations
- Challenges powerful opponents
- Fights honorably
- Rarely retreats

### Weak Point: Armor Joints

**Called Shot (Armor Joint)**

**Hit:** The Darknut's Armor Class is reduced by 2 until the start of its next turn.

**Critical:** A section of armor breaks away. The Darknut permanently loses 1 AC.

## Deku Baba

Deku Babas are carnivorous plants commonly found in forests, swamps, and overgrown ruins. Though rooted to the ground, they strike with surprising speed and are known to devour small animals whole.

### Behavior

- Ambush predators
- Remain motionless until prey approaches
- Often found in groups
- Defend territory aggressively

### Weak Point: Stem

**Called Shot (Stem)**

**Hit:** The Deku Baba cannot use Snap until the end of its next turn.

**Critical:** The Deku Baba is knocked prone and restrained until the end of its next turn.

## Dodongo

Dodongos are enormous reptilian monsters famous for their explosive weakness. They inhabit volcanic caverns and consume rocks, minerals, and occasionally adventurers.

### Behavior

- Extremely territorial
- Defends nesting grounds
- Consumes minerals
- Feared by Gorons

### Weak Point: Mouth

**Called Shot (Mouth)**

**Hit:** The Dodongo cannot use Fire Breath until its next turn.

**Critical:** The Dodongo is stunned until the end of its next turn.

Special Rule: If a lit bomb enters the Dodongo's mouth, the Dodongo takes 4d10 force damage and is stunned until the end of its next turn.

## Wallmaster

Wallmasters are giant disembodied hands that lurk on ceilings and upper walls of cursed dungeons. Their sole purpose is to seize intruders and drag them away.

- Prioritize isolated targets
- Ignore most treasure
- Hunt relentlessly

### Weak Point: Wrist

**Hit:** The Wallmaster cannot use Grab until the end of its next turn.

**Critical:** The Wallmaster falls prone.

- Found in tombs and crypts

**Critical:** The Gibdo loses all resistances for 1 minute.

# The Lizalfos

*Scaled Hunters of Hyrule*

> *"Bokoblins fight because they are angry. Moblins fight because they are strong. Lizalfos fight because they have already decided how you will die."*
>
> — Captain of the Castle Guard

The **Lizalfos** are among the most intelligent and dangerous monsters found throughout Hyrule. Unlike the brutish Blins, Lizalfos rely upon agility, cunning, patience, and martial skill. They are accomplished hunters capable of stalking prey for hours before striking with terrifying speed.

Though many Hylians mistake them for simple monsters, Lizalfos display signs of organized tribal behavior, tactical thinking, and sophisticated combat techniques. Some tribes inhabit swamps and deserts, while others dwell within volcanoes, ruins, forests, and ancient strongholds.

Across the ages, three major branches of the species have emerged; Lizalfos, Dinolfos, Aeralfos.

Each represents a different evolutionary adaptation of the same reptilian lineage.

---

### Physiology

Lizalfos possess lean, muscular bodies covered in scales ranging from green and brown to deep black.

Their greatest weapons are often parts of their own bodies:

- Powerful tails capable of sweeping enemies from their feet
- Razor-sharp claws
- Serrated teeth
- Camouflaged scales

Unlike many monsters, Lizalfos are naturally athletic and capable of climbing sheer surfaces, traversing difficult terrain, and swimming with ease.

Their tails are particularly important, serving as both weapons and balancing organs.

---

### Hunting Behavior

Lizalfos are ambush predators first and warriors second.

A typical hunting strategy involves:

- Remaining hidden until prey approaches
- Striking from advantageous terrain
- Isolating weaker targets
- Retreating before a counterattack
- Re-engaging from another angle

Many adventurers mistake a retreating Lizalfos for a fleeing enemy.

Usually it is repositioning for a better kill.

---

### Lizalfos Society

While less hierarchical than the Blins, Lizalfos often form tribal groups led by the strongest warriors.

Strength alone does not determine leadership.

A successful chieftain must also possess:

- Hunting skill
- Tactical intelligence
- Territorial knowledge
- Personal combat prowess

Tribal disputes are often settled through ritual combat rather than outright warfare.

---

### Weapons and Combat

Lizalfos are among the most skilled natural combatants among Hyrule's monsters.

Many carry:

- Curved blades
- Spears
- Tribal shields
- Bone weapons
- Salvaged military equipment

They are known for adapting to an opponent's fighting style and exploiting weaknesses in defenses. In several eras of Hyrule's history, warriors have noted that experienced Lizalfos rapidly learn from repeated attacks and alter their tactics accordingly.

---

### Elemental Adaptations

Certain Lizalfos tribes absorb environmental energies much like ChuChus.

Known variants include:

- Fire Lizalfos
- Ice Lizalfos
- Electric Lizalfos

These elemental subspecies are particularly common in regions saturated with magical energies, including volcanic mountains, frozen wastes, and storm-prone deserts.

---

### Relations with Other Monsters

- **Blins:** Temporary allies under stronger warlords.
- **Constructs:** Often occupy the same ruins but rarely cooperate.
- **Dragons:** Frequently revered or feared.
- **Hylians:** Regarded as rival predators rather than prey.

Among monster races, few creatures command as much respect as a powerful Dinolfos or Aeralfos chieftain.

## Lizalfos

*The Common Hunters*

Lizalfos form the majority of reptilian monster populations across Hyrule.

They are fast, disciplined, and deadly.

Unlike Bokoblins, a lone Lizalfos remains dangerous even when isolated.

### Behavioral Traits

- Patient ambushers
- Highly territorial
- Skilled climbers
- Frequently attack from concealment
- Rarely fight to the death if escape is possible

### Variants

- **Green Lizalfos:** Common hunters and scouts.
- **Blue Lizalfos:** Veteran warriors and tribal champions.
- **Black Lizalfos:** Elite hunters possessing exceptional speed and resilience.
- **Elemental Lizalfos:** Adapted to fire, ice, or lightning-infused regions.

## Dinolfos

*Elite Reptilian Warriors*

Where Lizalfos are hunters, Dinolfos are soldiers.

Known as **Dynalfos** in some historical records, Dinolfos are larger, stronger, and far more heavily armored than their lesser cousins. They often serve as tribal champions, temple guardians, or war leaders.

Many scholars believe Dinolfos represent an elite caste within Lizalfos society rather than a separate species.

### Characteristics

- Larger frames
- Heavy armor
- Greater intelligence
- Superior weapon mastery
- Remarkable durability

Dinolfos frequently wield large swords and are capable of matching trained knights in direct combat.

Some varieties have even demonstrated the ability to breathe fire.

### Behavioral Traits

- Aggressive duelists
- Prefer honorable combat
- Rarely retreat
- Often command lesser Lizalfos

### Variants

- **Dinolfos:** Veteran warriors and champions.
- **Black Dinolfos:** Tribal warlords and elite commanders.
- **Flame Dinolfos:** Rare warriors capable of exhaling fire.

## Aeralfos

*Masters of the Sky*

The rarest branch of the Lizalfos family is the **Aeralfos**.

These winged reptilian warriors possess powerful leathery wings that allow them to dominate aerial battlefields. Armed with swords and shields, Aeralfos often patrol ancient sky ruins and elevated fortresses.

Many historians believe they evolved from isolated Lizalfos populations that adapted to life among Hyrule's floating structures.

### Behavioral Traits

- Territorial aerial predators
- Execute diving attacks
- Harass enemies from above
- Use shields to protect themselves while approaching

### Combat Style

Unlike most flying monsters, Aeralfos are disciplined combatants.

They frequently:

- Circle prey
- Dive from above
- Strike and withdraw
- Force enemies to expose weaknesses
- Coordinate attacks with ground forces

Aeralfos are often encountered as leaders among reptilian warbands or as guardians of ancient skyborne ruins.

# The Octoroks

*Living Artillery of Hyrule*

> *"Most monsters charge. Octoroks aim."*
>
> — Veteran Guard of Castle Town

Among the oldest monsters known throughout Hyrule, **Octoroks** are bizarre creatures descended from ancient aquatic life. Though often dismissed as simple pests, they have adapted to nearly every environment in the kingdom, from rivers and forests to volcanic mountains, frozen tundra, and even the skies themselves. Their remarkable ability to launch projectiles from great distances has made them one of the most widespread and persistent threats encountered by travelers.

Though lacking intelligence, Octoroks possess powerful survival instincts and specialized adaptations that allow countless subspecies to thrive in wildly different climates.

---

## Biology

Octoroks are soft-bodied creatures resembling a strange cross between an octopus and a mollusk. Their most recognizable feature is their tubular snout, which functions as a biological cannon capable of launching rocks, snowballs, seeds, explosive projectiles, and other materials depending on the species.

Most possess:

- Powerful lungs capable of compressing air
- Elastic internal sacs used to launch projectiles
- Natural camouflage
- Excellent hearing and vibration detection
- Surprisingly durable hides despite their appearance

Though they lack complex reasoning, Octoroks demonstrate remarkable environmental adaptation.

---

## Behavior

Despite their many forms, most Octoroks share several behavioral traits:

- Prefer attacking from range
- Retreat when approached directly
- Ambush prey from concealment
- Remain solitary outside breeding seasons
- Attack anything perceived as a threat

Unlike Blins or Lizalfos, Octoroks possess no true society and do not organize into tribes.

---

## The Great Defense Mechanism

Across nearly every appearance throughout Hyrule's history, Octoroks possess one famous weakness:

### Reflected Projectiles

Whether launching stones, snowballs, seeds, or magical projectiles, Octoroks rarely survive their own ammunition being returned to them.

Many experienced warriors intentionally bait an Octorok's attack before redirecting the projectile with a shield or weapon. Legends claim entire generations of Hylian soldiers learned shield techniques specifically to combat Octorok infestations.

{{footnote Enemies | Octoroks }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Octorok Variants

Over centuries, Octoroks have evolved into numerous specialized subspecies.

### Red Octoroks

The most common variety.

Found throughout plains, roads, grasslands, and wilderness areas, Red Octoroks rely on simple rock projectiles and skittish hit-and-run tactics.

They are often the first monster encountered by new adventurers.

### Blue Octoroks

A tougher and more aggressive breed.

Blue Octoroks possess stronger musculature and can launch stones with significantly greater force than their red cousins.

They are commonly found in dangerous wilderness regions and monster-controlled territory.

### Forest Octoroks

Masters of camouflage.

Forest Octoroks disguise themselves as bushes, grass clumps, or vegetation until prey approaches. They remain nearly motionless for hours before attacking.

### Water Octoroks

Aquatic hunters found in lakes, rivers, and coastlines.

Unlike land-based species, Water Octoroks spend most of their lives submerged and emerge only long enough to launch attacks.

### Rock Octoroks

Mountain-dwelling Octoroks adapted to volcanic regions.

These creatures consume ore, stone, and metallic debris. Their internal grinding organs can pulverize even solid rock before launching it as deadly ammunition. In some regions they have become infamous for swallowing and regurgitating weapons and equipment.

### Snow Octoroks

Cold-weather ambushers.

Snow Octoroks hide beneath drifts and disguise themselves as patches of winter grass. They emerge suddenly to launch compacted snowballs at unsuspecting travelers.

### Sky Octoroks

Among the rarest known subspecies.

Using leaf-like membranes and buoyant gas sacs, Sky Octoroks drift among floating islands and high-altitude regions. They attack aerial travelers with surprising accuracy.

### Relations With Other Monsters

- **Blins** often hunt Octoroks for food.
- **Lizalfos** frequently compete with Water Octoroks for territory.
- **Moblins** sometimes use captured Octoroks as living artillery.
- Most monsters view Octoroks as nuisances rather than allies.

Because of their solitary nature, Octoroks rarely participate in organized monster armies.

## Gohma, Parasite of the Deep Root

> *"The Great Tree does not complain. It does not cry out. It simply grows quiet, and that silence is how you know something is wrong."*

**Recommended Party Level:** 2–3
**Recommended Party Size:** 3–5
**CR:** 4 (1,100 XP)
**Dungeon Item:** Deku Sling (a sturdy slingshot found in the dungeon's second chamber, dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage at range with the ability to fire Deku Seeds, treat as ammunition that can be foraged at no cost within any Deku-aligned forest)
**Central Mechanic:** None, a clean, teaching-focused boss with no environmental gimmick beyond the arena's vertical space.

---

### Context: The Hollow Root

Deep beneath the canopy of an ancient, living Deku tree (not corrupted, just old and vast enough to hold its own ecosystem), something has taken root that should not be there. The tree's guardian Deku Scrubs have sealed the lower chambers and called for help: a massive, segmented parasite has burrowed into the heartwood, and the tree's sap has begun running thin and pale.

This is **Gohma**, not malevolent in any complex sense, simply a voracious larval predator that has found an extraordinary food source. It does not scheme. It does not bargain. It hungers, and it has nearly eaten through to the tree's core.

Unlike the Thornheart Sanctum (a sealed ruin reclaimed by corruption), the Hollow Root is a *living* dungeon, its walls breathe, faint bioluminescent fungus lights the lower chambers, and the tree's own immune response (animated root tendrils, Deku Scrub guardians) is actively, if weakly, fighting back against the infestation alongside the party.

\column

### The Arena: The Heartwood Chamber

*A vast, hollow chamber at the tree's core, easily sixty feet across and forty feet tall, ringed with thick root-shelves at three different heights, connected by knotted vine-ladders. Pale fungal light filters down from cracks far above. At the chamber's center, a single massive taproot descends into darkness, and clinging to its underside, easily the size of a cart horse, is Gohma.*

**Arena features:**
- **Three root-shelves** at heights of 0, 15, and 30 feet, connected by vines that can be climbed (DC 10 Athletics, or freely by anyone with a climbing speed).
- **The central taproot** dominates the chamber's middle. Gohma is initially anchored to its underside, near the ceiling.
- **Falling debris zones**: when Gohma is struck hard enough (see Phase 2), chunks of disturbed root and bark fall in a 10-foot radius beneath it, dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage to anyone standing there at the start of Gohma's turn (Dexterity save DC 12 negates).
- **Deku Seed pods** grow naturally along the root-shelves, any character can spend an action to gather a handful, refilling a Deku Sling's ammunition entirely.

{{imageMaskCenter1,--offsetX:0%,--offsetY:0%,--rotation:0

}}

{{footnote Bosses | Gohma }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Phase 1. The Watching Eye (100% → 60% HP)

*Gohma clings to the underside of the great taproot, a segmented horror of chitin and too many legs, motionless except for a single massive eye that swivels to track movement below. It has not yet engaged. It is deciding whether you are food.*

**Discovery:** Self-evident. Gohma's single oversized eye is the obvious, instantly recognizable weak point, and that is intentional. This fight exists partly to teach new players the Weak Point system in its purest, least obscured form. No hint roll is needed; even players unfamiliar with the Zelda series will look at a giant eye on a monster and understand what to do with it.

**Behavior:** Gohma remains anchored to the ceiling-taproot for this entire phase, periodically dropping small **Larval Spawn** (use Keese statistics, reflavored as parasite young) onto the lower shelves to harass the party while it watches.

**Attacks:**
- *Acid Spit* (Recharge 5–6): Ranged attack against one target within 60 feet, +5 to hit. On hit: 2d6 acid damage.
- *Summon Larval Spawn:* No action cost, triggers automatically at the start of Gohma's turn if fewer than 2 Larval Spawn are present. One new Larval Spawn drops onto a random shelf.

**Exploitation:** Gohma's eye is only struck effectively by **ranged attacks** while it remains anchored to the ceiling. It is too high and too well-armored along its body for melee to reach the eye directly. A successful ranged attack roll against AC 14, specifically called as a Called Shot (Eye), forces a reaction.

**Vulnerability Window:** On a successful Called Shot (Eye) hit, Gohma shrieks and **releases its grip on the taproot, falling to the nearest root-shelf** (DM's choice of the closest unoccupied shelf to the party). It takes 2d6 fall damage and is **stunned until the end of its next turn**. This transition triggers Phase 2 automatically, regardless of remaining HP. *Gohma's connection to height is itself a kind of structural weak point.*

> **DM note. Hint Roll:** If the party hasn't attempted a ranged attack against the eye after three rounds, allow a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check. Success: *"The creature's eye swivels constantly to track movement, but it never seems to anticipate attacks from a distance the way it does melee."*

\column

### Phase 2, The Fall (60% → 25% HP), Transition: Environmental + Cosmetic/Tactical

*Gohma drops from the ceiling and lands hard on the nearest shelf, the impact cracking root-wood. It is grounded now, and furious. Its legs scrabble for purchase as it turns to face you directly, eye still tracking, but vulnerable in a different way now.*

**What changed:** Gohma is now on the same vertical level as the party (whichever shelf it landed on) and fights at melee range. Its falling debris hazard (see Arena features) is now active beneath wherever it stands.

**Attacks:**
- *Claw* (×2): Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft. On hit: 1d10 + 3 slashing damage.
- *Acid Spit* (Recharge 5–6): As Phase 1.
- *Skittering Charge:* Once per turn, Gohma may move up to its full speed (30 ft.) toward a creature and make one Claw attack at the end of the movement without provoking opportunity attacks.

**Exploitation:** Now grounded, Gohma's eye can be targeted by **melee or ranged Called Shots** equally. However, it actively tries to keep its body angled away from melee attackers, favoring whichever character it perceives as the greatest ranged threat. A melee Called Shot (Eye) requires the attacker to either flank Gohma (advantage from positioning) or wait for it to complete a Claw attack (its eye is more exposed mid-lunge, treat the round after any Skittering Charge as granting advantage on Called Shots against the eye).

**Vulnerability Window:** A successful Called Shot (Eye) stuns Gohma until the end of its next turn and causes it to flinch backward 10 feet. Three successful eye hits during this phase force the transition to Phase 3 (this is a hard trigger rather than an HP threshold: the eye has finally taken lasting damage).

{{footnote Bosses | Gohma }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Phase 3, Death Throes (Triggered at 3 eye hits, or 25% HP, whichever comes first), Transition: Cosmetic/Tactical

*Gohma's eye is cracked and weeping dark fluid. It shrieks, a sound with no analog, half insect and half something older, and its legs begin moving erratically. It is dying, and it knows it, and it is more dangerous now than at any point in the fight.*

**What changed:** Gohma's remaining attacks become faster and less predictable, but its defenses drop sharply as its body fails.

**Attacks:**
- *Frenzied Claws* (×3): Melee attack, +6 to hit, reach 10 ft. On hit: 1d8 + 3 slashing damage. (Same total attacks per round as Phase 2's combination, redistributed into three weaker strikes, more chances to hit, but each less individually threatening.)
- *Final Acid Burst* (1/combat): When Gohma is reduced below 10% of its maximum HP, it unleashes a final desperate attack, each creature within 15 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 acid damage (half on success). This can be telegraphed clearly: *"Its body swells, fluid building visibly beneath its cracked carapace."*

**Exploitation:** Gohma's eye is now AC 10 (its defenses have collapsed) and any hit against it, Called Shot or not, triggers the Vulnerability Window.

**Vulnerability Window:** Any successful attack against the eye in Phase 3 ends the fight; treat Gohma as automatically reduced to 0 HP on a hit (no damage roll needed; this is a finishing blow, not a damage race).

\column

### Defeat

*Gohma's legs curl inward. The shrieking stops. For a moment, the chamber is utterly silent, and then, faintly, you hear something the tree hasn't done in days: the soft, slow creak of healthy growth resuming.*

The parasite's body dissolves into the root-wood within minutes, leaving behind only a hardened chitin shell.

**Failure State:** If the party cannot find or successfully land a Called Shot (Eye) for five consecutive rounds in any phase, Gohma's Larval Spawn production doubles (two new spawns per round instead of one), creating escalating pressure that should make the eye's importance impossible to ignore without ending the fight outright.

---

### Reward

**Mechanical:**
- **Gohma's Chitin Shell:** A crafting component. A Goron smith or Deku Thornweaver-trained Sage can use it to craft a piece of light armor granting resistance to acid damage.
- **Heart of the Root:** Each player gains +2 to their maximum hit points (permanent), the tree's gratitude made tangible.
- **Rupee Cache:** 60 rupees in tree-sap amber, plus a handful of rare Deku Seeds (functionally infinite Deku Sling ammunition for the rest of the campaign).

**Narrative:** The Deku Scrubs who sealed the lower chambers emerge cautiously, and word spreads quickly through any nearby Deku Grove. The party's name becomes known, however small the deed seemed to them, as "the ones who saved the Hollow Root."
