## Great Fairy Fountains

A Great Fairy Fountain is a spring of still water in a place nobody built, sheltered by a bud the size of a cottage. The bud is closed. Something enormous is asleep inside it, and it has been asleep for a long time.

Great Fairies are the oldest sanctioned magic left in Hyrule that is willing to help you. They heal, they restore what magic has cost you, and they will rebuild your armor into something the person who forged it could not have made. What they want in return is rupees and rare things, and they are not shy about the rupees.

### Finding a Fountain

Fountains are hidden, and they stay hidden. They are not marked on maps, they do not appear in surveys, and the people who know where one is tend to be cagey about it.

A party finds a fountain by **being told** (a bard's song, a hermit's directions, a line in an old text) or by **noticing** it: a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Nature) check of DC 15 while travelling through an area that contains one, at the DM's discretion. There is usually a smell of flowers where there is no flower for a mile.

Every fountain contains one Great Fairy, and every Great Fairy is a distinct person with her own temper, her own price, and her own opinion of you.

### Waking a Great Fairy

The bud opens for rupees, and for nothing else. Set the sum by the age of the fountain and how much the party has already spent elsewhere:

| Which fountain | Cost to wake |
|:--|--:|
| The first one you find | 100 rupees |
| The second | 500 rupees |
| The third | 1,000 rupees |
| The fourth and beyond | 10,000 rupees |

Once woken, a Great Fairy stays woken. She is available to that party for the rest of the campaign, and she remembers what they paid.

\column

### What a Great Fairy Does

**Healing.** A creature that bathes in the fountain regains all hit points and ends every disease, poison and non-magical condition afflicting it. A Great Fairy will do this freely, as often as asked, for anyone who has woken her. She will not do it for someone she has not met.

**Restoration.** Bathing also restores all **Magic Points** and all **Stamina Points**, and removes **one Arcane Wound**. Removing further Arcane Wounds costs 500 rupees each, and she will explain, at length, that this is a bargain.

**Upgrading Armor.** This is what parties come for. A Great Fairy can raise one piece of armor by one star, from ★ up to ★★★★, in exchange for rupees and materials.

| Tier | Rupees | Materials |
|:--:|--:|:--|
| ★ | 10 | 3 common monster parts or plants |
| ★★ | 50 | 5 uncommon materials, at least one regional |
| ★★★ | 200 | 8 rare materials, including one from a boss-tier creature |
| ★★★★ | 2,000 | 10 very rare materials, including one that no longer occurs naturally |

Each armor set names its own materials in its entry, or the DM names them. The right materials are the point: an upgrade quest is a reason to go somewhere specific and fight something specific, which is why this rule exists at all.

**Not every fountain can do every tier.** A newly woken Great Fairy works to ★★. Waking a second raises the ceiling to ★★★, and a third to ★★★★. A party that wants a fully upgraded set has to find three fountains, which is a campaign's worth of travelling.

> ##### Gorons and Stone Hide
> A Goron's **Stone Hide** counts as a chest piece for this purpose. A Great Fairy can upgrade it to ★★, and no further; past that she runs out of things to add to a person who is already made of rock.

> ##### What She Will Not Do
> A Great Fairy will not raise the dead, will not remove a curse laid by a god, will not touch anything Malice has been in, and will not discuss the Triforce. Ask her twice about any of these and she stops being cheerful.

{{footnote Items | Great Fairy Fountains }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

## Adventuring Gear & Consumables

Hyrule's adventurers carry more than steel. The world is full of alchemical brews, enchanted tools, elemental arrows, and curious devices that have saved countless heroes from certain death. This chapter covers the consumables, ammunition, tools, and gadgets available to purchase, find, or craft across the realm.

Unless noted, consumable items are used as an **action**. Items marked *bonus action* can be used more quickly, for practiced or desperate use.

---

### Potions & Elixirs

Hyrulean potions are brewed from the natural materials abundant across the kingdom: monster parts, critters, and the magical flora found in every region. Most potions are bought from traveling merchants, apothecaries in larger settlements, or brewed at a **Cooking Pot** with the right ingredients.

Brewing a potion at a Cooking Pot requires a short rest's worth of time and the materials listed. A brewer may attempt an improvised potion by combining materials with similar properties; the DM determines the result.

#### Red Potion (Fairy's Tonic)
*Potion, common*

A vivid crimson potion drawn from Hyrule's most plentiful healing herbs. The original staple of every adventurer's pack, sold in nearly every settlement since before recorded history.

**Effect:** You regain 2d4 + 2 hit points when you drink this potion.

**Cost:** 50 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Hearty Radish or similar potent herb + monster part

---

#### Blue Potion (Life Elixir)
*Potion, uncommon*

A richer, more concentrated brew than the Red Potion. Often the result of added Blue Fire essence or rarer reagents. Restores more vitality and can lift some negative conditions.

**Effect:** You regain 4d4 + 4 hit points. In addition, you end one of the following conditions affecting you: poisoned, frightened, or blinded.

**Cost:** 150 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Premium healing herb + Sunset Firefly + monster part

---

#### Green Potion (Magic Elixir)
*Potion, uncommon*

A deep green concoction that replenishes the magical reserves of a caster, called "magic" in older texts, and "stamina" in more modern usage. Equally useful for fighters burning through Stamina Points.

**Effect:** You recover 3 expended Stamina Points or 3 expended Magic Points (your choice).

**Cost:** 100 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Restless Cricket or Energetic Rhino Beetle + monster part

---

#### Hearty Elixir
*Potion, uncommon*

A golden, richly flavored brew that temporarily swells the drinker's vitality beyond its normal limits.

**Effect:** You gain 10 temporary hit points, which last for 1 hour.

**Cost:** 200 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Hearty Lizard or Hearty Truffle + monster part

---

*Potion, uncommon*

A sharp, metallic-smelling brew brewed from Rhino Beetles and monster ichor. Warriors prize it before difficult fights.

**Effect:** For 1 hour, your weapon damage rolls gain a +1d4 bonus.

**Cost:** 150 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Bladed Rhino Beetle + monster part

---

#### Tough Elixir (Defense Up)
*Potion, uncommon*

A dense, earthy-smelling elixir brewed from armored insects. It temporarily toughens the skin and fortifies the muscles.

**Effect:** For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to AC.

**Cost:** 150 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Rugged Rhino Beetle + monster part

---

#### Sneaky Elixir (Stealth Up)
*Potion, uncommon*

A dark, almost odorless tincture brewed with Sunset Firefly essence. The drinker's footsteps become muffled and their silhouette subtly less distinct.

**Effect:** For 1 hour, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

**Cost:** 100 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Sunset Firefly + monster part

---

#### Hasty Elixir (Speed Up)
*Potion, uncommon*

A fizzing, tingly potion that quickens the legs and sharpens the reflexes.

**Effect:** For 1 hour, your walking speed increases by 10 feet and you have advantage on Dexterity (Initiative) checks.

**Cost:** 100 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Hot-Footed Frog + monster part

**Effect:** For 30 minutes, you gain 1 level of Cold Resistance (see Environmental Hazards).

**Cost:** 60 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Sizzlefin Trout or Warm Darner + monster part

---

*Potion, common*

A cool, mint-tinged tincture that lowers the body's temperature and protects against scorching heat.

**Effect:** For 30 minutes, you gain 1 level of Heat Resistance (see Environmental Hazards).

**Cost:** 60 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Winterwing Butterfly or Cold Darner + monster part

---

*Potion, common*

A faintly buzzing, acrid-smelling brew that temporarily makes the drinker's body resistant to electrical current.

**Effect:** For 30 minutes, you have resistance to lightning damage and advantage on saving throws against the paralyzed condition from electrical sources.

**Cost:** 80 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Electric Darner or Thunderwing Butterfly + monster part

---

*Potion, uncommon*

A thick, magma-orange brew that coats the lungs and skin against the volcanic heat of Death Mountain.

**Effect:** For 30 minutes, you are immune to the environmental hazard of Scorched heat and have resistance to fire damage from non-magical sources.

**Cost:** 120 gp &emsp; **Brewing Materials:** Fireproof Lizard + monster part

*Potion, rare*

A bottled Great Fairy's blessing, the most cherished emergency item a traveler can carry. When the holder falls unconscious, the fairy automatically emerges and revives them.

**Effect (Automatic):** When you drop to 0 hit points, the fairy is automatically released. You immediately regain consciousness with 1d4 + your Constitution modifier hit points, and the bottle becomes empty. Alternatively, you may release the fairy as a bonus action to grant these hit points to any creature you can touch. 

**Cost:** 500 gp (when available) &emsp; Fairies cannot be purchased in most markets. They must be caught near Fairy Fountains or in meadows with a bottle in hand.

*Potion, uncommon (OoT / Classic)*

A shimmering purple brew found primarily in older alchemical traditions. Completely replenishes a caster's magical reserves.

**Effect:** You recover all expended Magic Points.

*Food, common*

Fresh creamy milk from the famous Lon Lon Ranch Talon family herd. Sold in bottles and prized across Hyrule for its restorative properties.

**Effect:** The bottle contains two servings. Each serving restores 1d4 + 1 hit points. *Bonus action* to drink.

**Cost:** 20 gp (full bottle, 2 servings)

*Potion, rare*

An exquisite vintage aged at Romani Ranch, only the finest milk, properly fermented and blessed. Its restorative powers are legendary.

**Effect:** You regain all expended Stamina Points and Magic Points. For 24 hours, you regain 1 Stamina Point at the start of each of your turns.

**Cost:** 200 gp (when available; rarely sold outside Termina and certain elite establishments)

### Arrows & Ammunition

Standard arrows are sold in bundles at most traders and fletcher shops. Special arrows (elemental, bomb, and light) are rarer and more expensive.

| Item | Cost | Notes |
|:--|:--:|:--|
| Arrows (20) | 1 gp | Standard wooden-shafted arrows |
| Arrows (50) | 2 gp | Bulk bundle |
| Fire Arrows (5) | 10 gp | Deal +1d6 fire damage; light flammable objects on contact |
| Ice Arrows (5) | 10 gp | Deal +1d6 cold damage; target must DC 13 Con save or be restrained until end of their next turn |
| Shock Arrows (5) | 10 gp | Deal +1d6 lightning damage; metal-armored targets have disadvantage on save |
| Ancient Arrows (3) | 75 gp | +2d8 force damage; constructs struck must DC 15 Con save or be stunned 1 round |
| Light Arrows (3) | 100 gp | +2d8 radiant damage; undead and creatures vulnerable to radiant take maximum damage |
| Bomb Arrows (5) | 25 gp | On hit, deal 2d6 fire damage in a 5-foot radius (Dex DC 13 half); cannot be fired in rain |
| Dusk Arrows (5) | 20 gp | Silenced on impact; no sound on hit or miss; ideal for stealth |
| Silver Arrows (1) | 50 gp | +2d6 radiant damage; bypass resistances of monsters tied to Ganon's power |
| Phrenic Arrows (5) | 15 gp | On a hit, target must DC 12 Wis save or be confused (as the *confusion* spell) until end of their next turn |

***Fire Arrows*** ignite flammable terrain, light campfires, and melt ice blocks on impact. A single fire arrow can start a grass fire in dry weather.

***Ice Arrows*** freeze water on impact (a 5-foot cube per arrow), creating temporary platforms or blocking waterways. Against creatures vulnerable to cold, the restraining effect has disadvantage on the saving throw.

***Shock Arrows*** deal double damage to creatures that are wet or standing in water. Two shock arrows fired into a pool simultaneously create a 10-foot radius electrified zone lasting 1 round.

***Light Arrows (Silver Arrows)*** are blessed ammunition that bypass the magical protections of Ganon and his servants. Against Blights, Malice constructs, and the King of Evil himself, light and silver arrows ignore damage resistances and immunities. Silver Arrows in particular are associated with the final, ritual defeat of Ganon across the ages. It is said that without a Silver Arrow, Ganon cannot truly be destroyed, only sealed.

***Bomb Arrows*** are notably unstable. They detonate if exposed to open flame, and they cannot be fired in rain without a DC 12 Dexterity check (on a failure, the arrow fizzles and the attack misses automatically).

{{footnote Items | Adventuring Gear & Consuma }}

### Bombs & Explosives

Bombs are one of Hyrule's most iconic adventuring tools, used for combat, mining, demolition, and solving the countless rock-sealed mysteries of the kingdom's dungeons.

#### Bomb
*Adventuring gear, common*

The classic black-powder Hyrulean bomb: spherical, fused, and devastatingly useful. Thrown as a ranged attack (range 20/60), or placed and detonated after a short delay.

**Effect:** When detonated, all creatures within 5 feet must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Bombs also destroy cracked or weakened stone walls and rock barriers.

**Placed Bombs:** A placed bomb detonates at the start of your next turn (or up to 3 rounds later, at your option). Placed bombs can be spotted with a DC 12 Perception check by alert creatures.

**Cost:** 5 gp each, or 25 gp for a bundle of 6

---

#### Bomb Flower
*Adventuring gear, uncommon*

A naturally occurring explosive plant found growing on cliffsides near volcanic and high-altitude regions. Bomb Flowers can be carried, thrown, or fused to weapons and arrows. Unlike manufactured bombs, they do not have a fuse. They detonate on impact.

**Effect:** As a bomb, but detonates immediately on impact. Range 20/60 as an improvised thrown weapon. When fused to an arrow, the arrow becomes a Bomb Arrow (see above).

**Cost:** 8 gp each (when found; they cannot be manufactured)

---

#### Remote Bomb
*Adventuring gear, uncommon (BotW/TotK)*

A Sheikah-tech explosive device with a distinctive square or spherical shape, detonated remotely by the user rather than a fuse. A Remote Bomb does not go off on its own. It only detonates when the user triggers it.

**Effect:** Same as a bomb, but detonates only when you use a bonus action on your turn to trigger it. The bomb remains inert until triggered, and you can only have one Remote Bomb active at a time. Triggering it has a range of 120 feet (line of sight not required; Sheikah resonance technology).

**Cost:** 40 gp (single use). If a character possesses a functional Sheikah Slate, Remote Bombs are available as an unlimited recharging ability (1 at a time; recharges after 30 seconds of real time = 5 rounds).

---

#### Water Bomb
*Adventuring gear, uncommon (OoT, TP)*

A specialized bomb that functions underwater without being extinguished. Uses a waterproofed casing and a different chemical reaction.

**Effect:** As a bomb, but can be used and detonated underwater without penalty.

**Cost:** 10 gp each

---

#### Bombchu
*Adventuring gear, uncommon*

A wind-up mechanical mouse packed with explosive material. When placed, it scurries along walls, floors, or ceilings toward its target before detonating. Fiendishly useful for reaching around corners or along surfaces a thrown bomb cannot reach.

**Effect:** Place the Bombchu on any surface within 5 feet. It moves up to 30 feet in a straight line along any surface (including walls and ceilings) at the start of your next turn, then detonates as a bomb (DC 13 Dexterity save, 3d6 fire damage, 5-foot radius). If it encounters a creature in its path, it detonates immediately. A creature can intercept or stomp a Bombchu with a DC 14 Dexterity check as a reaction.

**Cost:** 15 gp each

{{footnote Items | Adventuring Gear & Consuma }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

### Tools & Gadgets

These are the durable, reusable items that define a Zelda adventurer's toolkit, things carried on belts, over shoulders, or in packs across a lifetime of dungeon-delving.

#### Hookshot
*Adventuring gear, uncommon*

A spring-loaded grappling device that fires a hooked chain at high speed. One of the most iconic and versatile tools in Hyrule, first developed in the Swamp Palace and spread across the kingdom by the adventurers who wielded it.

**Effect:** As an action, you can fire the Hookshot at a target surface or object within **30 feet**. If it finds purchase (wood, stone, metal, or similar solid material), you are immediately pulled to a location adjacent to that surface. This counts as movement and does not provoke opportunity attacks.

Alternatively, you can fire the Hookshot at a **creature** within 30 feet. Make a ranged attack roll (+your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). On a hit, the creature takes 1d6 piercing damage and is pulled up to 15 feet toward you (if Small or Medium). Large or larger creatures are not pulled but are still damaged.

The Hookshot can also grab and retrieve items up to 5 lbs. within 30 feet.

**Cost:** 400 gp

---

#### Longshot
*Adventuring gear, rare*

An upgraded version of the Hookshot with an extended chain, developed by Sheikah engineers in the Water Temple. Functionally identical but with greater reach.

**Effect:** As the Hookshot, but with a range of **60 feet**.

**Cost:** 800 gp (or upgrade an existing Hookshot for 450 gp)

---

#### Clawshot
*Adventuring gear, rare*

A Twilight-era refinement of the Hookshot, featuring a claw mechanism that can grip rough surfaces like vines, mesh gratings, and cave ceilings that a standard hook cannot catch.

**Effect:** As the Hookshot (30-foot range), but can also attach to vines, plant life, rock ceilings, and grated surfaces. In addition, you can hold the Clawshot extended and hang from any surface it is attached to for up to 1 minute before needing to reattach.

**Cost:** 500 gp

---

#### Double Clawshot
*Adventuring gear, very rare (TP)*

Two Clawshots worn on each wrist, allowing an adventurer to cross entire chasms by firing one while hanging from the other.

**Effect:** You carry two Clawshots. While both are equipped, you can use a bonus action to fire the second Clawshot after hanging from the first, effectively allowing you to traverse ceilings, walls, and vertical surfaces indefinitely without falling. Each Clawshot has a 30-foot range. You can also use them to attack twice with a single action, each dealing 1d6 piercing damage.

**Cost:** 1,200 gp (or 600 gp to pair with an existing Clawshot)

---

#### Empty Bottle
*Adventuring gear, common*

A sturdy glass bottle with a tight stopper, absolutely indispensable. Used to carry potions, catch fairies, scoop water, or store curious substances found in the world. Adventurers learn quickly that an empty bottle is rarely truly empty for long.

**Effect:** Holds a single liquid potion, a fairy, milk (2 servings), or similar substance. Certain quests and discoveries require a bottle to carry their reward. You can catch a fairy near a Fairy Fountain or in a fairy meadow with a DC 14 Dexterity check.

**Cost:** 10 gp

---

#### Lantern (Oil Lantern)
*Adventuring gear, common*

A brass-cased oil lamp that illuminates the otherwise impenetrable darkness of Hyrule's dungeons, caves, and the Depths.

**Effect:** Sheds bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light in an additional 15 feet. Burns for 6 hours on a full flask of oil. Can be used to light torches, campfires, and flammable surfaces.

**Cost:** 10 gp (lantern) + 1 gp per flask of oil

---

#### Blue Candle / Red Candle
*Adventuring gear, common / uncommon (Classic)*

Magical candles from Hyrule's earliest adventuring traditions. The Blue Candle can be used once per room; the Red Candle has no such restriction.

**Blue Candle (5 gp):** Once per short rest, you can light a 10-foot cone of magical fire as an action, dealing 1d6 fire damage to creatures in the cone (Dex DC 12 half) and shedding bright light for 1 minute.

**Red Candle (50 gp):** As the Blue Candle, but recharges each round (no usage limit). In addition, it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius at all times while carried unsheathed.

{{footnote Items | Adventuring Gear & Consuma }}

#### Deku Nut
*Adventuring gear, common*

Seed pods from Deku Babas or Deku Scrubs. When thrown or smashed, they release a brilliant flash of light and a concussive shockwave.

**Effect:** As a ranged attack (thrown; range 20/60) or as an action to smash at your feet: all creatures within 10 feet that can see you must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they are **blinded** until the end of their next turn. Undead and creatures without eyes are immune.

**Cost:** 5 gp each, or 10 gp for 5

---

#### Deku Stick
*Adventuring gear, common*

A dry, resinous stick harvested from Deku Babas. Burns brightly and for a surprisingly long time. Used as a torch, or as an improvised weapon in desperate situations.

**Effect:** Functions as a torch (bright light 20 ft., dim light 20 ft.) for 30 minutes when lit. Can be used as an improvised club (1d4 bludgeoning). A lit Deku Stick also deals 1d4 fire damage on a hit, but the fire is extinguished if the stick is submerged.

**Cost:** 1 sp each

---

#### Magnesis Orb (Sheikah Tech Tool)
*Adventuring gear, rare*

A Sheikah-technology device that generates a powerful magnetic field, allowing the user to lift, move, and manipulate metallic objects from a distance. Most commonly encountered as a function of the Sheikah Slate, but portable versions exist.

**Effect:** As an action, target one metallic object within 30 feet that weighs 500 lbs. or less. The object levitates and can be moved up to 30 feet in any direction as part of the same action (or on subsequent turns as a bonus action). You can use this to strike a creature (ranged attack; 2d8 bludgeoning) or set the object down precisely. The orb recharges after 1 minute.

**Cost:** 600 gp (rare Sheikah artifact, usually not for sale)

---

#### Paraglider
*Adventuring gear, uncommon (BotW/TotK)*

A silk-and-wood gliding wing based on designs found across the Sheikah's legacy. Links across the ages have found variants of this tool essential for navigating Hyrule's vast open terrain.

**Effect:** When you fall from a height, you can deploy the paraglider as a reaction. While gliding, you descend at a rate of 10 feet per round (rather than 500 feet) and can move horizontally up to 30 feet per round. You take no falling damage when landing while gliding. The paraglider cannot be used indoors or in enclosed spaces. Gliding in strong winds may require a Strength or Dexterity check at DM discretion.

**Cost:** 150 gp (civilian version). The legendary Paraglider blessed by the Deku Tree or King Rhoam is not available for purchase.

---

#### Pegasus Boots
*Wondrous item, uncommon (ALttP, OoT, ALBW)*

Enchanted boots found in Kakariko Graveyard and other places touched by swift spirits. When activated, they launch the wearer into a sprint of almost supernatural speed.

**Effect:** As a bonus action, activate the Pegasus Boots. Until the end of your turn, your walking speed is tripled and you do not provoke opportunity attacks. If you move in a straight line and strike a creature at the end of this movement, the attack deals +2d6 bludgeoning damage and the target must make a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. Recharges after a short rest.

**Cost:** 500 gp (when available; usually acquired through specific quests)

---

#### Roc's Feather / Roc's Cape
*Wondrous item, uncommon / rare (Oracle games, Minish Cap)*

A magical feather (or its more powerful cape variant) that allows the wearer to leap far higher than natural ability would permit.

**Roc's Feather (200 gp):** Once per turn, you can jump up to 15 feet horizontally or 10 feet vertically as a bonus action, without requiring a running start.

**Roc's Cape (600 gp):** As Roc's Feather, but your jump distances are doubled, and after jumping you can glide horizontally up to 30 feet before descending. You take no falling damage if you land while the cape is active.

---

#### Bunny Hood
*Wondrous item, uncommon (MM, OoT, ALBW)*

A headpiece styled after a woodland rabbit, said to carry the speed of a frightened hare. In Termina, the spirit of a lost runner is said to reside within.

**Effect:** While wearing the Bunny Hood, your base walking speed increases by 10 feet. In addition, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing, and you cannot be surprised while wearing it.

**Cost:** 300 gp

\page

#### Gale Boomerang
*Wondrous item, uncommon (TP)*

An enchanted boomerang inhabited by a captive Fairy of Winds. When thrown, it generates a focused whirlwind that can extinguish fires, spin mechanisms, and scatter lighter enemies.

**Effect:** Functions as an Iron Boomerang (1d6 bludgeoning, returning, 40/80 range). In addition, when thrown, it generates a burst of wind in a 10-foot cone at the point of impact: small fires are extinguished, lightweight objects (less than 5 lbs.) are hurled 10 feet away, and flying creatures of Medium size or smaller must make a DC 13 Strength save or be knocked prone.

**Cost:** Artifact, not for sale; must be found or won

---

#### Spinner
*Wondrous item, rare (TP)*

A top-like Sheikah/ancient relic that, when deployed, expands beneath the user's feet and allows them to race along special rail tracks embedded in certain ancient ruins and dungeons.

**Effect:** When standing on an ancient rail (narrow grooved track found in certain ruins), you can use the Spinner to travel the track at up to 60 feet per round without expending movement, automatically following the track's path. Off-track, the Spinner can be used as a thrown weapon (range 20/60; 2d6 bludgeoning; returning) that pins Medium or smaller creatures in place on a hit (DC 14 Strength save to escape, freeing costs all movement on that turn).

**Cost:** Artifact, found in specific ruins; not for purchase

---

#### Hawkeye Lens
*Wondrous item, uncommon (TP)*

A precision optical scope worn over one eye, crafted by Rito artisans for long-distance spotting. When combined with a bow, it effectively transforms any ranged shot into a sniper's tool.

**Effect:** While wearing the Hawkeye, you can use an action to take careful aim at a creature you can see within your bow's long range. Your next ranged attack made this turn ignores the disadvantage imposed by long range and cover (unless the target is fully behind total cover). In addition, you can see clearly up to 1 mile in good conditions.

**Cost:** 150 gp

---

#### Lens of Truth
*Wondrous item, rare (OoT, MM)*

A monocular device of Sheikah origin that allows the user to perceive what is hidden: invisible creatures, illusory walls, false floors, and disguised enemies all become visible.

**Effect:** As an action, you peer through the Lens. Until the start of your next turn, you can see invisible creatures and objects, see through illusions (as if you had succeeded on a saving throw), and detect secret doors within 30 feet that are within your line of sight. The Lens functions continuously if held to the eye, but requires concentration. Continuous use beyond 1 minute per short rest begins to give you a headache from overstimulation.

**Cost:** Sheikah artifact; not for sale

---

*Wondrous item, uncommon (BotW)*

A Sheikah Slate attachment or standalone device that pulses faintly when certain designated objects (Shrines of Trials, Korok Seeds, specific materials) are nearby.

While attuned, the Sensor pulses audibly when the target type is within 60 feet, and pulses faster as you grow closer (within 20 feet). It does not give direction, only proximity.

\page

# Relics & Sacred Artifacts

> *"These are not merely weapons or tools. They are pieces of the world's soul, fragments of divine intent, sealed power, and the endless struggle between light and shadow that has defined Hyrule since its first dawn."*
> ##### — Impa of the Sheikah

Relics are items of extraordinary power, deep history, or sacred origin. They are not bought in shops or pried from monster loot. They are found at the heart of ancient dungeons, earned through trials set by the goddesses themselves, passed down through royal bloodlines, or drawn from the ruins of civilizations that no living person can name.

Relics marked with ✦ are **quest items**. They cannot be sold, traded, or permanently lost by their rightful bearer. If separated from the bearer, they will find their way back within 1d7 days unless sealed by powerful divine magic.

---

## The Relic Tiers

**Relics in this book are deliberately strong.** A Zelda story is a story about finding a thing that changes what you are capable of, and a small conditional bonus will not carry that weight. The balancing lever here is **when the relic arrives**, and that lever belongs to the DM.

What this chapter gives you is a ladder, so that you know what you are handing over.

{{classTable,frame,wide
##### Relic Tiers
| Tier | Name | What it does to a campaign | Attunement | Examples |
|:--:|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **0** | **The Triforce** | Ends one campaign and begins another. Nothing in this book is stronger, and nothing should be. | Special (see below) | The Triforce and its three pieces |
| **1** | **Divine Artifact** | Defines the rest of the campaign. The party will be known for carrying it. | Required | Master Sword, Fused Shadows, Mirror of Twilight, Ocarina of Time |
| **2** | **Sacred Relic** | Defines an arc. Usually the reward at the end of a dungeon chain. | Required | Sage Medallions, the Four Elements, Sacred Flames, Pendants of Virtue |
| **3** | **Wondrous Relic** | Changes how one character plays. A memorable single-dungeon reward. | Usually required | Spiritual Stones, Essences, Goddess Harp, Bombos Medallion |
| **4** | **Lesser Relic** | Solves a problem, opens a route, or gives a character one new verb. | Rarely required | Lens of Truth, Pegasus Boots, Roc's Feather, Magic Cape |
}}

**Most of a campaign happens at Tier 4 and Tier 3.** A party that finds a Lens of Truth in their third session and a Roc's Feather in their fifth has exactly the Zelda experience: a growing bag of verbs, each of which reshapes what a dungeon can ask of them. Tier 2 relics arrive at the end of arcs. Tier 1 relics arrive once or twice in a campaign. Tier 0 arrives at the end, or never.

{{footnote Relics | Using Relics }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Rules That Apply to Every Relic

> ##### New Rule: The Relic Save DC
> Where a relic forces a saving throw and does not name a DC, that DC is:
>
> **8 + your proficiency bonus + your highest ability modifier**
>
> This is your **Relic save DC**. It is the same for every relic you carry, it does not depend on your class, and it scales with you, so a relic found at 5th level is still worth using at 15th.

> ##### New Rule: Once Per Turn
> **A relic that adds damage to your attacks adds it once per turn**, on the first attack that qualifies, unless the relic says otherwise.
>
> This is the single most important balance rule in the chapter. Extra Attack, multiattack effects and bonus-action strikes would otherwise multiply every relic in this chapter by two or three, and the character contributing that damage would not need any class features at all.

**Attunement.** Every relic states whether it requires attunement, and the standard limit of three attuned items applies. It is a real constraint: a character carrying the Master Sword, a Sage Medallion and an Element has no slot left, and that is the intended cost of carrying three legends at once. Forming the bond takes a short rest unless the entry says otherwise, and several of the greatest relics do.

**The Triforce is the exception.** Its pieces are not items you attune to so much as marks you bear, and they do not count against your limit.

\column

## Handing Out Relics

Four questions, and the fourth is the one that matters.

**1. What does it let them do that they could not do before?** A relic that adds a number is forgettable. A relic that adds a *verb* (jump, dig, see the invisible, walk on water, flip an object over) reshapes every room the party enters afterward. Prefer verbs.

**2. What did it cost to get?** A relic handed over is a gift. A relic taken out of a dungeon is a trophy. The second is worth four times the first, and the difference costs you nothing but one session of build-up.

**3. Who else wants it?** The best relics in Hyrule's history are all contested. Someone should want this back.

**4. What does the world look like once they have it?** If the answer is "the same, but the fighter hits harder," reconsider. If the answer is "now they can reach the sunken city," you have picked the right relic.

{{footnote Relics | Using Relics }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## The Triforce
*Tier 0*

*Wondrous item, artifact (attunement is automatic and does not count against your limit of three)*

The three golden triangles left behind when the Golden Goddesses, Din, Nayru, and Farore, departed the world at the moment of its creation. Together they form the Triforce: a wish-granting relic of absolute power, and the axis around which the fate of Hyrule has turned since the beginning of time.

> ##### The Ceiling
> **Nothing in this book is stronger than the Triforce, and nothing should be.** Every other relic in this chapter was written to sit beneath it. If you invent a relic for your own campaign, measure it against this page and keep it lower.

**The test is balance, not virtue.** The Triforce grants the wish of whoever touches it, and it does not judge their reasons. If the heart of the one who grasps it holds Power, Wisdom and Courage in balance, they receive the whole. If it does not, the Triforce splits, and the toucher keeps only the piece representing the force they most believe in. The other two pass to two people in the world chosen by destiny, who from that moment bear the mark on the backs of their hands.

A perfectly good person who lacks wisdom will split the Triforce exactly as surely as a tyrant will. That is the point of it.

**Resonance.** Pieces of the Triforce in close proximity strain toward one another. A bearer always knows the direction to the nearest other piece, and the distance to within a mile. So does every other bearer. This is how the heroes find each other, and it is how the villain finds them.

### The Triforce of Power
*Tier 0. The golden triangle left by Din.*

It burns with an inner heat visible through the back of the hand it marks. Ganondorf has held it across most of recorded history, but it is not inherently evil. Power is a force. How it is wielded determines its nature.

**Passive Effect.** Your Strength and Constitution scores each increase by 3, to a maximum of 26. You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

**Unkillable.** Damage cannot reduce you below 1 hit point. You can still be brought to 0 by a **killing blow**, which means any of the following, and nothing else:

- A **critical hit from a legendary creature**, or from any creature wielding an artifact or a Tier 1 relic.
- Damage from an **artifact**, from the **Master Sword**, or from a **god, demon king, or comparable power** acting directly.
- A single instance of damage equal to **half your hit point maximum or more**.
- An effect that reduces your hit point maximum to 0, or that kills outright without dealing damage.


**Regeneration.** You regain 10 hit points at the start of each of your turns. This does not function on any turn during which you have taken **radiant damage** since the end of your last turn, or at any point while a drawn Master Sword is within 30 feet of you.

**Death's Door.** If a killing blow does bring you to 0 hit points, you automatically succeed on your first death saving throw each round, and you stabilize after two successes rather than three.

**Requirement.** The Triforce of Power seeks those with strength of conviction, for good or ill. If a creature attuned to it ever willingly surrenders without need, it may slip away.

---

### The Triforce of Wisdom
*Tier 0. The golden triangle left by Nayru.*

It gleams with a soft blue-white light and seems to clarify the thoughts of those nearby. It has most often chosen Zelda, princess of Hyrule, of a lineage of seers and prophets whose wisdom guards the kingdom even when its armies cannot.

**Passive Effect.** Your Intelligence and Wisdom scores each increase by 3, to a maximum of 26. You can never be surprised. You have advantage on all saving throws against spells and magical effects.

**The Clear Mind.** You can cast *detect thoughts* at will, without expending magic points or components, and *foresight* once per long rest.

**Healing Hand.** As an action, you can touch a creature and restore 6d8 hit points, or end one disease or one condition afflicting it. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

**Death's Door.** When you drop to 0 hit points, you automatically succeed on your first death saving throw each round, and you stabilize after two successes rather than three.

**Requirement.** The Triforce of Wisdom is drawn to those who seek truth over advantage. It will not remain with one who uses *detect thoughts* to manipulate or exploit.

{{footnote Relics | The Triforce }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### The Triforce of Courage
*Tier 0. The golden triangle left by Farore.*

It pulses faintly gold on the back of the left hand, warm to the touch. It has most often chosen Link: an ordinary person reborn across the ages to face extraordinary evil, not because he is born to power or blessed with genius, but because he does not turn away.

**Passive Effect.** Your Dexterity and Charisma scores each increase by 3, to a maximum of 26. You are immune to the frightened condition.

**Ward Against Magic.** You have advantage on saving throws against any effect that would compel you to flee, surrender, or abandon an ally, and resistance to damage from spells.

**The Last Step.** Once per long rest, when you would take damage that would reduce you to 0 hit points, you can reduce that damage to 0.

**Death's Door.** When you drop to 0 hit points, you automatically succeed on your first death saving throw each round, and you stabilize after two successes rather than three.

**Requirement.** The Triforce of Courage stays with those who act despite fear, not those who feel none. It will not stay with one who avoids all risk, or who harms the innocent without cause.

---

### The Complete Triforce
*Tier 0.*

A single being holding all three pieces gains every effect above at once, and one more.

**Divine Audience.** Once, while holding the complete Triforce, you may cast *wish*. Unlike a normal casting, this version does not damage or weaken the caster, and it is not bound by *wish*'s usual list of safe uses. It is the pure expression of divine will made manifest, and it will do exactly what you ask, in exactly the way you asked for it.

**After the Wish.** The instant the wish is granted, the Triforce shatters. Each piece vanishes and reappears somewhere in the world, in the possession of or near the three individuals who best embody Power, Wisdom and Courage at that moment. Where they land is at the DM's discretion, and they may land with heroes, with villains, or somewhere nobody can reach for a hundred years.

This is the cycle. It has happened before. It will happen again.

\column

> ##### Running the Triforce
> Treat the Triforce as a **campaign ending** rather than a balance problem. Everything below assumes you are running the last act.
>
> **Give a piece, not the whole.** A single piece is a Tier 0 relic and still the strongest thing at the table by a wide margin. A campaign in which one player holds Courage, an ally holds Wisdom, and the villain holds Power is the entire premise of most Zelda games, and it works because none of the three can simply win.
>
> **The other two pieces are plot, not treasure.** They are held by "others chosen by destiny." Decide who those people are before you split it. One of them should be someone the party cares about.
>
> **The mark is visible.** Anyone who knows what it means can see who holds a piece. This is a target on the back of a hand.
>
> **The wish is the end.** When someone completes the Triforce and wishes, the campaign is over, in the sense that whatever happens next is a different campaign. Plan the session accordingly, and let the player say the wish out loud in their own words.

{{footnote Relics | The Triforce }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## The Master Sword
### *The Blade of Evil's Bane*
*Tier 1*

*Weapon (broadsword), artifact (requires attunement by a creature the sword recognizes)*

*"The Master Sword is a sacred blade that evil can never touch."*

The Master Sword is not merely a weapon. It began as the **Goddess Sword**, forged by the goddess Hylia against the rising power of Demise, and was made into the Master Sword by her chosen hero, who bathed it in the three Sacred Flames. Zelda's blessing completed it. Sleeping within it is **Fi**, the spirit the goddess placed there.

**Base statistics.** The Master Sword is a broadsword dealing 1d8 slashing damage, with the **versatile (1d10)** and **fine** properties. Everything below is in addition to that.

> ##### On the sword's origins
> The histories do not agree, and this book does not pretend otherwise. The oldest Hylian record says the people of Hyrule forged the blade after Ganon claimed the Triforce. Another says the gods ordered it made long before, precisely so that something would exist to oppose whoever seized the Triforce. A third credits the ancient Sages. The oldest account of all says Hylia made it herself.
>
> Pick one for your Hyrule. They cannot all be true, and the sword does not care.

**Sentience.** The Master Sword is a sentient weapon of neutral good alignment, with Intelligence 14, Wisdom 18 and Charisma 16, hearing and truesight out to 120 feet. It communicates through impressions, feelings and visions rather than words. Its bearer always knows its emotional state and its intent. **Fi** may manifest as a translucent blue figure to speak more directly, at the DM's discretion.

**The Chosen Bearer.** The sword chooses. One it does not recognize who grasps the hilt takes 4d8 radiant damage and cannot attune to it. It recognizes anyone marked by the Triforce of Courage automatically; anyone else must have proven themselves through equivalent divine trial. Attunement takes a full day rather than a short rest.

**Evil's Bane.** **Once per turn**, when you hit a creature that is undead, a fiend, a creature of pure shadow, or a creature under Ganon's influence, the Master Sword deals an additional **2d6 radiant damage** and ignores that creature's resistance to radiant damage. Against Ganon himself, this increases to 4d6 and also ignores immunity.

\column

**Sword Beam.** While you are at full hit points, you can use a bonus action to fire a beam of light: a ranged spell attack at a target within 60 feet, using **your proficiency bonus plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier**, whichever you use to attack with the sword. On a hit it deals 2d8 radiant damage. Against a creature vulnerable to radiant damage, the beam scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

**Barrier Breaker.** Your attacks with the Master Sword ignore, and destroy on a hit, any magical barrier, ward, seal or *forcecage* of 6th level or lower. Against higher-level barriers, one hit suppresses the barrier until the end of your next turn.

**Curse Breaker.** As an action, you can touch a creature or object with the Master Sword to end one curse, one polymorph effect, or one magical transformation affecting it, as though you had cast *remove curse* or *dispel magic* at 9th level.

**Indestructible.** The Master Sword cannot be broken, destroyed, or permanently disenchanted. Any effect that would destroy it instead returns it to its pedestal, where it rests until its bearer or the next chosen hero comes for it.

**Return to the Pedestal.** If the bearer is slain, or willingly returns it, the sword flies to its pedestal. The bearer always knows the direction and approximate distance to it, wherever in the world it rests.

**Sealing Power.** Once per long rest, as an action, you can touch one creature of CR 10 or lower and attempt to seal it inside a vessel of your choosing: a statue, a sword, a standing stone. The target makes a Charisma saving throw against your **Relic save DC**. On a failure it is sealed for 100 years, or until the vessel is destroyed or the seal is deliberately broken. On a success it is stunned until the end of its next turn.

A sealed creature may attempt to break out once per year, repeating the save. With additional divine sanction, and at the DM's discretion, this power can be turned on far greater beings; that is how Ganon was sealed the first time.

}}

{{footnote Relics | The Master Sword }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

### Drawing the Master Sword

Two legends survive about where the sword sleeps and what unlocks it. Both are told as fact in different parts of Hyrule, and both appear in the oldest records. **Choose one for your campaign before the party goes looking**, because they gate the sword in completely different places.

{{classTable,frame,wide
##### The Two Legends
| | **The Lost Woods** | **The Temple of Time** |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Where it sleeps** | On the Pedestal of Time, in a clearing deep in the Lost Woods that will not stay in one place | On the Pedestal of Time, in the inner sanctum behind the Door of Time |
| **The key** | The three **Pendants of Virtue**, from the Forest, the Desert and the Tower | The three **Spiritual Stones**, plus the Ocarina of Time and the Song of Time, played at the altar |
| **The journey** | Three dungeons, then a maze that tests whether you should be there at all | Three peoples, each of whom must be persuaded to part with a treasure, then one ritual |
| **What it feels like** | A pilgrimage. Nobody is watching. The forest decides. | A diplomatic campaign. The whole kingdom knows what you are doing. |
| **Best for** | A party of outsiders and wanderers | A party tied to Hyrule's politics and peoples |
}}

**Whichever you choose, the other set of keys still exists and still matters.** If the Pendants gate the sword, the Spiritual Stones instead open the Door of Time onto the Sacred Realm itself, which is a different and more dangerous prize. If the Spiritual Stones gate the sword, the Pendants are three Tier 2 relics granting the blessings of the three goddesses, and a bearer holding all three is recognized by the sword without further trial.

**The pedestal is a lock in both directions.** Returning the sword to its pedestal is how a bearer walks away, and in the Temple of Time it is more than that: the pedestal is a port on the river of time. A bearer who sheathes the blade there and draws it again may find that years have passed, or that they have not yet happened.

\column

> ##### If the Bearer Is Not Ready
> The sword does not simply refuse. A bearer the sword judges too young, too weak, or not yet who they will become is **sealed within the blade** until they are ready. In the oldest account this took seven years, and the world got worse the entire time.
>
> This is a legitimate campaign turn and not a punishment. Used well, it is the mid-campaign time skip that changes the map, ages the NPCs, and lets the villain finally win something.

> ##### The Sword Can Be Weakened
> The Master Sword's power to repel evil was **given**, not born in it, and what is given can be taken away.
>
> In one age its power was sustained by two Sages praying in distant temples. Kill the Sages and the blade dims: while its power is broken, the Master Sword loses **Evil's Bane**, **Barrier Breaker**, **Sword Beam** and **Curse Breaker**, retaining only its base statistics and its indestructibility.
>
> This is the best villain move available to a DM whose party has become too comfortable, and it is entirely canonical. Restoring the blade should be its own arc.

**Those with evil hearts cannot touch it.** This is not a saving throw. A creature the sword refuses simply cannot pick it up, and the party's most morally compromised member may discover this in front of everyone.

{{footnote Relics | The Master Sword }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## The Goddess Sword and Sacred Flames
*(Skyward Sword). Tier 2.*

Before the Master Sword existed there was the **Goddess Sword**, the prototype blade carried by the chosen hero in the era before Hyrule was founded. Bathing it in the **three Sacred Flames** remakes it by stages into the Master Sword.

These relics belong in a campaign set in Hyrule's ancient past, before the Master Sword has been forged. Each Flame is a Tier 2 relic in its own right and grants its bearer a blessing whether or not there is a sword to temper.

*Each Sacred Flame requires attunement.*

### Farore's Flame ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

A pure green flame held in the Ancient Cistern beneath Lake Floria, tended by the Water Dragon Faron. It embodies Farore's virtue: life, courage, the willingness to act.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on death saving throws and cannot be paralyzed by magical effects.

**Tempering (on the Goddess Sword).** The blade lengthens and sharpens, becoming the **Goddess Long Sword**: +1 to attack and damage rolls. In addition, once per turn, you may declare a **lunge** before making a melee attack with it, extending your reach by 5 feet for that attack.

---

### Nayru's Flame ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

A soft blue flame preserved aboard the Sandship, protected by the mechanical crew LD-301 Skipper commanded. It embodies Nayru's virtue: law, wisdom, the clarity to see truth.

**Passive Effect.** You automatically succeed on saving throws against illusion spells and have advantage on Insight checks.

**Tempering (on the Goddess Sword).** The blade turns white with inner light, becoming the **Goddess White Sword**: +2 to attack and damage rolls, and the bearer can dowse, as a Sheikah Sensor attuned to any one target type of their choosing, changeable after each long rest.


### Din's Flame ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

A roaring red-orange flame sealed in the Fire Sanctuary atop Eldin Volcano, the most dangerous of the three to reach. It embodies Din's virtue: power, will, the force to shape the world.

**Passive Effect.** **Once per turn**, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you deal an additional 1d6 fire damage. You automatically succeed on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by heat.

**Tempering (on the Goddess Sword).** Din's Flame completes the transformation. The Goddess White Sword becomes the **True Master Sword**, its primordial form, awaiting only Zelda's blessing. It gains every Master Sword statistic except **Evil's Bane** and **Sealing Power**, which awaken only after that blessing or an equivalent divine rite.

---

## Pendants of Virtue
*(A Link to the Past). Tier 2.*

Three sacred pendants recovered from the Great Hyrule Forest, the Desert Palace and the Tower of Hera in the Golden Age before Agahnim's betrayal. In the Lost Woods legend they are the key to the Master Sword: the password by which the blade identifies a worthy bearer.

Each pendant can be worn as a necklace or carried, and glows faintly in its own color. *Each requires attunement.*

### Pendant of Courage ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

The green pendant from the Great Hyrule Forest, associated with Farore. Its surface is carved with tiny leaf-veins.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on saving throws against the frightened condition, and woodland creatures treat you as a trusted ally by default.

---

### Pendant of Power ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

The red pendant from the Desert Palace, associated with Din. It is warm to the touch and occasionally pulses.

**Passive Effect.** **Once per turn**, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you deal an additional 2 damage of the weapon's type. You have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks.

---

### Pendant of Wisdom ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement)*

The blue pendant from the Tower of Hera, associated with Nayru. It is the heaviest of the three despite its small size.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on saving throws against spells, and you can cast *comprehend languages* at will without expending magic points.

---

**The Three Together.** A bearer holding all three Pendants may draw the Master Sword from the Lost Woods pedestal if the sword recognizes them. In a campaign using the Temple of Time legend instead, the three Pendants together grant the recognition without the journey: the sword accepts a bearer who wears all three, though they must still reach the pedestal.

## Sage Medallions
*(Ocarina of Time). Tier 2.*

When a Sage awakens to their calling, they forge a medallion and send it to the chosen hero as a symbol of their bond and a conduit of their power. There are six, one from each of the Sages who sealed Ganon in the Ocarina era. They cannot be purchased. They are gifts, and they pass from Sage to hero across the ages.

*Each medallion requires attunement.*

> ##### Medallions Are Not Affinities
> The six Sage Medallions and the six **Elemental Affinities** of the Sage class are different things, and the lists deliberately do not match.
>
> The **medallions** are historical relics named for the six Sages who actually held those offices in one particular era: Forest, Fire, Water, Shadow, Spirit and Light. They are people's legacies.
>
> The **affinities** are the six elemental disciplines a living Sage studies: Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Spirit and Light. They are a curriculum.
>
> So there is a Forest Medallion with no matching affinity, and a Wind affinity with no matching medallion, and that is correct. A Sage of the Wind may carry the Forest Medallion; it only means Saria chose them.
>
> | Medallion | Nearest affinity | |
> |:--|:--|:--|
> | Forest | Earth or Wind | *no exact match* |
> | Fire | Fire | |
> | Water | Water | |
> | Shadow | Spirit | *no exact match* |
> | Spirit | Spirit | |
> | Light | Light | |
>
> If you would rather they line up in your Hyrule, swap Forest for Earth and Shadow for Wind and nothing else in the book breaks.

\column

### Forest Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Saria, Sage of the Forest.*

A green disc threaded with the living wood of the Sacred Meadow.

**Passive Effect.** You can cast *speak with plants* at will without expending magic points. Difficult terrain made of plant growth does not slow you. Plant creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

---

### Fire Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Darunia, Sage of Fire.*

A red disc that is warm to the touch. The Goron sage's fierce courage is bound within it.

**Passive Effect.** You automatically succeed on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by heat. **Once per combat**, the first time you deal fire damage, that damage is maximized. You have advantage on Strength checks and **Strength** saving throws.

---

### Water Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Princess Ruto, Sage of Water.*

A blue disc that is always cool and slightly wet, as if just pulled from a deep lake.

**Passive Effect.** You can breathe water and have a swim speed of 30 feet. Currents, floods and pressure do not affect you. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws.

---

{{footnote Relics | Sage Medallions }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

### Shadow Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Impa, Sage of Shadow.*

A dark purple disc that seems to drink the light near it. It is never warm.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. You can cast *darkness* at will, centered on yourself only, without expending magic points, and you see normally through your own darkness. Undead have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

---

### Spirit Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Nabooru, Sage of Spirit.*

A golden disc that smells faintly of desert spice. It carries the proud will of the Gerudo sage.

**Passive Effect.** You are immune to being charmed or magically compelled. You can cast *mirror image* once per long rest without expending magic points. In desert terrain you cannot become lost or disoriented.

---

### Light Medallion ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Gift of Rauru, Sage of Light.*

A warm gold disc that hums at a pitch only its bearer can hear. The first medallion, from the Sage who built the Temple of Time.

**Passive Effect.** You shed dim light in a 5-foot radius that nonmagical darkness cannot suppress. Undead and shadow creatures within 30 feet have disadvantage on attack rolls. You can cast *daylight* once per long rest without expending magic points.

---

**All Six Medallions.** A bearer holding all six can open a gateway to the Sacred Realm once per year, on the anniversary of the day they were united. It leads to the Chamber of the Sages, where the Sages themselves may be consulted in person.

## The Four Elements
*(The Minish Cap). Tier 2.*

Crystalline vessels of primal elemental energy, each recovered from one of the four great dungeons of Minish-era Hyrule. The Four Elements were used to reforge the shattered Picori Blade into the **Four Sword**. Even without a blade to infuse, each Element radiates its power to whoever carries it.

*Each Element requires attunement.*

> ##### A Different Sword
> The Four Elements belong to the **Picori Blade → White Sword → Four Sword** lineage, not to the Master Sword. The two blades look alike and are constantly confused for one another, including by scholars who should know better. They are not the same weapon and the Elements will not temper the Master Sword.

### Earth Element ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Deepwood Shrine, Minish Woods.*

A clear green crystal that smells of clean soil and rain. The first of the four, and the most fundamental: the stable ground that makes all other growth possible.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would move you against your will. Your hit point maximum increases by 10. When you finish a short rest on natural ground, you regain one additional Hit Die.

---

### Fire Element ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Cave of Flames, Mount Crenel.*

A deep crimson crystal, warm to the touch, glowing faintly in darkness. Fire brings light into darkness and the strength to press forward when the path is unclear.

**Passive Effect.** **Once per turn**, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you deal an additional 1d6 fire damage. You do not suffer disadvantage on attack rolls caused by magical or nonmagical darkness. Once per short rest you can cast *burning hands* without expending magic points, using your **Relic save DC**.

\column

### Water Element ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Temple of Droplets, Lake Hylia.*

A pale blue crystal, always cool, catching light from no obvious source. Water flows around obstacles and purifies what it touches.

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws. When you finish a short rest you may remove one of the following from yourself: the poisoned condition, the blinded condition, one level of standard exhaustion, or one level of Weather Exhaustion. Once per long rest you can cast *create or destroy water* or *water walk* without expending magic points.

---

### Wind Element ✦
*Sacred relic, Tier 2 (requires attunement). Palace of Winds, Cloud Tops.*

A translucent white-silver crystal that drifts upward slightly in still air. Wind carries seeds to new lands. It is the force of possibility, of travel, of beginning again.

**Passive Effect.** Your jump distances are doubled and you take no damage from falls of 30 feet or less. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. Once per short rest, as a bonus action, you can cast *gust of wind* or *feather fall* without expending magic points. You always know the wind's direction and can sense approaching weather up to 24 hours ahead.

---

**All Four Together.** A bearer holding all Four Elements can have a sword infused with all four powers at once. This requires a Minish smith or equal craftsperson and an 8-hour ritual. The resulting weapon deals an additional **1d6 damage once per turn** of a type you choose from fire, cold, lightning or thunder, and you may change the chosen type as a bonus action.

In the age it was made for, each Element also granted the wielder one **duplicate of themselves**, and a blade holding all four could field three. That power sleeps in the modern era. A DM who wants it awake should treat it as a Tier 1 effect and price the quest accordingly.

## Essences of Nature
*(Oracle of Seasons). Tier 3.*

The eight Essences of Nature are the primal forces that give Holodrum its seasons, its growth and its vitality. When Onox disrupted the seasons by capturing Din, the Essences scattered, the Maku Tree withered, and the land fell into shifting chaos. Each was hidden in a dungeon and guarded.

Each Essence is a jewel-like object about the size of a Deku Nut, pulsing with quiet organic light, warm or cool according to its nature. A character holding one always feels a faint connection to the living world.

*Essences do not require attunement. A character may carry any number.*

### Fertile Soil ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Seeds scattered across bountiful lands are nourished in this Fertile Soil!"*

**Passive Effect.** Once per day you can make up to 30 square feet of natural ground lush and fertile; by the next morning it sprouts enough edible vegetation to feed six people. Crops planted near you grow in days rather than months. Plant-based difficult terrain does not slow you.

---

### Gift of Time ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Seeds sprout as seasons change with the Gift of Time!"*

**Passive Effect.** While you are below half your hit point maximum, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) at the start of each of your turns. This healing stops for 1 minute if you take necrotic damage or damage from an artifact. You need only half the usual sleep and suffer no ill effects from an irregular schedule.

---

### Bright Sun ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Young shoots grow quickly under the warm rays of the Bright Sun!"*

**Passive Effect.** You radiate warmth in a 10-foot radius; you and allies within it have advantage on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by cold. You have advantage on saving throws against magical darkness and blindness. **Once per turn**, while in direct sunlight, you may add +2 to one Athletics, Acrobatics or Sleight of Hand check.


### Soothing Rain ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"A single drop of the Soothing Rain can make flowers bloom!"*

**Passive Effect.** Once per short rest you can touch a willing creature to remove the poisoned condition or reduce its exhaustion by one level. You have advantage on Wisdom (Medicine) checks, and any creature you stabilize heals 1d4 hit points at the end of your turn.

---

### Nurturing Warmth ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Balmy days build strong saplings with their Nurturing Warmth!"*

**Passive Effect.** You and allies within 10 feet have **advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration**. When you or an ally within 10 feet spends Hit Dice during a short rest, they may reroll any 1s and take the second result. You have advantage on Weather Exhaustion checks caused by cold.

---

### Blowing Wind ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Sweet fruit is born when pollen is carried by the Blowing Wind!"*

**Passive Effect.** Once per day you can send a spoken message of up to 25 words to any creature you have met, as *sending*, at any distance; the message travels on the wind. You have advantage on Perception checks relying on hearing, and you cannot be surprised by flying creatures.

---

### Seed of Life ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Life begins anew when birds carry this, the Seed of Life, to new lands!"*

**Passive Effect.** Once per long rest, when you drop to 0 hit points, you **immediately and automatically** regain hit points equal to half your hit point maximum. This requires no action and works even after death saving throw failures, provided it triggers before your third. You have advantage on death saving throws while this Essence is on your person.

---

### Changing Seasons ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Scattered seeds sprout in spring, grow in summer, bear fruit in fall and sleep through winter. It is an endless cycle of life... the Changing Seasons!"*

**Passive Effect.** You sense the season within a mile. Once per long rest, as an action, you can shift the local season one step: spring → summer → fall → winter → spring. The change lasts 24 hours or until you leave. While a season you have set is active, you have advantage on one skill of the DM's choosing suited to that season.

---

**All Eight Essences of Nature.** You are in harmony with the living world. Once per day you can cast *control weather* without components or magic points, and plants and animals will never willingly harm you.

{{footnote Relics | Essences of Nature }}

{{pageNumber,auto}}

\page

## Essences of Time
*(Oracle of Ages). Tier 3.*

The eight Essences of Time are the forces that give history its meaning: memory, identity, passion, truth, and the pull of destiny. When Veran possessed Nayru and began rewriting the past, they scattered across Labrynna's dungeons. Each carries a fragment of a truth about time that those who find them come to understand wordlessly.

*Essences do not require attunement. A character may carry any number.*

### Eternal Spirit ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"Even after life ends, it speaks across time to the heart."*

**Passive Effect.** Once per long rest you can cast *speak with dead* without components or magic points. In addition, **once per year**, if you are slain by an undead creature, you return to life 24 hours later with 1 hit point, provided the Essence is still on your person.

---

### Ancient Wood ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"It whispers only truth to closed ears from out of the stillness."*

**Passive Effect.** You automatically know when a creature of CR 5 or lower is lying to you. You have advantage on Insight checks against any creature. Once per long rest you can cast *zone of truth* without components, using your **Relic save DC**.

---

### Echoing Howl ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"It echoes far across the plains to speak to insolent hearts."*

**Passive Effect.** Once per short rest you may speak a command of one word or a short phrase; each creature of CR 3 or lower within 60 feet that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your **Relic save DC** or be affected as by *command*. You have advantage on Intimidation and Persuasion checks.

---

### Burning Flame ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"It reignites wavering hearts with a hero's burning passion."*

**Passive Effect.** You are immune to the frightened condition. Once per short rest, when an ally within 30 feet fails a saving throw, you may use your reaction to let them reroll it. Your critical hit range expands by 1 (you score a critical hit on a 19 or 20).

\column

### Sacred Soil ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"All that lies sleeping in the bosom of the earth will know the nourishing warmth of the Sacred Soil."*

**Passive Effect.** You have tremorsense out to 60 feet and sense tunnels, buried objects and hidden chambers within it. Once per long rest you can cast *meld into stone* without components. You always know your exact depth underground and cannot become lost in caves.

---

### Lonely Peak ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"It is a proud, lonely spirit that remains stalwart, even in trying times."*

**Passive Effect.** You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, frightened, or having your will overridden. While you are the last conscious member of your party, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls, saving throws and AC. In addition, creatures do not gain advantage on attack rolls against you from **Pack Tactics**, flanking, or any similar effect that rewards outnumbering you.

---

### Rolling Sea ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"The mystical song of the sea roars into a crashing wave that sweeps heroes out into adventure."*

**Passive Effect.** You have a swim speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater. You have advantage on Charisma checks made to persuade someone to join a journey or take a risk. Once per long rest, as an action, you release a crashing wave in a 30-foot cone: 4d8 bludgeoning damage, and a creature is pushed 15 feet away, on a failed Strength saving throw against your **Relic save DC**, or half damage and no push on a success.

---

### Falling Star ✦
*Wondrous relic, Tier 3*

*"The eternal light of this heavenly body acts as guide to the other essences."*

**Passive Effect.** You always know the direction and approximate distance to every other Essence of Time or Nature in the world. You cannot become lost by any means. Once per long rest you can cast *guiding bolt* without expending magic points, dealing 8d6 radiant damage instead of 4d6. Outdoors, you always know the exact time of night, the season, and your cardinal direction.

---

**All Eight Essences of Time.** Once per year you can cast *time stop* without components or magic points, and you do not age while it is active. You also sense temporal disturbance: you feel unease on entering any location whose timeline has been altered.

{{footnote Relics | Essences of Time }}
